### 1. The combo table calls engines "win conditions" and drowns the signal (L)

**Where:** `/results/[file]`, section "Win conditions". The table is at `web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:438-633`, the h2 at `:451`, and the "AI can fire this; results meaningful" chip at `:568`. Data comes from `engine/analysis.py`, and `engine/combos.py:90-101` (`_slim()`) drops Spellbook's variant family (`of`) and template pieces (`requires`).

**What the player sees:** on the Kess run, 37 to 41 rows.
- Squirrel Girl has 28 near-duplicates that all carry "draw odds predicted ~0.2; too few games to measure this" (33 identical chips).
- Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring gets "Assembled 1 of 8, Converted 1, AI can fire this". Spellbook's own results for that line are "Infinite colorless mana, infinite storm count", and Kess won that game in combat.
- Stella Lee alone counts as a combo "assembled 8 of 8", although the loop never ran (137 idle online turns).
- At 1440px the table is 1692px wide inside a 1196px scroller, so the "Reading" column starts off-screen and no scroll hint is shown.

**Why it matters:** substance before style. An expert trusts every other number less after reading this. It also breaks the product's own honesty contract: "Converted" means "that seat later won", yet it is rendered as a causal claim. And it contradicts the source it cites, because Commander Spellbook folds variants and separates cards, prerequisites, steps and results.

**Fix:** rebuild it as per-deck combo lines. §5.3 has the full spec. Group variants by Spellbook family. Classify each family by what it produces: finisher, combat finisher, engine that needs a payoff, or commander loop. Replace "Converted" with "won that game" and "won with it". Show Spellbook's structure on expand and link out. Fold lines that never came together. **Stopgap this week:**
- Rename the section "Combo lines (from Commander Spellbook)".
- Render `produces` as visible chips; today it only appears in a `title` tooltip.
- Delete the "AI can fire this" chip.
- Let the combo cell wrap.
- Fold rows with 0 assemblies and expected < 1 behind "N more lines never came together".

### 2. The replay misstates the game at its decisive moment (S)

**Where:** `web/lib/replay.ts:245` is `raw.match(/^(.+?)'s (.+)$/)`, a lazy match. Related spots:
- `:261` `isCombatPhase`
- `:569-583` `labelOrd` falls back to end-of-turn
- `:468-471` poison accumulates but never eliminates
- `replay/[game]/page.tsx:341` sets `decidingIdx` to the start of the last turn

**What the player sees:** "Skrat's Revenge's Declare Blockers Step" parses as player "Skrat" and phase "Revenge's declare blockers". So the header reads "Round 9 · revenge's declare attackers", the attack markers vanish at declare blockers ("Goblin Token blocks Phyrexian Beast Token" with no attack drawn), and shim reads jump to end-of-turn state, putting a Main-2 Squirrel token on the table during declare attackers.

Krenko (46 poison) and Stella (19 poison) stay seated at full opacity for 95 more events. "Jump to the deciding turn" lands on round 10's untap step, 30 to 74 events after Triumph of the Hordes and the infect alpha strike that actually decided the game.

**Why it matters:** possessive deck names are the Commander norm ("Edgar's Vampires", "Yuriko's Ninjas"), so this hits most imported decks. It makes a shim board, which the page labels exact, show the wrong state. It also re-creates the "blocker with no attack" class of bug that CLAUDE.md records as fixed.

**Fix:**
1. Parse phase lines against the known player keys, longest first (`raw.startsWith(stripAi(key) + "'s ")` or `+ "' "`). Check `engine/forge_log_adapter.py` for the same pattern. Add a fixture with "Skrat's Revenge", then re-run `board.py` on a shim result and a stdout fixture.
2. Show a **"lethal poison (10+)" state** on the seat from the logged counter, and mark the seat "Out" only when Forge says so. Ask the shim to record each loss when Forge applies it; today the "has lost" lines are batched at game end. Forge stays the rules authority.
3. Compute the deciding moment as the first step of the largest single-turn swing that took the winner's last opponent from alive to lethal. Land on the cast or attack that started it and label it "Watch the swing: Triumph of the Hordes, turn 9".

### 3. The cost and status of a sim are misstated before and after you commit (S)

**Where:**
- `web/lib/format.ts:118-124` (`SECONDS_PER_GAME = {2: 2.5, 3: 11, 4: 52}`)
- `/new` rail and runbar at `web/app/new/page.tsx:258-269, 295`
- home `hub-est` at `web/app/page.tsx:283`, also baked into `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:251`
- engine `TYPICAL_GAME_SECONDS = 240` at `engine/mtg_engine.py:556`
- rotation rounding at `engine/mtg_engine.py:474-476`
- the only `simStatus` caller is `web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:61`

**What the player sees:**
- `/new` says "about 14 min" for 4 decks and 16 games, and home says "≈ 8 min". The engine's record for the latest 4-deck, 8-game job is 55 min 56 s, and CLAUDE.md gives 40 to 105 min for 16 games. One click later, `/runs` switches to the server's range.
- The button says "Run 16 games" when 3 decks will play 18.
- "1 game, so you can watch this one play out" actually plays 4 games over tens of minutes.
- "Seat order is the order you pick" is false, because every run rotates seats.
- Close the tab and the running sim has no address anywhere: home and `/results` list finished runs only.

**Why it matters:** this is the only number shown before a JVM job of up to an hour, so a wrong figure breaks trust at the most expensive moment in the product. It breaks CLAUDE.md's "three timing numbers" invariant and the rule to "show the played number and say why". Users who can't find their running job re-queue it, which slows both copies (the engine's own warning).

**Fix:**
- Delete the client estimate table and expose `estimate_sim_seconds` from the engine (for example `GET /estimate?decks=4&games=16`).
- Offer only whole rotations, computed per pod: "4 games (each deck starts once)", "8 (twice)", "16 (four times)". Put the played count on the button.
- Say beside the primary: "Usually 40 to 105 minutes. You can close this tab; it lands in Sims when it's done."
- Pin a "Running now" row, using the design system's live-dot shape, to the top of the Sims list and home, and put a live dot on the Sims nav item.
- Make `/runs` copy state-specific. On a finished job it still says "The simulation keeps running" (`:613`) and points to "the home page" for past runs.

### 4. The report is about the pod, not your deck, and the deck page is a dead end (L)

**Where:** `/results/[file]` (`page.tsx:272-751`); `/decks/[file]` (`web/app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:170-313`); `/new` (`page.tsx:178-283`). Nothing in `web/app` has a concept of "your deck".

**What the player sees:** as the owner of Skrat's Revenge, the lede and headline figures are about Kess. My deck's raw rate is the third scorecard, unmarked. The modelled estimate is 1.75 screens down and the combos 2.4 screens. "What killed it" sits on another tab behind a dropdown that defaults to Kess.

Import ends in a filename and a small link. The deck page never mentions the deck's 14 sims: its actions are "Use in a run · Playtest · Delete deck". There is no "change the deck, sim again, compare" loop.

**Why it matters:** the user arrives with three questions: how good is my deck, why did it win or lose, and what should I change. The page makes them hunt for all three (recognition over recall; verdict first, evidence second, raw data last, which the repo's own `design_principles.md` asks for). Moxfield, Archidekt and EDHREC all centre one deck identified by its commander art.

**Fix:** record a focus deck on the job: the "Your deck" slot on `/new`, falling back to `?deck=`. Default the report to it with a four-deck switcher (§5). Make `/decks/[deck]` the hub with Cards · Sims · Playtest tabs and a "Sim this deck" primary (§3). After import, land on the new deck's hub.

### 5. The replay isn't watchable: pacing, navigation, and no way to find the moment (M)

**Where:**
- `replay/[game]/page.tsx:21` (`SPEED_MS {1:300, 2:150, 4:75}`) and `:211` (uniform `setInterval`)
- `:342-343` (only 81 log rows ever rendered)
- `:456-477` (the scrubber is a click-only `div`)
- `:504-520` (log rows have no click handler)
- `:379-385` and `:525-531` (the same action worded "Jump" in one place and "Skip" in the other)

**What the player sees:**
- Phase markers and mana taps are 60.5% of game 1's 980 steps and 64% of game 4's.
- "Cleanup step" holds the screen exactly as long as "cast Ruby Medallion", so a game at 1x runs 4.9 to 8.6 minutes, mostly dead air. At 4x, spells flash past too fast to read.
- Clicking a log row does nothing. Dragging the scrubber gives no feedback until release.
- The position readout says "event 846 of 980".
- The URL never tracks the playhead.
- Home, End, j/k and ? all do nothing.

**Why it matters:** the viewer's attention goes into the gaps (aesthetic and minimalist design, respect for the user's time). Every good replay viewer navigates in turns and plays and treats its log and timeline as navigation: 17lands, HSReplay/Joust, lichess, Board Game Arena.

**Fix:** a beats index with importance tiers; Highlights, Turn by turn and Every event modes; a four-lane timeline with life lines and key-moment glyphs; clickable, grouped, virtualised log rows; a real `role="slider"` scrubber; a keyboard map; and `?t=` kept up to date on pause and seek. Full spec in §4.

### 6. The replay stage: illegible cards, transport off-screen, invisible zones and stack (M)

**Where:**
- `globals.css:611` (`.stage 1fr 330px; gap 40px`, copied verbatim from the Vercel-palette wireframe `mockups/simlab_v3_replay.html`), plus `.page` max-width 1280
- `globals.css:644` (`.tc` 46x64) and `:664, :688` (30x42)
- `Tabletop.tsx:79` (native `title` tooltip)
- `replay.ts:545` (`BoardState.stack` computed, never rendered)
- `Tabletop.tsx:123-124, 181` (seats in array order in a 2-column grid)

**What the player sees:**
- At 1440x900 the stage starts at y=358 and the transport sits at y≈1025 to 1256. You can see the top seats or the controls, never both.
- The table gets 826 of 1440px.
- At 375px the four seats stack 1,366px tall, and the controls start at y≈2,050.
- Cards can't be read. Hovering one gives a delayed OS tooltip, and the table holds zero focusable elements.
- There is no graveyard, exile, library or command zone, which matters for a reanimator deck whose plan is its graveyard.
- The stack is invisible.
- Turn passes in a Z across the 2x2 grid instead of clockwise.
- The active player is marked by a 12px grey "· active" and a 4.5%-alpha tint.

**Why it matters:** in Magic the card is the unit of meaning. Scrubbing is a look-and-drag loop, and the loop breaks when the control is off-screen (Fitts's law, visibility of status). Tiles fail WCAG 2.1.1. The app already has a full preview hook (`useCardPreview`) that `/decks` and `/playtest` use but the replay doesn't.

**Fix:** a full-bleed theatre that fits 100dvh with a sticky transport; clockwise seats around a centre "in focus" column (stack spotlight, docked card preview); art-crop tiles with P/T and name ribbons; lands collapsed to a strip; a zone rail on shim runs; a phase ladder; and hue-free combat arrows. Spec in §4.

### 7. Names read as machine-made (S)

**Where:** `web/lib/format.ts:10-15` (`shortName` keeps the first whitespace token) and `:27-33` (`runTitle`); `web/app/import/page.tsx:78-83` (the deck name defaults to the first card); `web/lib/replay.ts:873-888` (`commanderGuess` matches the deck name's first word against cast spells).

**What the player sees:** "Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko" as the report h1. "The vs Atraxa vs Ant-Man vs Inspirit". "Living vs NanMan vs Kambal vs Kilo,". Seat plates reading "Kess,". No avatar for Skrat's Revenge or Nekusar Punisher. "Kambal Taxes B3" in copy. The raw filename flashes as the back link while a replay loads.

**Why it matters:** it is the most-read string in the product, and a stray comma in an h1 is the fastest "nobody looked" signal there is.

**Fix:**
- Use the commander as the identity everywhere: short name = the commander's card name up to the first comma, with a leading "The " stripped. That gives Kess, Stella Lee, Krenko and "Unbeatable Squirrel Girl".
- Give owners an editable **table name** on the deck hub ("Squirrel Girl"). Fall back to the deck name only on a clash.
- Add a 24 to 32px Scryfall art-crop avatar beside every deck mention.
- The engine should put commander names (from the `.dck` `[Commander]` section, already parsed at `engine/analysis.py:232-236`) into the run summary, the results index and the game payload. Never guess from the deck name.
- Batch avatar art through the `cards.ts` collection cache instead of four `/cards/named` calls per replay.

### 8. Win rates: three numbers for one fact, no uncertainty, fake "winners" (M)

**Where:**
- `page.tsx:164` (wins / all games) vs `DeckScorecards.tsx:112-116` (wins / decided)
- `PredictionPanel.tsx:52-111` and `engine/predict.py:153-157` (interval = expected ± LOO MAE, independent of n)
- `/results` "Winner" column at `web/app/results/page.tsx:136, 202-217`
- home leaderboard at `page.tsx:187-206`

**What the player sees:**
- One screen shows Kess at "50%" in the lede and the figure, "4 of 7 57%" on its card, and "Simulated 50.0%" in the prediction table.
- "Power Cosmic 25%" is crowned Winner of a 4-deck run, which is exactly the even share.
- Talrand won 0 of 6 decided games and is shown as "Expected 28.2%, 24.3 to 32.2", ranked above a deck that won.
- Rails show 57% vs 0% from n=7, although 0/7 has a 95% interval of 0 to 35% that contains 25%.
- The home leaderboard ranks decks pooled across different pods, then disclaims the ranking in fine print.

**Why it matters:** two numbers for one fact make a careful reader assume the maths is wrong. False precision is the exact overclaim `SIM_CALIBRATION.md` exists to prevent. It is also the weakness of the direct competitor, Grim.Cards ("97.3 power · 1 sim"), and the place Sim Lab can visibly beat it.

**Fix:**
- Use decided games as the single denominator everywhere, stating the exclusion once and inline. Have the engine publish the rate so pages can't drift.
- Show one interval chart per pod (§5.2).
- Widen the model's range with sample size, and grey out rows below 12 decided games.
- Replace "Winner" with "Leader vs even share", showing "tie" or "no clear leader".
- Rank the home leaderboard by points above each pod's even share, weighted and with n shown, or delete it.

### 9. Telemetry is broken for imported decks and scores other decks' plans (M)

**Where:** `engine/mtg_engine.py:866` (`compute()` called without a commander); `engine/deck_telemetry.py:68-91` (`_commander_of` fails for `/data/decks/*`); `web/app/results/[file]/telemetry/page.tsx:198-199, 266-285` (hardcoded rows).

**What the player sees:**
- Kess Reanimator and Skrat's Revenge both say "No commander could be identified", while bundled decks resolve fine.
- Every deck's only plan rows are "Charge counters 0.12/g Partial" and "Proliferate 0/g Never fired". Those are Atraxa-era metrics counted across all seats.
- The lede for a reanimator deck reads "The table logged charge counters 0.12 times a game and proliferate 0."
- The coach (`coach.py:109`) is fed the same rows.

**Why it matters:** the user's own deck gets the broken view and the house decks get the working one, which is backwards. Template leakage like this is the texture of generated output.

**Fix:** pass the deck's `[Commander]` line through `_find_deck()` and add a `/data/decks` test. Delete the universal rows. Until real plan rows exist, show commander first-cast turn, combo-line pieces (from `/analysis`) and "What killed it". Fold the tab into the per-deck report (§5).

### 10. Unfinished and operator states reach players (S)

**Where:**
- `page.tsx:28-31` (`fmtClock` makes "NaN:NaN" on clock-cut draws), `:702` ("T36"), `:706-717` ("Draw (draw)")
- `DeckScorecards.tsx:19-23` ("combat damage / life loss" relabelled "by combat damage", so a Vito + Exquisite Blood drain reads as combat)
- raw Forge strings in the replay log
- `coaching/page.tsx:276-302` (glowing primary "Generate coaching report (~$0.01, about 20 s)" above "the button above will fail. Set MTG_LLM_API_KEY in deploy/.env and redeploy")
- `rules/page.tsx:209, 264-268` ("ASK" primary although `health.llm` is false)
- `ENGINE_CMD` "Start it with python3 engine/mtg_engine.py serve 8484" on four pages
- `Chrome.tsx:136` (ApiBaseSetting "Engine /engine Change" in the public phone nav)

**What the player sees:** NaN in a table, a turn counter in a unit nobody uses, env var names, a shell command, a per-call dollar price, and a primary button the page admits will fail.

**Why it matters:** "never disable the primary" was applied mechanically to a feature that cannot work. Operator detail shown to players is the clearest sign that nobody walked the page as a user (Nielsen #2 and #9, error prevention).

**Fix:**
- Formatter guards: missing values render as an en dash; an outcome label never repeats its category.
- Draws say why: "Draw: hit the 15-minute clock on turn 10".
- Label life-total kills "life reached 0 (combat or life loss)" until `analysis.py` attributes the source.
- Read `health().llm`. When it is false, hide the Coaching tab and make "Search the rules" the only primary on `/rules`.
- Gate all ops copy behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`.
- Add to `.claude/skills/ui-review`: "no NaN, undefined, raw ids, braces, env vars or file names in rendered text".

### 11. The home page is an AI template that never says what the product is (M)

**Where:** `web/app/page.tsx:98-114` (pips as tally icons), `:216-283`, `:248` ("What would you like to do today?"), `:254-274` (four hardcoded hexes), `:297, :395` (loading renders as empty). The spec mandates this layout in `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §5-6.

**What the player sees:**
- A mascot and wordmark over storm art.
- "43 decks on this engine · 317 games simulated · 46 finished runs · 3,152 rules loaded", counting up from zero, with the White, Blue, Red and colourless medallions as ornaments.
- A chatbot greeting.
- Four equal all-caps glowing buttons that duplicate the nav.
- While data loads: "0 decks" and "No finished runs yet" beside "loading…".

**Why it matters:**
- It fails the 10-second test.
- It hits five items on the repo's own AI-tell list in `mockups/design_principles.md` Part 1: #2 glass and glow, #3 stat banner, #6 all-caps, #8 Space Grotesk, #9 centred hero.
- It breaks DS law 3: a red medallion beside "46 finished runs" reads as red decks.
- False zeros tell a returning player they have nothing.

**Fix:** a content-first home (§3). A two-sentence lede computed from data, one primary, a "running now" row, your latest sim as a single sentence with four commander avatars, and your decks. Loading, empty and error are three separate states.

### 12. The AI pilot's reasoning, the differentiator, is never shown (M)

**Where:** `game.agent_events` and `game.rubric` are in every shim result. Grep finds no reference to `agent_events` in `web/`.

**What the player sees:** nothing. The data exists: game 1 has 37 agent events, for example "finisher_hold Triumph of the Hordes creatures=1 need=3", "kingmaker_reaim onto=Skrat's Revenge leaderThreat=8", "tutor_steer steer=Hullbreaker Horror over=Blasphemous Act" and "counter_veto Crackle with Power". The rubric records declined blocks (15 legal blocks declined on the final turn) and mulligans.

**Why it matters:** "why did that player do that?" is the question this product alone can answer. It is also the evidence an investor wants to see the model producing.

**Fix:** add a "Pilot's notes" layer: inline log rows, timeline glyphs and a one-line caption under the phase ladder, translated into player language and always worded as the AI's stated reason, never as right or wrong (§4.9).

### 13. The deck page is a 10-screen oracle dump with raw `{1}{G}{G}{G}` (M)

**Where:** `web/app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:28-69, 246-300`; `globals.css:869-877`.

**What the player sees:** 75 rows at 92px each (9,370px tall): the full oracle text of cards this audience already knows. Costs appear as raw braces in 11.5px ink-4 mono. There is no curve, colour demand, bracket, commander banner, record or link to the deck's sims, and it says "99 cards" where every deckbuilder counts 100. While facts load, all 99 cards briefly sit under "Unidentified".

**Why it matters:** Jakob's law. Moxfield and Archidekt have trained this audience to expect dense grouped columns with a docked preview. Raw braces are the strongest "unpolished" signal a Magic site can show.

**Fix:**
- A compact 3 to 4 column list grouped by type ("Creatures 25"): quantity · name · cost glyphs.
- Oracle text only in a docked preview.
- A stats strip: curve 0 to 7+, type counts, coloured pip demand vs sources.
- A header: art-crop banner, identity, bracket, "100 cards", record.
- A view toggle (List / Visual / Full text) kept in the URL.
- Skeletons, never "Unidentified", while loading.

### 14. Type, spacing, contrast and colour are in a fog, and the palette collides with WUBRG (M)

**Where:**
- `globals.css`: 136 `font-size` declarations across 18 distinct sizes; the `--size-*` tokens are used 9 times
- `.mono { font-size: 0.93em }` at `:163` compounds into sizes like 12.09px and 12.555px; 48% of the results page's text nodes are JetBrains Mono
- about 290 raw px spacing values across 31 distinct sizes
- `outline: none` on `input.txt`, `textarea.paste`, `.inp input` (`:522, :574, :577`) beats the global 2px ring
- `--hairline-strong` measures 1.45:1 against panels
- In the tokens file: `--arcane-violet` (`:48`) and `--pip-b` (`:84`) are both `#A855F7`; `--state-failed` (`:106`) and `--pip-r` (`:85`) are both `#EF4444`; `--state-done` (`:105`) and `--pip-g` (`:86`) are both `#10B981`. The replay draws attackers in `--state-failed`.

**What the player sees:** a fog of near-identical small grey text; buttons touching on `/rules` (zero gap); inputs that are faint rectangles with a weak focus cue; red meaning red mana, failure and attacking all at once; deck-performance chips drawn in job-status shapes (Krenko's 0 of 7 looks like a crashed job).

**Why it matters:** this is the unnamed "jank". Without a scale, hierarchy collapses. `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` §8 promises WCAG 1.4.11 and 2.4.7 and breaks both on the fields people type into. Law 3 ("a colour never means two things") is broken at the token level.

**Fix:** a six-step type ramp, a 4px spacing grid, a `--control-edge` token at 3:1, and the global focus ring restored. Retire violet as a UI accent, draw status marks by shape alone, draw combat without hue, and stop using status glyphs for deck outcomes. Details in §6.

### 15. The playtest sandbox is below the Moxfield/Archidekt baseline and fails keyboard and touch (L)

**Where:** `web/app/playtest/[deck]/page.tsx:230-246` (moves are drag-only), `:452-461` (the library is `role=button` with no tabIndex), `:280-315` (buttons nested inside a role=button); `globals.css:906-921` (18px counter buttons, shown only on hover).

**What the player sees:** Skrat's opening hand held Finale of Devastation and Nature's Rhythm, and the sandbox can resolve neither. There is no library search, no look-at-top-N, no standalone shuffle and no undo; tokens are all named "Token"; Reset has no confirmation. Keyboard users can't send a card to the graveyard or add counters. On a phone, hand-to-graveyard is a 600px drag. The zone label reads "Battlefield (tap to tap)".

**Why it matters:** it fails WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7 and 2.5.8. An enfranchised player compares it with Moxfield once and leaves.

**Fix:**
- A per-card action menu (Tap, To hand, graveyard, exile, top or bottom of library, counters).
- Keyboard shortcuts matching Moxfield and Archidekt habits (D, M, N, S, Ctrl+Z, ?).
- Search library, look at top N, shuffle, undo.
- Named tokens from Scryfall `all_parts`.
- A playmat layout.

All of it stays rules-free: the user decides, and the app only moves cards.

**Below the line, still worth fixing:**
- The deck gallery is 43 flat tiles. Seven Inspirit and eight Kilo variants share identical art. The colour filter is OR where it should be subset. Dev decks are public. Group by commander, show "Your decks" first, and hide test lists behind a toggle.
- Import has three dead "coming soon" tabs and a lede promising suggested fixes that don't exist. Partner and background commanders can't be set.
- Every route's title is "Arcane Sim Lab". There is no favicon, no `<main>` or skip link, and there are eight bare "Watch" links.
- `/rules` search misses 903.9a for the commonest Commander question, and cuts excerpts mid-word.
- `CardPreview.tsx:239` shows the previous card until the new image decodes (fix with `key={src}`), and has em dashes in its aria-label.
- "Delete deck" sits at the same weight as the primary.
- A 2.65 MB PNG backdrop loads on every route.

## 3. Information architecture

### 3.1 The nouns (a glossary to enforce everywhere)

One concept currently has seven names: simulation, sim, run, gauntlet, pod, result, report. Cut them to five.

| Noun | Means | Never call it |
|---|---|---|
| **Deck** | A Commander list, identified by its commander's art and table name | "decklist file", `.dck` |
| **Sim** | N seat-rotated games of 2 to 4 decks, running or finished | run, gauntlet, result, report, job, simulation (except in long-form copy) |
| **Pod** | The set of decks in a sim | (fine as a descriptor: "the pod", "pod average") |
| **Game** | One game inside a sim | round, match |
| **Replay** | Watching one game | playback |
| **Playtest** | Solo, rules-free goldfishing | test |

"Sim" wins because it is the brand word and what players say ("I simmed it"). I rejected "Test", FR-11's proposal, because it collides with Playtest in the same nav. "Engine" and "telemetry" leave user copy entirely. "Turn N" always means the table round: everyone's first turn is turn 1. Forge's global counter (T36) is never displayed.

### 3.2 Navigation

`[archivist head] Sim Lab     Decks   Sims (•)   Playtest   Rules                 [New sim]`

- Four noun items and one action button, styled secondary so the page's own primary stays the only primary.
- The Sims item carries a live dot while any sim is running.
- Inside a sim, the tab set never changes: **Summary · Games · Coaching**. Coaching is hidden while `llm` is false. Telemetry folds into Summary. A replay is a sub-state of Games, not a tab set of its own.

### 3.3 The primary loop

```
Import deck ──> Deck hub ──"Sim this deck"──> New sim (your deck + opponents preset + rotations + honest duration)
     ^                                                   |
     |                                                   v
 Update deck <── "What to look at" <── Summary (your deck) <── Sim page (running: live playback, can leave)
 (diff since                              |
  last sim)                               v
                                 Games as stories ──> Replay, landing on the swing ──> next game [ ]
```

The loop that is missing today is **change the deck → sim again against the same pod → compare**. It needs deck versions (re-import onto an existing deck), a "same pod as last time" preset, and a "since last sim" diff on the hub: cards in and out, and whether the win rate moved beyond noise at this sample size.

### 3.4 Page map

| Route | Purpose | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| `/` | What Sim Lab is (2 computed sentences), one primary, Running now, Your latest sim, Your decks | Hero, tally, hub |
| `/decks` | Your decks first, then sample decks grouped by commander, with sort by recently simmed | 43 flat tiles |
| `/decks/new` | Paste box (detects Moxfield/Archidekt URLs and explains the export path), live checks, save, then land on the hub | `/import` |
| `/decks/[deck]` | **The hub.** Header: art banner, identity, bracket, 100 cards, record. Tabs: **Cards · Sims · Playtest** | Dead-end card dump |
| `/sims` | All sims, running ones pinned first; "Leader vs even share" column; deck chips filter | `/results` |
| `/sims/new?deck=` | "Your deck" slot, an Opponents picker with presets ("Bracket 3 field", "Same pod as last time"), rotations, engine-sourced duration | `/new` |
| `/sims/[id]` | **One URL, two states.** Running: live playback, progress, a seat grid filling in, "you can close this tab". Finished: the Summary (§5) | `/runs/[id]` + `/results/[file]` |
| `/sims/[id]/games/[n]` | Replay (§4) | `/results/[file]/replay/[game]` |
| `/sims/[id]/coaching` | Only when live | Always-visible dead tab |
| `/playtest/[deck]` | Goldfish | Same |
| `/rules` | "Search the rules" (plus Ask when live), with chips for 903, 704, 613, 506-511 | Same |

URL renames are optional. The words matter more than the paths. If routes do change, redirect every old `/results/...` link, because playtesters share them.

## 4. Replay viewer redesign spec

### 4.1 What people open a replay for

In order: (1) **How did it end?** (2) **What was the swing?** (3) **Why did they do that?** (4) **What did my deck actually draw and do?** The default view answers (1) and (2) within five seconds. The Pilot's notes answer (3). Seat focus and the log answer (4). Watching is lean-back and studying is lean-forward, so the viewer supports both (the chess.com Game Review pattern: a directed key-moment mode beside a free stepper).

### 4.3 Regions

**A. Header strip.** Back to the sim, four commander avatars and the matchup (commander short names), and a game switcher. Each game chip shows the winner's avatar, or an en dash for a draw. `[` and `]` move between games. Also here: a provenance chip ("Board: read exactly", or on stdout runs "Board: inferred from the log, 86% exit match") that opens the full TabletopNote, and a copy-link icon.
- The H1 becomes the page title: "Game 1: Squirrel Girl wins with poison (turn 10)". Never "Game 1".
- Delete the page-level note "Replays fold the event log into board state locally" (`page.tsx:492-495`). On shim runs it contradicts the chip.

**B. Phase ladder.** Read-only and compact, after MTG Arena's deliberately minimal ladder. It shows "Turn 9 · (avatar) Squirrel Girl", then Beginning · Main 1 · Combat · Main 2 · End with the current step filled. Combat expands into attack, blockers and damage only during combat, and splits damage into first-strike and regular only when the log shows both.
- The ladder replaces every "X's Upkeep step" row as a playback stop.
- **B'** is a single caption line that shows the Pilot's note or key-moment caption for the current beat, and is empty otherwise.

**C. Table: clockwise seats with stable geometry.** Seat 1 top-left, 2 top-right, 3 bottom-right, 4 bottom-left. Turn passes clockwise as at a real table and in SpellTable's four-quadrant grid; today it goes in a Z. Seats never reflow during playback.
- I rejected the Untap.in-style "accordion follows the active seat" as the default. It would reflow 36+ times a game, destroy the viewer's spatial memory ("Kess is top-left"), and make combat arrows jump.
- Focus is available on demand (4.4).

Seat anatomy, top to bottom:
1. **Plate.**
   - 40px commander avatar; partner pairs as a split circle.
   - Table name, with the deck name as a subtitle.
   - **Life as the loudest numeral on the plate** (28px tabular). A ±delta chip shows for about 900ms on change, and stays static under reduced motion.
   - Poison and commander-damage chips appear only when non-zero, and switch to warning treatment at 7 poison and 15 commander damage.
2. **Zone rail** (shim runs): Library · Graveyard · Exile · Command, each a count that opens a popover of the actual cards at the playhead. A crown glyph (inline SVG, not a WotC symbol) marks the commander wherever it is, with "cast 2x · tax 4" from Command→Stack records.
3. **Creatures band:** art-crop tiles 96x70 with a 16px name ribbon and a P/T badge. Tapped rotates only the frame; the name ribbon stays upright. A token stack shows a ×N count and a partial-tap chip ("3 tapped").
4. **Other permanents:** 72x52 art crops, same grammar.
5. **Lands strip:** a single line, "Lands 9 · 3 untapped". Expanding it lists names with counts ("Forest ×4, Breeding Pool…"). Untapped-land count is what players actually scan for open mana. It frees roughly 40% of a seat's height for creatures (the Mystmin and Arena pattern).
6. **Hand:** "Hand 4", with small card backs, or faces on shim runs where hands are exact. A "mulled to 6" note appears when relevant.
7. An **"Entered this turn"** marker on tiles, read from the zone stream. This is a fact. "Summoning sick" would be a rules inference, so it isn't shown.

- **Active seat:** a 2px cyan frame. This is the sanctioned glow for live activity, and it is the only one on the page.
- **Eliminated seat:** its board greys out, and the plate reads "Out on turn 9 · poison (Squirrel Girl)" in the design system's "out" shape.
- **Lethal but not yet reported:** a "Lethal poison (46)" badge.

**D. Centre column, "In focus" (208px).** The single place the eye goes each beat, after HSReplay's played-card spotlight, 17lands' stack card and Forge's card-detail pane.
- When the stack is non-empty it shows the top object as a Scryfall `normal` image at 200px, with "Cast by Squirrel Girl" and "→ targeting Phyrexian Beast Token" parsed from Forge's `targeting [X (id)]`. Below it: a numbered stack list with the caster's avatar.
- When the stack is empty it shows the hovered or focused card, or failing that the last card to resolve.
- It fades on `stack_resolve`. Hovering any tile or log name shows that card here, so the preview never covers the board.

**E. Combat overlay (SVG over the table), hue-free.** One arrow per defender lane, running from the attacking seat's creature band to the defender's plate, labelled "10 attackers · 40 power → Krenko". Stroke weight scales with power.
- Attacking tiles lift 6px, the Arena "moves forward" cue, and get an ink-max outline. Blockers get a dashed connector to the creature they block.
- Duplicate names collapse: "10× Phyrexian Beast Token (4/4)".
- There is no red. Red is a WUBRG colour and the failed-status colour, and today it also means "attacking" (§6).

**F. Right rail (340px): Moments | Log.**
- **Moments** (the default tab in Highlights mode) lists the game's key moments, typically 4 to 8, each with its turn, the actor's avatar and one line: "Turn 9 · Squirrel Girl: Triumph of the Hordes, 15 infect attackers at Stella and Krenko". Clicking seeks.
- **Log** is covered in 4.9.

**G. Lane timeline**, the Commander equivalent of lichess's evaluation graph. There is one lane per seat, in turn order, with the seat avatar at the left, all on a shared x-axis of turns. Small multiples avoid the need for four seat hues.
- Each lane shades the blocks where it was that seat's turn, with width proportional to the beats in that turn (HSReplay and 17lands proportional segments).
- Inside each lane is that seat's life line, with its own scale from 0 to the starting 40. Poison is a dotted overlay, and an × marks elimination.
- Five key-moment glyphs, inline SVG and always the same five: ◆ commander cast, ▲ big swing, ◼ board wipe (3+ nonland permanents leaving in one phase), ◇ combo line came together (from `/analysis` piece-arrival turns), × elimination. Pilot's notes are small ticks. Focusing a seat brightens its glyphs and fades the others (the League of Legends Annotated Timeline pattern).
- The playhead is one vertical line crossing all four lanes. The timeline is `role="slider"` with pointer-capture drag that seeks on `pointermove`, throttled to animation frames. Hovering shows a tooltip: "Turn 9 · Squirrel Girl · Triumph of the Hordes · 66 events".
- The swing becomes visible as the moment the lines split.

**H. Transport (sticky, 44px).** Previous turn · previous play · Play/Pause · next play · next turn; a mode selector (Highlights · Turn by turn · Every event); speed (0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x, persisted in `localStorage` inside try/catch); "?"; a position readout reading "Turn 9 of 10", not "event 846 of 980". Key hints live in button titles ("Next turn (Shift+→)"). Delete the separate "Keyboard:" paragraph.

### 4.4 Surviving dense boards

Commander boards win with tokens, and Skrat's won with 10 Beasts and a pile of Squirrels. In order:
1. Stack identical permanents as ×N, keeping token copies separate from originals, which the replay already does correctly.
2. Collapse lands to the strip.
3. Shrink creature tiles 96 → 72 → 56px as the band fills.
4. Past that, show a "+N" button that opens **Seat focus**: the seat expands to the full table and the other three become compact strips across the top in turn order (avatar, life, hand, creature count, total power, top three threats by power). The trigger is either the "+N" button or pressing 1 to 4 or clicking a plate; `0` or Esc returns. The layout does not reflow on its own.

This is SpellTable's Focused layout and Untap.in's Full Board, used on demand. Cockatrice's four even strips are the documented failure.

On a combat beat, overflowing attackers always render in the attacking seat's band first. The attack is the point of the beat.

### 4.5 Beats, tiers and pacing

`lib/replay.ts` builds a beats index over `timeline.steps` and assigns each step a tier:

| Tier | Steps | Highlights | Turn by turn | Every event |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | phase markers, mana abilities, `player_control`, `match_result`, reminder-text lines | skipped (the ladder shows them) | skipped | 250ms |
| 1 | land played, cast, resolve, trigger, "didn't block" runs (collapsed into one beat: "Kess didn't block 15 attackers") | skipped | 600ms | 600ms |
| 2 | attack, block, damage, life change, nonland permanent leaving the battlefield | 900ms | 900ms | 900ms |
| 3 | elimination or lethal state, commander cast, board wipe, the swing, combo line came together | 1800ms + caption held in B' | pause at turn end with a one-line turn summary | 1500ms |

Times are at 1x. **Highlights** is the default for the Play button: an 8-minute game becomes a roughly 60-second story. **Turn by turn** pages through computed turn summaries ("Turn 9, Squirrel Girl: Triumph of the Hordes; swung 15 infect at Stella and Krenko; Krenko 46 poison, Stella 19"). Arrow keys step visible beats; Alt+arrow steps raw events.

### 4.6 Key moments and "Watch the swing"

Key moments come only from logged events, the zone stream and `/analysis` piece-arrival turns, never from oracle text. They are: eliminations and lethal states, the largest life or poison swing per turn, mass zone changes, commander casts, a combo line coming together, a counterspell (agent `counter_fire`), and the swing itself as defined in problem 2.

The replay lede says: "Squirrel Girl won with poison. The swing came on turn 9: Triumph of the Hordes, then 15 infect attackers at Stella and Krenko." Its primary is **[Watch the swing]**, and the old duplicated "Jump/Skip to the deciding turn" links go away.

### 4.7 The log (Log tab)

- **Virtualised full list** instead of the 81-row window, so Ctrl-F works. Every row is a `<button>` that seeks (the Board Game Arena and lichess move-list pattern). The current row stays highlighted and in view.
- **Sticky turn headers** ("Turn 9 · (avatar) Squirrel Girl"), collapsible.
- **Filter chips:** Key plays (tier 2+) · Combat · one per seat · Pilot's notes · Everything.
- **Grammar rewritten** in `lib/replay.ts`:
  - "Life: Kambal Taxes B3 50 > 47" → "Kambal 50 → 47 (−3)"
  - a bare resolve line → "Ruby Medallion resolves"
  - strip `[Card: … Activator: … SpellAbility: …]`
  - drop "has restored control over themself" and the match-score line
  - "receives 46 poison counter" → "Krenko: +15 poison (46)"
  - "Turn 18" → a game-over row
  - instance ids appear only when two same-named objects need telling apart (the existing disambiguation at `replay.ts:192` stays)
- Every card name gets a hover or focus target that fills the In Focus column and pulses the matching tile.
- Fix the current-row overflow jitter by replacing the negative margin with `padding-inline` + `box-shadow` (`globals.css:734`).

### 4.8 Pilot's notes (the differentiator)

Translate `agent_events` codes into plain English and show them in three places: an inline log row in a distinct register (thin ink-3 left rule, a "Pilot" label, italic), a tick on the timeline, and the B' caption while the relevant beat is on screen.

| Code | Rendered |
|---|---|
| `finisher_hold Triumph of the Hordes creatures=1 need=3` | "Held Triumph of the Hordes: 1 creature, wanted 3." |
| `kingmaker_reaim moved=2 onto=Skrat's Revenge leaderThreat=8` | "Stella moved 2 attackers onto Squirrel Girl, the table leader." |
| `tutor_steer steer=Hullbreaker Horror over=Blasphemous Act` | "Kess searched for Hullbreaker Horror over Blasphemous Act." |
| `counter_veto Crackle with Power threat=4.0` | "Kess let Crackle with Power resolve (threat judged too low to counter)." |
| rubric `legalMissed 15` | on the defender's plate during that combat: "Declined 15 legal blocks, took 12." |
| rubric mulligans | pregame: "Squirrel Girl mulliganed to 6 (first seven had 1 land)." |

Never label a play correct, wrong or a blunder; chess.com's redefinitions of Brilliant and Blunder show how that backfires. These notes are the AI's stated reasons. A "Show pilot's notes" toggle, on by default, lets purists hide them.

Keep the code dictionary next to the shim's code list, so a new code shows as "Pilot: (unrecognised note)" rather than silently disappearing.

### 4.9 Beginning and end

- **Pregame:** each seat's kept hand fanned at readable size, with mulligan notes. On shim runs, where hands are exact, this is something no Arena or MTGO replay can show.
- **End card**, overlaid on the table at the final step on an opaque surface with no glass:
  - winner avatar and "Squirrel Girl wins with poison, turn 10"
  - elimination order with turns and causes ("Krenko: turn 9, poison. Stella: turn 9, poison. Kess: turn 10, poison.")
  - the killing card at full size
  - [Watch the swing] and [Next game]
- **Draws:** "Cut off by the 15-minute game clock on turn 10, with Stella (33), Krenko (17) and Kess (8) still in. Squirrel Girl was already out." Draws hide the swing link.

```
   [Watch its win: game 1, the turn-9 swing]      Watch its fastest loss

HOW DID IT WIN AND LOSE?            won: poison 1 . lost: 0 life 5 . 1 draw (clock)
   Knocked out on turn 8 on median (table median 10). Most damage taken from:
   Kess, Dissident Mage 24 . (card hover on every name)   -> each row filters the game list

DID THE COMBOS GO OFF?              (§5.3)
DID THE MANA WORK?                  kept-hand lands vs what its land count predicts . missed land drops per 10 turns
WHAT'S WORTH A LOOK                 bottleneck cards . one card away from a finisher line . a watched card
ITS GAMES                           story cards, won then lost (§5.4)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

```

- Section headings are the player's questions, each followed by one computed sentence answering it, then the figure. This is Playgroup.gg's pattern, the closest match to how Commander players already read stats.
- The focus deck is the default and the switcher changes the whole report.
- The pod-level lede ("Kess won 4 of 7…") moves into the pod section.
- **Delete** the four headline figures, which restate the lede, and "Still standing at the end of 57% of them", which in a four-player game always equals the win rate.

### 5.2 Presenting win rates honestly

1. **One denominator: decided games.** State the exclusion inline, once: "4 of 7 decided (57%); 1 game hit the clock and isn't counted." The engine publishes the rate, and the lede, figures, prediction and pod table all read it.
2. **One interval chart for the pod**, replacing the rails and the prediction table:

```
                0%        25%|       50%        75%       100%
                          even share
 (K) Kess       ....[=====o==|=====(o)==========]....       4 of 7   floor: engine deck
 (S) Stella     .[===o=======|==(o)====]...                 2 of 7
 (Q) Sq. Girl   [=o==========|==]  (o)                      1 of 7   your deck
 (R) Krenko     o============|                              0 of 7
                o sim result + 95% range     (o) playgroup model's estimate      | archetype baseline tick per row
```

   - Wilson 95% intervals on decided games: Kess 4/7 → 25-84%, Stella 2/7 → 8-64%, Squirrel Girl 1/7 → 3-51%, Krenko 0/7 → 0-35%.
   - The filled dot is the sim. The hollow dot is the model, always hollow because it is inferred.
   - The 25% even share is a labelled vertical rule, with each deck's archetype baseline as a small tick on its row (as `SIM_CALIBRATION` requires).
   - Engine and combo archetypes carry a "floor" tag.
3. **Whole percents below 30 decided games.** No decimals on eight-game runs.
4. **Small-sample treatment:** below 12 decided games the model's dot is suppressed and the row says "Too few games for a model estimate", in ink-3, as 17lands and Playgroup's italics do. One line in the section: "8 games is a first look; about 32 separate decks with confidence."
5. **The model gets a job and a basis in plain words:** "Trained on 66 precons played by people, with stock Forge. This sim used Sim Lab's pilot on custom decks." Each deck's existing `explanation` ("Adjusted up because this deck runs few creatures") renders under its row.
   - If the model's ranking differs from the sim's, the lede's second sentence says so. There are never two unexplained verdicts.
   - Widen `predict.py`'s range by carrying the sim's binomial uncertainty through the model's sim weight before adding the MAE.
6. **Leaders, not winners:** in lists, "Kess 57% (+32 over even share)". Show "tie" for ties and "no clear leader" at or below 1/N.
7. **Show the rotation instead of stating it:** a deck-by-seat grid with a win mark in each cell (for example, Kess won from seats 1, 2 and 4, not only from going first).

### 5.3 The combo section, rebuilt the way an expert expects

**Heading:** "Did the combos go off?" **Answer line** (computed, Kess run): "No game was won by a combo line. 6 ended at 0 life (combat or life loss), 1 by poison, 1 hit the clock. One engine came together once."

**Per deck**, under a commander-art subhead, grouped into bands in this order:

1. **Finishers: ends the game on the spot.** Spellbook results include "Win the game", infinite damage or life loss to opponents, "each opponent loses", or infinite opponent mill.
2. **Combat finishers: builds a lethal board, still has to attack.** Infinite hasty tokens, infinite power.
3. **Engines: need a payoff.** Infinite mana, storm, ETB/LTB, untaps, draw. Each engine lists its payoffs using only Spellbook's own data: a larger combo in the same 99 whose cards include the engine and which produces a win becomes the payoff line. Otherwise it reads "No payoff in this 99 that Commander Spellbook lists." This keeps classification inside Spellbook's results and never derives card behaviour from oracle text.
4. **Commander loops:** lines whose only card is the commander, and which therefore depend on prerequisites. "Assembled" must never mean "commander on the battlefield".

Maintain the mapping from Spellbook's result features to bands as a table in `analysis.py`, with a test over every feature name in the cache. An unknown feature defaults to Engine.

**One row per family, never per variant.** `_slim()` must keep Spellbook's `of` (family), `requires` (template pieces), `bracketTag` and each card's initial zone; then re-fetch the cache. The fallback heuristic, used only if `of` is missing: same results, and all cards but one in common.

```
Squirrel Girl  (The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl)
  COMBAT FINISHER   [results per Spellbook]                                  Commander Spellbook ->
  Squirrel Girl (commander) + one of 5 [Concordant Crossroads, Thousand-Year Elixir, Akroma's Memorial, ...]
                            + one of 5 [Cryptolith Rite, Enduring Vitality, Elven Chorus, ...]     25 variants in your 99
    Needs        You control four or more Squirrels
    In play      0 of 8 games (any variant). Expected about 0.2 times in 8 games from draw odds.
    Bottleneck   [card most often missing, hover preview]
  ...2 more lines never came together (each expected under once in 8 games)

Kess  (Kess, Dissident Mage)
  ENGINE, needs a payoff
  Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring + a permanent castable for colourless mana              Commander Spellbook ->
    Makes        infinite colourless mana, infinite storm count
    Payoff       none in this 99 that Commander Spellbook lists
    In play      came together in 1 of 8 games. Kess won that game in combat, not with this line.

Stella  (Stella Lee, Wild Card)
  COMMANDER LOOP
  Stella Lee (commander) + [Spellbook's prerequisites]
    On the battlefield in 8 of 8 games; the loop never ran. The pilot doesn't execute this
    loop yet, so treat Stella's results as a floor.
```

*Illustrative layout: the slot lists and "Needs" line come from the playtester's run; placeholders in brackets are Spellbook fields.*

- **Stats per line** count any variant: games it came together, earliest turn (table rounds), "won that game", and **"won with it"**. "Won with it" means the game's loss line matches the line's results on or right after the turn it came online. `analysis.py` computes it so the UI and the coach agree, and only "won with it" can ever read as "fired".
- **Expand** shows Spellbook's structure verbatim (Initial card state · Notable prerequisites · Steps · Results) plus a link to `commanderspellbook.com/combo/{id}`. Sim Lab never re-explains the steps.
- The **commander** gets a chip on its piece, and template pieces get a muted chip ("+ a permanent castable for colourless mana").
- Show the per-line **bracket tag**.
- **Order within a deck:** finishers first, then by games in play. Fold anything never assembled with expected < 1.
- **"One card away"** belongs in "What's worth a look": the three cards that would complete the most finisher lines, from Spellbook's near-combos, each with a hover preview.
- **Never** use the words "win condition" for anything other than the Finishers band.

### 5.4 Games as story cards

Replace the Game / Winner / Ended / Duration / Decided by / Replay table, which today mixes "T36" with "round 10", shows NaN:NaN, and repeats the winner. Use one card or row per game:

```
 1  (Q) Squirrel Girl . poison . turn 10          out: (R) t9 poison . (S) t9 poison . (K) t10 poison
    Turn 9: Triumph of the Hordes, 15 infect attackers at Stella and Krenko.     [Watch the swing]
 6  Draw . hit the 15-minute clock on turn 10     out: (Q) t8 . still in: Stella 33, Krenko 17, Kess 8
```

- The whole row links to the replay, deep-linked to the swing.
- Deck chips filter the list ("Kess 4 · Stella 2 · Squirrel Girl 1 · Draw 1"); clicking a kill source in "How did it win and lose?" filters it too, which ties statistics to evidence.
- Sorts: "biggest swing" and "combo came together".
- Wall-clock duration moves to Sim details.
- Every winner gets the same identity marker, not only the leader's green squares.

### 5.5 The pod side by side

Replace the four prose scorecards with one comparison table: decks as columns, each headed by art, pips and W-L; rows grouped as below, plus a **pod average** column.
- **Outcome:** median win turn, median knocked-out turn.
- **Mana:** missed land drops per 10 turns, kept-7 rate, lands in kept hands against what that deck's land count predicts for a kept hand.
- **Combat:** blocked %, chump share, attackers committed.

Highlight only cells that differ meaningfully from the pod average. Blocking detail goes behind "Combat detail" (the 17lands summary/table split). One computed sentence per deck moves into its focus report.

### 5.6 What moves and what dies

- **Telemetry:** "What killed it" moves into the report. The universal charge-counter and proliferate rows are deleted. "Watched cards" gets a visible "Track a card" field, autocompleted from the decklist, where today it needs a hand-typed `?watch=`.
- **Coaching:** hidden until live. When it ships, it reads the combo lines, the comparison figures and the prediction. Every change must quote its number and name a replacement. "Matchups" becomes "Who beat you".
- **Every card name** on these pages gets `CardPreview`. Every deck mention gets its avatar.

## 7. Voice and microcopy

*(Section 6, visual language, follows after this, because the voice rules inform the type choices.)*

**Principles**
1. **Write like a player writing up pod night.** "Kess won 4 of 7", "knocked out on turn 8", "mulliganed to 6". No engine words (engine, telemetry, event, job, .dck), no Forge turn counter.
2. **Computed, never canned.** Every lede and heading answer is built from this sim's data. If a sentence would read the same on another sim, delete it.
3. **Every number carries its denominator and its comparison,** in the same sentence.
4. **Facts plain, opinions labelled.** The model's estimate is "modelled"; the pilot's reasons are "Pilot's note"; coaching is signed. Never "results meaningful".
5. **Caveats sit next to their number,** in a few words. The 70-word hedge paragraphs collapse into one "How to read this sim" disclosure.
6. **Sentence case everywhere,** buttons included. No chatbot greetings, no exclamation marks, no puns ("tap to tap").
7. **Dark features say so in player language** and show no primary. Operator detail never reaches players.
8. **No em dashes** (house rule). An en dash for empty values. A true minus (−16 pts).

**Before and after (real strings)**

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Home, main line | "What would you like to do today?" | "Paste a Commander list. Sim Lab seats it at a four-player table against Forge's AI for 8 to 64 games, rotating seats so nobody keeps the first turn, and shows you how it wins, how it loses, and every game to watch." |
| Home, estimate | "two decks ≈ 5 s a game · four decks ≈ 8 min for 16" | (beside the primary on /sims/new) "Four decks, 16 games: usually 40 to 105 minutes. You can close this tab; the sim lands in Sims when it's done." |
| /new games select | "1 game, so you can watch this one play out" | "4 games (each deck starts once)" |
| /new empty rail | "Seat order is the order you pick" | "Every deck takes every seat, so order doesn't matter." |
| Report h1 | "Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko" | "Kess vs Stella vs Squirrel Girl vs Krenko" (with four avatars) |
| Combo chip | "AI can fire this; results meaningful" | "Came together in 1 of 8 games. Kess won that game in combat, not with this line." |
| Combo chip (×33) | "draw odds predicted ~0.2; too few games to measure this" | (once, above the list) "Lines you'd expect to see less than once in 8 games are folded below." |
| Games table, draw | "Draw (draw)" · "NaN:NaN" | "Draw: hit the 15-minute clock on turn 10 (Squirrel Girl already out)" · "–" |

## 6. Visual language

The Arcane system gives Sim Lab an ownable identity: commissioned pips, the brass archivist and painted plates. It also bakes the AI-slop look into the binding spec, and its colour rule is broken at the token level. **Direction: art is ceremony, data is paper.** Keep one signature moment and make the data interior the craft.

### Keep, cut, change

| Element | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| **Backdrop art** | **Change.** Only on the home masthead band (about 220px, scrimmed), empty states, 404, and the running-sim screen (the one place you wait). Every page you read sits on opaque `--bg-void` / `--surface-obsidian`. Re-encode to AVIF/WebP at about 200 KB with a 750w variant (today it is a 2.65 MB PNG on every route). Drop the plane name in the spec: hedrons read as Zendikar to players, and the spec says Dominaria. | Reading data over high-contrast storm art costs attention on every glance (Rams: unobtrusive). Apple's own guidance for glass: never in the content layer. |
| **Glass** | **Cut from content, keep on chrome.** Header, sticky transport, popovers, card preview. Content panels become opaque with a 1px `--control-edge`. Drop `backdrop-filter` on `.page`. | Glass under 85% opacity is invisible and expensive. Glass over data is design tell #2 in `design_principles.md`. |
| **Glow** | **Change: live activity only.** A running sim's dot, the active seat's frame, the playhead while playing. Primaries become a solid cyan fill with dark ink and no glow. Delete `--atmosphere-leylines` and the violet and blue gradient buttons. | A glow that is always on is decoration; on live things it is information. |
| **Mascot** | **Keep, give it a job.** Head as the nav mark and favicon (from `mascot-brass-archivist-head.webp`). Full figure only in empty states ("Your deck hasn't sat down at a table yet"), the JVM warm-up line, and as the byline on coaching ("The archivist's notes"). Never speaks as a chatbot. | A brass artifact creature suits a simulation lab and is IP-safe. It earns warmth where the product is empty or waiting, not as page chrome. |
| **Cinzel** | **Keep:** wordmark only, once per page (the existing rule). | It is the one flourish, used once. |
| **Painted pips** | **Keep for identity ≥ 18px** (deck tiles, headers, seat plates, filter). **Ban as ornament** (the home tally). **Commission a flat cost-glyph set** for sizes under 18px (W U B R G C, hybrid, generic numeral disc). The spec itself says the black skull disappears below about 20px. Until the set exists, show painted pips at 18px on deck rows; never braces. | Raw `{1}{G}{G}{G}` is the strongest "unfinished" signal on a Magic site. WotC symbols stay off-limits. |
| **Status shapes** | **Keep the shapes, drop the hues** except live cyan. Done = filled ink square, queued = hollow circle, failed = filled circle **plus the word "Failed"**. Use them for job state only, never for deck performance. | `--state-done` = `--pip-g` and `--state-failed` = `--pip-r` (identical hexes). Shape already carries the meaning. |
| **Violet** | **Retire as a UI accent.** Secondary buttons become neutral (ink border). | `--arcane-violet` = `--pip-b` = `#A855F7`. The black-mana colour cannot also mean "secondary". |
| **Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono** | **Replace.** UI and body in **IBM Plex Sans** with tabular lining figures (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`) for every number; **IBM Plex Mono** only for ids, seeds, filenames and the raw-log toggle. Before committing, set the scorecard table and the replay log in Plex Sans and in Source Sans 3 and choose by reading them. | Space Grotesk is tell #8 in the repo's own list, and the face generators converge on. Mono is 48% of the results page's text. Plex has real tabular figures, distinct Il1/0O for counts, compact width for long card names ("Circle of Dreams Druid"), and an engineered character that fits a lab without the fingerprint. |
| **All-caps CTAs** | **Cut.** Sentence case, 14 to 15px. | Tell #6; long all-caps payloads ("NEXT TURN: UNTAP ALL, DRAW 1") read as shouting. |
| **Home §5-6 of the spec** | **Cut** the tally banner, the prompt line and the four-button hub from `DESIGN_SYSTEM.md`. | The spec mandates the slop (tells #3, #6, #9). |
| **A11y contract, law 5 "fixes subtract", em-dash rule, ink floor** | **Keep and enforce.** | These are the best parts of the system. |

### Typography

A six-step ramp tied to tokens, with a stylelint rule banning raw `font-size` outside `:root`:

| Token | Size / line | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--size-meta` | 12 / 16 | Captions, table headers, chips. **The floor for anything read.** |
| `--size-data` | 13 / 18 | Table cells, log rows |
| `--size-body` | 15 / 22 | Prose, ledes, answers |
| `--size-section` | 19 / 26 | Section questions |
| `--size-title` | 26 / 32 | Page title |
| `--size-hero` | 34 / 38 | The one figure that matters (focus deck's record), replay life totals at 28 |

Delete `.mono { font-size: 0.93em }`. Nothing on screen is under 12px: the replay's 8.5 to 10px tile text is replaced by the 16px ribbon and P/T badge. Give each page two or three `--ink-1` / `--ink-max` anchors; today 482 of 628 text nodes on the results page are ink-3 or ink-4.

### Spacing and density

- A 4px grid: `--sp-1..8` = 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64, linted.
- `.btns { display:flex; gap: var(--sp-2); flex-wrap: wrap }` globally, which fixes the touching buttons on `/rules`.
- Tables go denser: 36px rows, right-aligned tabular numbers under right-aligned headers, quiet 12px ink-3 headers (fixes `.telet` centred over left-aligned numbers). The saved space goes to the replay board, which needs size.
- Filters appear only when a list passes about 20 rows (an 8-row games table doesn't need a search box).

### Colour roles for data

| Role | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Interaction (links, focus ring, primary, playhead, selected) | Cyan `--mana-cyan` / `--mana-cyan-ink` |
| Live activity | Cyan + glow (the only glow) |
| Colour identity, mana | WUBRG painted pips and flat cost glyphs, never anything else |
| Seat identity | Commander art avatar + seat number + position. **No seat hues** (every hue collides with a mana colour); the timeline uses lanes instead of coloured lines |
| Observed facts | Ink ramp; filled marks |
| Modelled or inferred values | Hollow marks + the word "modelled" or "inferred" in the legend or chip |
| Pilot's notes | Register, not hue: "Pilot" label, italic, thin ink-3 left rule |
| Combat | Hue-free: lift + ink-max outline + arrows for attacks, dashed connectors for blocks |
| Warning thresholds (7+ poison, 15+ commander damage, sample too small) | A `--warn` token that is not a WUBRG hue, paired with the diamond shape and a word |
| Controls | New `--control-edge` ≥ 3:1 against the surface; `--hairline` for decorative dividers only |

Add `@media (forced-colors: active)` so the status shapes draw with borders (today they vanish in High Contrast mode). Stay dark-only until the type and spacing debt is paid.

## 8. Craft details that signal a player made this

1. **The commander is the deck's face.** An art-crop avatar beside every deck mention. Partner and background pairs as a split circle. An editable table name ("Squirrel Girl").
2. **"Turn 9" always means the table round,** explained once. Forge's T36 never appears. Median turns are never fractional.
3. **Mana costs drawn, never braced;** generic mana as a numeral disc. "Tax 4" drawn the same way.
4. **Commander badge** (crown, inline SVG) on the commander wherever it is, with "cast 2x · tax 4". **Commander damage** tracked per source against 21, and poison against 10, both visible on the plate.
5. **Life is the loudest number on a seat,** with a brief ±delta chip on change.
6. **Lands as "9 · 3 untapped".** Open mana is what players actually scan.
7. **A token tile designed by someone who plays:** big P/T, an upright name ribbon when tapped, a ×N count, the creature type underneath.
8. **"Entered this turn"** marks from the zone stream: a fact, not a summoning-sickness ruling.
9. **Elimination order strips** on game rows and the end card ("Krenko t9 poison · Stella t9 poison").
10. **Mulligan theatre:** "Mulliganed to 6: first seven had 1 land", with the kept hand fanned.
11. **The rotation grid**, deck by seat with win marks, so seat rotation is visible rather than only claimed.
12. **Bracket on every deck header and tile,** a Game Changer tag on those cards, and pod presets by bracket ("Bracket 3 field"). Since the 2025 bracket system, it is the first thing players ask about a list.
13. **"Watch Kess win on turn 9"**, not "Watch", deep-linked to the swing. **"Watch its fastest loss."**
14. **Numbers set with care:** true minus (−16 pts), whole percents under 30 games, a thin space before %, en dashes for empty values, right-aligned tabular numbers.
15. **Per-route titles:** "Game 1 · Kess vs Stella vs Squirrel Girl vs Krenko · Sim Lab". A favicon from the archivist's head.
16. **A docked card preview** that never covers what you are scanning, and a hover target on every card name in tables, log, combo lines and coaching.
17. **The paste box recognises Moxfield's "// Commander" and Arena's "Commander" headers,** and gives the exact export path when someone pastes a URL.
18. **Plain-English filter restatement,** the Scryfall habit: "6 of 43 decks have green in their colour identity".
19. **An outbound toolbox:** the commander on EDHREC, combos on Commander Spellbook, the original Moxfield or Archidekt URL, and Scryfall on every card name.
20. **The JVM warm-up line says what is true:** "Forge is loading its card database and shuffling four decks." Never a generic spinner.

| **One `/sims/[id]` page, two states** (running becomes the report in place), redirects from old routes | 3, 4 | [eng S] job→result mapping |
| **Kill-source attribution and win-method taxonomy** (Playgroup's seven: combat, non-combat damage, combo, commander damage, poison, mill, alternative) in `analysis.py`, so "How" and the human comparison line up | 1, 10 | [eng M] |
| **Model honesty:** range widened with sample size, explanation surfaced, basis stated, suppression below 12 decided games | 8 | [eng M] `predict.py` |
| **Elimination timestamps** from the shim; permanents leave when Forge says so | 2 | [eng S-M] shim release (GPL repo, thin adapter) |
| **Playtest to baseline:** per-card action menu, keyboard map, search library, top-N, shuffle, undo, named tokens from `all_parts`, playmat layout, confirm on reset, 44px targets | 15 | [eng S] `all_parts` in the `cards.py` cache |
| **Coaching relaunch:** context from combo lines, comparison figures and prediction; quote-the-number rule; "Who beat you"; card previews | 10 | [owner] `MTG_LLM_API_KEY`; [eng M] `coach.py` |
| **Rules search:** golden set of 20 Commander questions, 903/704 boosting, sentence-boundary excerpts, section chips | below the line | [eng M] rules KB retrieval |

### What not to do

- **No 0-100 power score, letter grade or one-decimal composite.** Grim.Cards shows "97.3 · 1 sim"; honesty is Sim Lab's edge.
- **No gameplay creep.** No opponent, adjudication or declared outcome in Playtest, and no "you would have won" in replays. Watching and goldfishing only.
- **No combo, payoff or card-role classification from oracle text.** Use Spellbook's results and families; Scryfall is for display typing only.
- **Don't replace the log with the board,** and don't upgrade stdout boards to "exact". The provenance chip stays.
- **No seat hues and no rainbow timeline.** Lanes, avatars and positions carry seat identity.
- **Don't make follow-active reflow the desktop default.** Stable geometry, focus on demand.
- **No sub-rotation game counts,** and never a single-seat rate.
- **No LLM-written ledes or headings.** Computed prose stays deterministic.
- **No server-rendered share images containing card art** (that would rehost Scryfall images). Let users screenshot the end card.
- **No count-ups, entrance animations or bounce hovers.** Motion only on change: life deltas, the stack fade.
- **No new disclaimer paragraphs.** Move caveats next to their numbers.
- **No light theme yet,** and no four-layout switcher (Untap.in's cost).
- **Nothing clever in the shim.** Pilot's notes cross the boundary as data; translation lives in our code.

---

## 10. Design principles for every future screen

1. **Name it the way it's said at the table.** Commander names and art for decks, "turn N" as players count it, combos by what they produce. No engine token, filename, id, env var or brace ever renders.
2. **The user's deck is the subject.** Every analysis screen defaults to the focus deck and answers its three questions (how good, why, what to change) before anything about the pod.
3. **Every number states its denominator, its comparison and its range.** Decided games, the even share and archetype baseline, and an interval. When n is too small, say it once and dim the figure; never score a plan you haven't identified.
4. **Every statistic links to the game that shows it.** A kill source filters the games, a game opens at its swing, a combo line jumps to the turn it came together. The replay is the evidence.
5. **Show the game first; the log stays one click away and authoritative.** Pace by importance, navigate by turns and plays, never make anyone step through bookkeeping.
6. **Facts in ink, inference labelled.** Observed values are filled; modelled values are hollow and say "modelled"; the pilot's reasons say "Pilot's note" and never judge.
7. **Collapse what is the same; fold what didn't happen.** Variants into families, repeated lines into counts, never-assembled lines into "N more". If deleting an element loses no information, delete it (law 5).
8. **Art is ceremony, data is paper.** Fantasy art only where nothing is read; opaque ground under every table, log and board. Glow means live and nothing else. A colour means one thing, and WUBRG means mana.
9. **Judgement over rules for broken states.** A dark feature disappears from players; a missing value is an en dash with a reason; a design-system rule never justifies a control that can't work.
10. **Choose, don't converge.** Every type, colour and layout choice needs a reason tied to Commander players. If a choice is what a generator would make with no brief, make it again.

critiques.verdict: I'd sign off on the mechanics but not on the draft as written. Keep the possessive-name parse fix, decided-games maths, folding the Spellbook variants, the stack spotlight, clickable log and turn/play navigation, and hiding dark features. The draft's own worked example is wrong, though, and a player would catch it immediately. I rechecked game 1 of sim_20260925_003803 against the game payload. The game was decided on round 8 (T30), when Ezuri's Predation killed every opposing creature, including all three enemy commanders, and left Skrat's with about 12 Beasts. Kess then died on round 10 (T36) to 45 ordinary combat damage ("life total reached 0"), not to poison. So the draft's lede, end card and game row are wrong, and its life/poison "swing" definition would still send people to round 9. It also treats "win conditions" as a table-formatting problem. It is really a modelling problem: the deck's actual finishers (Craterhoof, Triumph, Predation) never appear, and the same Spellbook list steers the AI pilot into bad plays. Would I use this weekly? No. I would use it every time I change a deck, but only if the results page tells me what to cut and how my finishers performed, and lets me sim against my own group's lists and add games to an existing sim.
strongest_objections: The draft gets its own central example wrong. Game 1 (Skrat's Revenge wins) turned on T30, round 8: Skrat's cast Ezuri's Predation, every opposing creature fought a 4/4 Beast, Kess, Stella Lee and Krenko all went to the graveyard, and about 12 Beasts stayed on the table. Triumph of the Hordes on T34 was the follow-through: 15 attackers, Krenko to 46 poison, Stella to 19. On T36 Kess took 45 from 15 non-infect attackers at 35 life. The game log says 'Kess, Reanimator has lost because life total reached 0'. So 'Squirrel Girl won with poison', the end card line 'Kess: turn 10, poison' and the story row '(K) t10 poison' are all wrong. In a pod every knockout has its own cause and its own killer.

The swing is defined as a life/poison swing, and the timeline is modelled on lichess life lines. In Commander, life lags the board. Stella sat at 35 life and Krenko at 18 through the Predation turn, so the lanes would be flat exactly when the game turned. 'Watch the swing' would open on round 9 and skip the play that decided the game. Key moments need to come from the board: total power and permanents per seat from the shim zones stream, mass Battlefield→Graveyard moves, and token bursts.

The Highlights tiers are built around combat. Cast, resolve and trigger are tier 1, which Highlights skips, yet Commander games turn on the stack. On T26, Skrat's cast Triumph, Kess answered with Negate, and Hullbreaker's trigger bounced Triumph back to hand (Negate fizzled). On T33, Kess cast Bedevil on a Beast and Stella Counterspelled it, with a Thousand-Year Storm trigger. Stella's counter left no counter_fire agent event, so relying on agent_events misses it. Detect a spell targeting a spell from the log's 'cast X targeting [<spell text>]', plus tutors, reanimation (Exhume at T35, Graveyard→Battlefield) and wipes. Rank by impact, not by event type.

The draft's combo rebuild stays inside Commander Spellbook. The playtester's complaint was that these aren't his win conditions. Skrat's real finishers are Craterhoof Behemoth, Triumph of the Hordes and Ezuri's Predation, fetched with Finale of Devastation. In the 8 games Craterhoof was never cast, Triumph was cast only in game 1 (twice), and Predation in games 1, 3 and 8. The draft shows none of this and bans card-role classification from oracle text, yet engine/deck_plan.py:124 already does exactly that (the _FINISHER regex) for the pilot. Recording that a tagged card was cast, on what turn, and whether that game was won is a fact, not rules adjudication. Let owners tag win conditions (Archidekt already has a 'Win Condition' category; Moxfield has tags), pre-fill from deck_plan, and report per card.

The combo list isn't only a presentation problem, because it steers the pilot. deck_plan.py:323 gives every Spellbook piece a weight of 8. In game 1 on T21, Kess cast Unmarked Grave (dest=Graveyard) and put Sol Ring in the yard over Blasphemous Act (tutor_steer steer=Sol Ring over=Blasphemous Act). With Kess on the battlefield, Act in the yard is castable from there; binning Sol Ring is a joke play. The combo taxonomy fix has to feed deck_plan too. Also, Forge's AI does not run infinite loops, so the draft's 'won with it' will read 0 forever and look like a verdict that the combo is bad. The honest measure is 'pieces together, with mana up', plus a plain statement that the AI doesn't loop.

Pilot's notes will surface AI misplays, and the draft has no plan for that. The translation table also has errors. 'Kess searched for Hullbreaker Horror' drops the fact that it went into the GRAVEYARD, which is the whole point of a reanimator tutor. The 'moved=2 onto=Skrat's Revenge' row is Krenko's re-aim on T20, not Stella's. Real notes would include:
- On T33 Hullbreaker bounced itself while 10 or more Beast tokens were legal targets.
- On T29 Krenko skipped a block because of a random 'blockiness-roll'.
- On the final turn the rubric says 'declined 15 legal blocks' when Kess, at 35 life with one blocker, faced 49 power and was dead regardless.
These notes need a 'Flag this play' button, a one-time explanation that the AI is deliberately humanized with randomness, and a check that suppresses block notes when lethal was unavoidable.

The biggest trust signal is missing: are these games realistic? Median win rounds are 14–26 (Kambal 26 in sim_20260907, Kess 17 here). 15 of 16 and 16 of 16 games end 'combat damage / life loss', including Nekusar, a punisher deck. A regular Commander player sees turn-17 wins and all-combat endings and concludes 'this isn't my table'. SIM_CALIBRATION.md:49 says the AI turns creatures into wins and cannot run setup-then-payoff plans. The results page should lead with what the sim can and cannot tell you, not put it in a footnote.

Don't replace the owner's deck name with the commander name. Moxfield and Archidekt lead with the deck name and show the commander as art. The actual bug is shortName keeping the first whitespace token and its comma ('Kess,', 'Skrat's'). The comma-cut rule also collides on Krenko, Mob Boss vs Krenko, Tin Street Kingpin and on two Atraxas, and it fails for partners and backgrounds. Commander names are right for the pod title, because that's how people describe a pod. The owner's deck keeps 'Skrat's Revenge'.

The draft puts archetype-baseline ticks on every row, but SIM_CALIBRATION.md:52-58 says the 38%/12% baselines were measured before the clock fix and must be re-measured 'before they are shown to a user as a threshold'. The draft ships them anyway.
missing:
Table politics, built from data that already exists:
- Attackers faced per seat (Skrat's 129, Krenko 121, Kess 94, Stella 70 in the scorecards).
- A kill-credit matrix: who knocked out whom.
- Leader re-aims: in game 1 the pilots re-aimed attacks onto Skrat's three times.
'The table treated your deck as the archenemy' is the most Commander-native insight available, and the draft never states it.

Causes per knockout. The app gives each game one method (game 1 = 'poison'); a pod needs a cause and a killer for every knockout. The damage lines already say 'combat damage' vs 'non-combat damage' and '(as poison counters)', so this is a small parse, not a medium engine job.

Commander tracking:
- Cast turn against mana value: Kess and Krenko, both 4-drops, came down in rounds 5–6.
- Times cast and tax paid.
- Where the commander went when it died: in game 1 all three commanders went Battlefield→Graveyard and never to the Command zone.
- Games where the commander was never cast: Squirrel Girl never came down in game 1 and the deck won anyway.

Stranded and dead cards. Shim hands are exact, so the app can list cards drawn but never cast and cards that sat in hand N or more turns (for example, Craterhoof never cast). This is the deterministic answer to 'what should I cut'. The draft only reaches 'what to change' through coaching, which is dark.
Tutor targets: what Finale of Devastation and Unmarked Grave actually fetched (from search_seen), with the destination (hand, battlefield or graveyard) stated.

Open mana by colour on other players' turns ('Stella: 2 Islands up') so viewers can read counter windows. Also an acting-player badge separate from the active-turn frame, for off-turn plays like Chaos Warp during Skrat's declare attackers or Stella's Comet Storm. The draft cites poker action badges but never specs one.
A hands-revealed toggle (the stream-style god view). On shim runs, seeing Stella holding Counterspell is what makes a game watchable.

The free mulligan. Forge logs 'mulliganed down to 7 cards' for it, so 'kept seven 63%' blurs 'kept the opening 7' with 'took the free mulligan'. The mulligan theatre should say 'took the free mulligan, then went to 6'.

When a player is out, their permanents leave the game (rule 800.4a). A seat with lethal poison should grey out and clear immediately, dated using Forge's own end-of-game loss cause. A 'Lethal poison (46)' badge on a seat that keeps sitting there for 95 events reads as broken.
'Run 8 more games' to extend the same pod and pool the results. That grows the sample, which is what builds trust, and it is the natural weekly habit.

A bracket badge on every deck and a pod-balance warning on the results page. Kess Reanimator with Hullbreaker and Exhume against Krenko Goblins may simply be a mismatch, which explains 4-of-7 vs 0-of-7 better than any interval.
Game length against human games, for example 'median win on round 17; human bracket-3 pods usually finish by around 9–10', ideally sourced from the model's human dataset.

Sorts for choosing a good game to watch: your deck's win, its fastest loss, the closest finish (three players alive going into the last round), counter wars, board wipes, comebacks. 'Biggest swing' by life total is the wrong sort.

A stale honesty note. On shim 0.15.0 runs the combo section still says 'Assembly is inferred from board reconstruction (83-86% exit-match)', which contradicts the replay's 'read exactly' note. The draft doesn't catch it.
