wrong_or_generic: 'Watch the swing' / 'the swing came on turn 9'. In Magic slang a swing is an attack ('swing for 45'), so this reads as 'watch the attack'. Say 'the turning point' or 'the turn that decided it', and point it at Predation, not Triumph.
The story row and end card list 'Kess: turn 10, poison'. Wrong: combat damage from 15 Beasts.
The pilot's-note table: 'Kess searched for Hullbreaker Horror over Blasphemous Act' (it went into the graveyard via Unmarked Grave), and 'Stella moved 2 attackers' (that re-aim was Krenko's, on T20).

'Declined 15 legal blocks, took 12' on the defender's plate. On that turn Kess was dead on board (49 power incoming, 35 life, 1 blocker), so the note is noise that makes the product look like it doesn't understand combat.

Hullbreaker + Sol Ring labelled 'Engine, needs a payoff; none in this 99' and 'Kess won that game in combat, not with this line'. A Kess player knows a Hullbreaker loop is a bounce lock that clears the table, after which you win in combat. Spellbook's produces list ('Infinite colorless mana, Infinite storm count') leaves out the derived bounce, so a band table built only on Spellbook features will misfile known lines. It needs curated overrides or owner confirmation.

A lane timeline with life lines and a five-glyph vocabulary (◆▲◼◇×), borrowed from lichess and League of Legends. Life totals are flat in Commander until a sudden kill, so plot board power or permanent count per seat.

Question headings in all caps ('HOW DID SQUIRREL GIRL DO?', 'DID THE MANA WORK?') break the draft's own sentence-case rule, and FAQ-style question headings are a template tell in their own right. Short labels read as human: Record, Knockouts, Mana, Win cons, Games.
'Even share' and 'Leader vs even share' are statistician's words. Players say '25% is average in a 4-pod'. Write '4 of 7 (average is 25%)'.

Swapping to IBM Plex as the anti-slop move. Plex and Inter are as much generator defaults as Space Grotesk. Players won't feel the font; they'll feel Kess's poison error, 'Kess,' in the h1 and 'revenge's main phase'. Fix correctness first.
Hue-free combat and retiring red for attackers. This is purity over clarity: Arena shows attackers with a strong cue, and no player reads a red attack arrow as red mana.
'The archivist's notes' as a mascot byline, and 'Your deck hasn't sat down at a table yet'. Twee copy is its own kind of generated feel.

Section 4.14's 'where each choice comes from', citing 11 products. It reads like a research dump. What makes a replay feel made by a player is Commander-specific: commander zone and tax, open mana, counter wars, archenemy, per-knockout causes.
feasibility_risks:
Scope. The plan has 15 problems, about 13 quick wins, 11 medium and 8 large items, for one owner. Only the correctness items are true priorities:
- The possessive parse. Confirmed live: 'Round 8 · revenge's main phase, precombat'.
- Cause per knockout.
- The pilot's combo weights.
- Name truncation.
- NaN and 'Draw (draw)'.
- The duration estimate.
The visual-language migration can wait.

Board-based key-moment detection needs total power per seat from the shim zones data. That exists only on shim runs, so older stdout runs need a fallback (mass exits and token bursts from the log) labelled as inferred.

Mapping Spellbook features to bands. The feature vocabulary is large, derived effects are missing, and the draft's default of 'Engine' for anything unknown will misfile lines. Because Forge never executes loops, the 'won with it' stat will stay at 0 and read as a verdict against the combo.

Pilot's notes shipped before the pilot is fixed will put the Sol Ring entomb, Hullbreaker bouncing itself and blockiness-roll skips in front of players and investors. Ship them together with a 'flag this play' loop, and fix deck_plan's combo-piece weights first.

Archetype baselines can't be shown as thresholds until someone re-measures them after the clock fix (SIM_CALIBRATION.md:52-58). CLAUDE.md and SIM_CALIBRATION currently pull in opposite directions here.
Owner-declared win conditions, the 'your deck' focus and deck versioning all assume an owner. There is no identity yet (task 06), so these items depend on auth work the draft doesn't list.
Dating each knockout: the final loss lines are enough for an interim fix. Recording the exact moment needs a shim release in the separate GPL repo, which must stay a thin adapter.

Using commander names as identity collides (two Krenkos, two Atraxas) and gets complicated for partners and backgrounds. It needs the engine to publish commanders in the results index and game payload first.
A 40–105 minute run means 'you can close this tab' alone won't bring people back. The weekly loop needs a done notification, and that is a new outbound-message surface with its own consent handling.
keep: Parse phase lines against known player keys, longest first, with a 'Skrat's Revenge' fixture. Possessive deck names are the Commander norm.
Decided games as the single denominator, Wilson intervals, whole percents under 30 games, hiding the model's estimate below 12 decided games, and no 0–100 power score.

Fold Spellbook variants into families (28 Squirrel Girl rows become 1), give commander-only lines their own band so 'assembled' never just means 'commander on the battlefield', and link out to Spellbook without re-explaining the steps.
Stack spotlight with 'Cast by' and the parsed target, and a numbered stack list.
Lands collapsed to 'Lands 9 · 3 untapped'. Open mana is what players scan (extend it with colours).
Clickable log rows, navigation by turn and by play, a real slider scrubber, a keyboard map, and a deep link per moment.
An end card with knockout order (with correct causes) and the killing card, plus a clear explanation for clock-cut draws.
A turn-by-turn mode with computed per-turn summaries. This is the Game Knights-style recap people actually want.
Mulligan theatre with the kept hand fanned (exact on shim runs), a rotation grid with win marks, and games as story cards linking to the key turn.
Pilot's notes as the differentiator, always worded as the AI's stated reason, never labelled right or wrong. Keep them, with the caveats above.
Hide Coaching and Ask while the LLM is off, and remove operator copy (env vars, shell commands) from player views.
Commander art avatars beside every deck mention, and CardPreview on every card name.
Stable desktop seat geometry with turn order running clockwise, focus on demand, and a one-seat follow-active view on mobile.
The 'What not to do' list, especially: no gameplay creep, no LLM-written ledes, no share images that rehost Scryfall art, and no upgrading stdout boards to 'exact'.

critiques.verdict:
I'd sign off on the thesis and the honesty stance: a Commander player's write-up of pod night, in table language, with every claim linked to a game. I would not sign off on this document as the plan. It is a well-sorted pile: 15 problems, about 35 roadmap items, 20 craft details and 10 principles, but nothing picks the smallest set that changes how the app feels, and the owner's actual complaint (jank, AI slop) sits at #14. Four of its claims are wrong or contradict each other when checked against the data:
- Deep links already work: every event carries `seq` on both paths.
- The type and spacing tokens it proposes already exist.
- The 'lethal poison' badge is exactly the kind of rules inference it rejects for summoning sickness.
- Its combo bands have no home for Lock.
The replay theatre also skips a prerequisite. On shim runs the board is only accurate per phase, not per event. Rewrite it as a feel-first phase 1 (about 7 changes, CSS plus formatters plus two small engine fields). Then re-test with the playtester who complained. Only then build the L items: theatre, interval chart, Pilot's notes, deck hub.
strongest_objections: It is ranked by bug severity, not by what makes the app feel careless. The biggest 'feel' lever is buried as #14 and gated on owner approval, yet it is almost free. Every route renders its whole content inside ONE translucent sheet: `.page` in globals.css:326-335 uses --panel-glass at 0.85 alpha plus backdrop-filter blur, over a 2.65 MB PNG mounted for every route in layout.tsx. Make `.page` opaque on reading routes and mount the backdrop only on home, empty and running screens. Drop text-transform and glow from `.action-btn` (globals.css:400-415). That is a CSS change of under 20 lines, and it changes the feel of every page in one commit. It belongs at the top of the quick wins, not in a 'Medium: type, spacing and palette migration [owner]' row.

The replay spec assumes the shim board is exact at every event. It is exact only per phase. `replay.ts` `atPlayhead()` and `battlefieldAt()` (around lines 575-670) apply zone, tap and counter records per phase, because the adapter keeps no ordering between log entries and shim records. So when you step cast by cast through a 20-event Main 1, the permanents are already on the table from the phase's first event. The proposed 'In focus' stack spotlight would show a spell being cast that is already on the battlefield, and 'Entered this turn' and Highlights beats inherit the error. The fix is cheap and missing from §4.13. shim_raw_*.jsonl already interleaves entry, zone, tap and agent records in emission order (one stream, parsed line by line in `shim_log_adapter.parse_shim_jsonl`), so the adapter can stamp every non-entry record with the seq of the preceding entry, followed by a readapt. That is engine S, it must land before the theatre, and it should be measured: how often does a card appear before its cast line, before and after.

Pilot's notes are treated as a clean differentiator. The data says otherwise. Game 1's agent_events include `block_skip blockiness-roll`: a personality dice roll from `deck_plan.py` 'blockiness', which means the AI randomly chose not to block. They also include diagnostics like `search_seen sid=1 options=80 ranked=20 agree=false pickedW=6 planW=8` and 8 `instant_hold` passes in one game. Caption a dice roll as the pilot's 'reason' and the expert concludes the sim is arbitrary. 'Kess let Crackle with Power resolve (threat judged too low)' reads as a blunder whenever Crackle kills someone. The owner's own finding is that the agent does not win more than stock AI, so surfacing its reasoning by default in the Highlights caption (B') exposes the weakest part of the model to both audiences. Use a whitelist of translated codes (finisher_hold, kingmaker_reaim, tutor_steer, counter_fire/veto, mulligans), off by default in Highlights and on in study mode. Never show an 'unrecognised note' fallback to players. Also, agent_events carry only {turn, player, event, detail}, with no phase or seq, so 'inline at the relevant beat' can only be anchored by turn plus a card-name match until the seq stamping above exists.

The interval chart is honest, and at the default run size it communicates nothing. On the playtester's 8-game run every Wilson range spans the 25% even share except Kess's (25-84%, touching it). Each row would carry 5 encodings: sim dot, hollow model dot, even-share rule, archetype tick, floor tag. The draft then makes the focus deck's record the page's one 'hero' figure while admitting it is noise. Its fix line, 'about 32 separate decks with confidence', is garbled, and the maths is wrong: 32 decided games per deck still gives about ±15 points. The honest product move is to lead the report with the metrics that 8 games do power, because they are counted over turns and attackers rather than games: land drops over about 80 turns, 94 attackers faced, commander cast turn, kept-hand lands. Demote the win rate to 'first look', and pool across sims of the same deck (task 17). The draft never faces that at 8 games the headline number can't carry the report.

'Your deck', 'Your decks first' and 'Your latest sim' assume identity the product doesn't have. There are no accounts (task 06 is blocked on task 04 Postgres), reads are public, and one instance serves several playtesters. The IA (§3.4) and home spec are unbuildable as written. Name the interim: a focus slot recorded on the job (engine S), plus a per-browser 'imported here' list in localStorage wrapped in try/catch. Say so on the page ('decks imported in this browser').

The 'Lethal poison (46)' seat badge and 'the swing = took the last opponent from alive to lethal' both have the app deciding a player has lost from a counter value. That is rule 704.5c applied by our code; Platinum Angel-style effects exist. It contradicts the draft's own refusal to show 'summoning sick' as a rules inference, and CLAUDE.md's 'Don't reimplement Magic'. Show '46 poison' with the warn shape and no verdict word. Get eliminations from the shim (engine S-M). Define the deciding moment from logged life and poison totals, without the word 'lethal'.

The draft doesn't reconcile with the owner's own backlog, which CLAUDE.md says to start from. tasks/13 (fetch Moxfield and Archidekt links directly) is contradicted by 'detect URLs and explain the export path'. tasks/14 (commander damage), tasks/17 (deck history page) and tasks/19 (zone rail; hands shipped, graveyard/exile/library not) are re-specified without being cited. The owner will get two competing specs for the same four features.
missing: A validation gate. Before any L item, run the redesigned phase 1 with the playtester who complained plus 2 or 3 Commander players, on scripted tasks: 'How did your deck do?', 'Why did it lose game 3?', 'Find the turn Skrat's won'. Measure time-to-answer and misreads before and after. Human-centred design without a test loop is just taste.

Instrumentation. The app has no usage analytics, so nobody knows whether replays get opened, past which step people give up, or whether anyone scrolls to the combo section. At least log replay opens, max step reached and 'Watch the swing' clicks server-side. Otherwise the Highlights and pacing work can't be judged.

An explicit engine prerequisite list, ordered ahead of UI work: (1) stamp shim records with the preceding entry's seq; (2) commander names from `.dck` [Commander] into the results index and game payload; (3) keep Spellbook `of`/`requires` in `_slim()`. The draft scatters these across four tables.

Log grammar for repeated combat damage. At the game-1 kill the log is a wall of 'Phyrexian Beast Token (979) deals 5 combat damage to Krenko Goblins (as poison counters)', one row per token. The draft collapses 'didn't block' runs but not damage runs, which are the bigger flood. Target: '10 Phyrexian Beast Tokens: 50 poison to Krenko (now 46)'.

Correct the stable-links claim. `seq` already exists on every event on both paths: the fixture has `{'seq': 52, ...}` and the live shim payload has seq 90+. So `?seq=` deep links are UI-only today. The real stability risk is only that readapt renumbers seq (the fixture went from 2,874 to 2,975 events), which a link-migration note covers.

The type and spacing tokens already exist: --size-meta 12, --size-data 13, --size-body 15, --size-h2 19, --size-h1 34, and --sp-1..9 on a 4px base in arcane-sim-lab.tokens.css. The debt is adoption: 141 font-size declarations, 2 using tokens, and 31 at 12.5px, 23 at 12px, 18 at 13px, 9 at 13.5px and 8 at 11.5px. The draft re-specifies a 'new' ramp with new names, which is churn. Map the raw sizes onto the existing tokens, add one 26px title step, then lint.

A fifth combo band. Lock is 543 of 5,582 cached variants, and 'Infinite turns' (310) and 'Infinite combat phases' (218) are neither finishers nor engines needing a payoff. With 343 distinct feature names in engine/combo_cache.json, the mapping table is a real maintenance surface. Say who owns it.

The waiting experience. A sim is 40 to 105 minutes and there are no accounts, so no email. 'You can close this tab' needs a way back: a per-browser 'my running sims' list, an optional browser Notification API prompt, and the running page as the one place the art and live playback (/sim-live already exists) earn their keep.

The archetype baselines' age. engine/archetype.py baselines were measured under STOCK Forge in July 2026, and the plan agent is now the default. Adding a baseline tick per row without re-measuring or labelling ('stock-AI baseline') trades one honesty gap for another. The overview currently shows only the even share, which is itself a CLAUDE.md violation the draft underplays.
A first-run state for a brand-new playtester, who has no decks of their own and sees 43 gallery tiles, dev variants included.
wrong_or_generic: 'Watch the swing'. In table slang 'swing' means attack ('swing at Krenko'). For a drain, combo or poison-by-spell ending it misleads. Use 'Watch the winning turn' or 'Watch how it ended'. That is table language that holds for every win method.

Replacing Space Grotesk with IBM Plex Sans is swapping one convergent 'engineered tech' face for another: Plex is IBM Carbon's default and a stock dev-tool choice. The measured problem is mono carrying 48% of the text and five sizes crammed between 11.5 and 13.5px, not the family. Fix usage first. The swap is cheap in code (one next/font import in layout.tsx), but it is the least evidenced recommendation and shouldn't gate the type work behind an owner decision.

Art-crop tiles at 96x70, shrinking to 56px, as the legibility fix. The 420x280 seat budget fits one row of four 96px creatures. Skrat's winning board (10 Beasts plus Squirrels plus others) trips '+N / seat focus' in every token game, and a 56px tile with a 16px ribbon holds about 7 characters: no more legible than today's 46px `.tc`. Token art also needs ambiguous Scryfall token lookups. The better default seat body is a text row per permanent group ('Phyrexian Beast Token 4/4 ×10 · 3 tapped') with a small art thumb, and the full image only in the docked preview.

Timeline 'combo line came together' glyphs read `/analysis` assembly, the same inference that counts Stella Lee alone as assembled 8 of 8. Shipping that glyph before the combo rebuild spreads the discredited signal into the replay.

§4.14's eleven-source citation list (League of Legends Annotated Timeline, poker replayers, Mystmin...) and §8's 20 'craft details' read as breadth for its own sake. Justification by precedent is itself a generated-document tell. Keep the 5 craft details that change a real screen: lands as '9 · 3 untapped', commander avatar plus short name, true minus and whole percents, no T36, drawn mana costs.
Principle 10 ('Choose, don't converge') and the 10-principle list are meta-advice. They don't tell the builder what to do on Monday.
The document puts §7 before §6 with a parenthetical apology, and says '§5' where it means '§3'. A synthesis that says 'a human took care' should not ship with its own seams showing.
Life lanes 'scaled 0 to the starting 40'. Kambal Taxes sat at 50 life in the same sims. Scale each lane to the game's maximum.

Rubric 'Declined 15 legal blocks, took 12' on the defender's plate. The rubric is a neutral observer's quality score, so putting it on the plate mid-replay frames the play as a misplay even with neutral wording. Keep it in study mode or the scorecard.
feasibility_risks: Full-bleed theatre inside the current shell. The replay lives inside `.page` (max-width 1280, 36px/40px padding, glass). Fitting 100dvh needs a layout escape (a `.page--theatre` variant or no shell) and a sticky transport. The 808px budget leaves almost no slack at 1366x768, the most common laptop resolution, where 768 minus browser chrome is about 650px.
Highlights mode and the In Focus stack card can't be trusted on shim runs until records are stamped with seq (see objections). Without that, main-phase beats show resolved permanents.

The combo rebuild needs a Spellbook cache refresh for the 102 cached decklists and a hand-maintained band map over 343 feature names. Both are engine M, and the map drifts as Spellbook adds features. Ship the client-side stopgap first: fold by identical `produces` plus all-but-one shared cards, rename the section, delete 'AI can fire this'. `_slim()` already keeps `description` and `prerequisites`, so 'show Spellbook's steps on expand' is buildable now, without the refresh.

Commander names in the payload are a dependency for about 8 recommendations (titles, seats, avatars, commander damage, ◆ glyphs, table names). If that engine S slips, most of phase 1 slips. Do it first, and cover it in the runs index and in old results via readapt.

The focus deck, 'same pod as last time' and the change-sim-compare loop need deck versioning and sims indexed by deck. Without accounts or Postgres (tasks 04 and 06), 'owner' is undefined on a shared instance.

Solo developer bandwidth. The quick-wins table alone is 13 items touching the engine, format.ts, replay.ts, four pages and the design system. Realistically that is 2 to 3 weeks, not 'days'. The M and L lists are several months of work. Without a cut line the owner will build the interesting parts (theatre, Pilot's notes) and ship none of the credibility fixes.

Deleting the design system's home §5-6 and retiring violet are owner decisions against a spec labelled BINDING. Package them as one small, reversible DS amendment with before/after screenshots, not scattered through the roadmap.
keep: The thesis and the ordering principle: verdict, then why, then evidence, then raw, with every statistic one click from the game that shows it.

Problem 2, the possessive-name phase parse (`replay.ts:245`, lazy `^(.+?)'s`). It is real (live header reads 'Round 9 · revenge's combat damage'), S-sized, hits most imported Commander decks, and falsifies a board the page labels exact. Fix it first, with a 'Skrat's Revenge' fixture and the board.py regression check.

Problem 3, the estimate. Delete the client SECONDS_PER_GAME table (format.ts:118) in favour of the engine's estimate, offer whole rotations only, and put the played count on the button. This is the only number shown before an hour-long job.

Problem 7, commander short names plus art-crop avatars from the .dck [Commander] section, never guessed from the deck name. 'Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko' is the most-read string in the product.

Problem 10's purge of machine strings (NaN:NaN, T36/T57, 'Draw (draw)', env vars, ENGINE_CMD, 'event 846 of 980'), and hiding Coaching and Ask when `health.llm` is false. 'Never disable the primary' should not justify a button the page admits will fail.

The combo stopgap: rename the section, show `produces` as visible chips, delete 'AI can fire this; results meaningful', and fold never-assembled rows under 'N more lines never came together'. Also 'won that game' versus 'won with it' as the only language that can imply a line fired.

Replay pacing tiers that skip phase markers and mana taps in playback (about 60% of steps), clickable log rows that seek, a real slider scrubber, `?seq=` links (buildable today), and `useCardPreview` on replay tiles.
Clockwise stable seating with focus on demand rather than follow-active reflow on desktop.
Decided games as the single denominator everywhere. Delete the headline stat strip and the 'survived to the end' tautology.
Status shapes for job state only, never for deck outcomes. On the live report Skrat's '1 of 7' currently renders with the hollow 'queued' circle.
The 'What not to do' list, especially: no power score, no LLM-written ledes, no share images rehosting card art, no count-ups, no gameplay creep in Playtest.

The smallest set that would change how it feels, as phase 1: (1) opaque paper for reading routes, backdrop only where nothing is read, buttons in sentence case with no glow; (2) commander names plus avatars everywhere; (3) the machine-string purge plus the phase-parse fix; (4) the combo fold stopgap; (5) replay fits one viewport with a sticky transport, skips bookkeeping steps, clickable log, card preview, collapsed damage runs; (6) home as a computed lede, one primary, recent sims with avatars, honest duration; (7) raw font sizes mapped onto the existing tokens and mono removed from prose.

walkthroughs.first_impression: The art is lovely and the brass robot has charm, but after 10 seconds I still can't tell what the product does. The first screen is a logo, four vanity counters ("3,152 rules loaded", "43 decks on this engine"), a chatbot line ("What would you like to do today?") and four equally loud neon buttons. Nothing says "paste your Commander list and we'll play it against a pod a few dozen times and show you why it wins or loses", which is the one sentence that would make me stay. The recent-sims list then shows "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal" with a "winner" at 25%, which any 4-player regular reads as broken. Decks opens onto 43 tiles of someone's test builds (seven Inspirits, eight Kilos), and a deck page runs ten screens of oracle text with raw "{1}{G}{G}{G}" costs, the opposite of what Moxfield has trained me to expect. The honesty underneath (seat rotation, validity flags, baselines in the report) is impressive, and the front door hides it.

findings.where: /new rail estimate and mobile runbar (web/app/new/page.tsx:258-269, 295), home hub note (web/app/page.tsx:283), source constants web/lib/format.ts:118-124 (SECONDS_PER_GAME {4: 52}); also baked into Design System/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:251
findings.what_happens: I seated Skrat's Revenge, Kess, Krenko and Stella at 16 games, and the rail said "about 14 min". Home says "four decks ≈ 8 min for 16". The engine's own record for the latest 4-deck, 8-game job (/engine/sim-status, id 9212fe0f3a11) shows elapsed 3,356 s (55 min 56 s), and its server-side typical_seconds is [1292, 3212] (21 to 54 min) for 8 games. CLAUDE.md puts a 4-deck, 16-game run at 40 to 105 min. /new's formula gives 7 min for that 8-game job, so the estimate is 4 to 8x too low. After you click Run, /runs/[id] switches to the server range, so you get two different durations one click apart.
findings.why_it_hurts: This number is the whole cost of the run, shown right before you commit to an hour-long JVM job. When it's wrong, people conclude the run has hung and re-queue it, which the engine's own comments say slows both copies. It breaks Nielsen's 'match between system and real world' and the error-prevention heuristic, and it breaks trust at the most expensive moment in the product.
findings.recommendation: Delete the client-side estimateSeconds table. Expose the engine's estimate_sim_seconds (for example GET /estimate?decks=4&games=16, or fold it into /health) and show the same range /runs uses: "Usually 40 to 105 min. You can close this tab; the run keeps going and lands in Results." Remove the hardcoded hub-est line from home (and from DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §6), or compute it from the same source.

findings.where: /new games select and primary button (web/app/new/page.tsx:115-128, 250, 267, 202); engine rounding in engine/mtg_engine.py:474-476
findings.what_happens: The button always says "Run 16 games" (whatever you requested), but the engine rounds up to a multiple of the seat count: 3 decks at 16 plays 18, and 4 decks at 1 plays 4. The "1 game" option adds ", so you can watch this one play out", which is false for a 3 or 4 deck pod: it plays 3 or 4 games and takes tens of minutes. The empty rail says "Seat order is the order you pick", and tiles get P1 to P4 chips, but every run is seat-rotated, so pick order doesn't matter.
findings.why_it_hurts: CLAUDE.md: "Any surface that shows a game count shows the played number and says why." Offering 1 and 2 games for a 4-deck pod invites exactly the single-seat result the calibration rules forbid. Implying seat order matters teaches a wrong mental model of the product's main honesty feature.
findings.recommendation: Phrase the options in seat-rotation terms, computed per pod: "4 games (each deck on the play once)", "8 (twice)", "16 (four times)"; drop anything below one full rotation. Show the played count on the button. Replace "Seat order is the order you pick" with "Every deck takes every seat, so order doesn't matter." Keep P1 to P4 only as selection order, or drop them.

findings.where: Home / above the fold (web/app/page.tsx:216-248, 252-283)
findings.what_happens: At 1440x900 and at 375x812, the first screen is the mascot, the wordmark, four rolling counters ("43 decks on this engine · 317 games simulated · 46 finished runs · 3,152 rules loaded"), "What would you like to do today?", and four all-caps glowing buttons: Run new simulation, Sim history & analytics, Import deck, Explore decks. No sentence anywhere says what the product is, who it's for, or what you get. The only explanatory text is an 11px mono line in ink-4 sitting directly on the art: "two decks ≈ 5 s a game · four decks ≈ 8 min for 16".
findings.why_it_hurts: It fails the 10-second test the owner asked about. It also breaks the project's own binding structural rule (mockups/design_principles.md:7, "every page opens with real prose computed from real data") and its AI-tell list (#3 stat-card banner, #10 no prose). The tally figures describe the server, not the visitor's problem. Four equally weighted doors force a choice before the visitor knows what any of them does (Hick's law).
findings.recommendation: Replace the tally and prompt with a two-sentence lede in the report's voice, computed from live data. For example: "Paste your Commander list and Sim Lab seats it against three other decks for 16 games with Forge's AI, rotating seats so nobody gets a free turn order. You get win rates against the 25% even share, replays of every game, and a read on how your deck actually wins." Then one primary, "Test your deck" (to /import, or to the deck picker if they already have one), and a single proof object: the latest clean run as a mini result card (four commander art avatars, win bars with the 25% tick, "Watch Kess win on round 9"). Demote the other destinations to quiet links; the nav already carries them.

findings.where: The analyse-MY-deck journey across /import (web/app/import/page.tsx:400-410), /decks/[file] (web/app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:170-313), and /new (web/app/new/page.tsx:178-283)
findings.what_happens: Import ends in a small note: "Saved as skrat_s_revenge_239c6293.dck · Run a gauntlet with it →". /new then gives you 43 identical-weight tiles with no guidance on which three opponents make a fair pod. The deck page has no link to the deck's runs, record or replays. Home says Skrat's Revenge has 14 runs, but its deck page never mentions them; the only route is typing its name into the /results filter. The deck page's actions are Use in a run · Playtest · Delete deck, nothing about results.
findings.why_it_hurts: The primary job is spread across four nouns that don't point at each other, so the user has to hold the model in their head (recognition over recall). Moxfield and Archidekt make the deck page the hub (a Playtester button, stats, change history). Here the deck is a dead end and a result is an orphaned file. There is no loop of 'tweak the deck, test again, compare'.
findings.recommendation: Make /decks/[file] the hub. Header: commander art_crop banner, name, identity pips, bracket. Tabs: Cards · Tests · Playtest. The Tests tab lists every run the deck was in, each with win rate against that pod's even share, games played, date, and a "Watch best game" link, and has a "Test again" primary. On /new, split the page into a "Your deck" slot (preselected from ?deck=) and an "Opponents" picker with presets (for example "Bracket 3 field: Atraxa Counters, Drana Vampires, Nekusar Punisher" and "Same pod as last time"). After import, route straight to the new deck's page with "Test this deck" as the primary.

findings.where: shortName/runTitle in web/lib/format.ts:10-15, 27-33; default deck name in web/app/import/page.tsx:78-83. Visible on home Most recent sims, every /results row, the /runs/[id] H1 and seat labels, and the report H1 (/results/sim_20260925_003803...json)
findings.what_happens: Titles are built from each deck's first whitespace token with punctuation kept: "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal", "The vs Atraxa vs Ant-Man vs Inspirit" (the first deck is The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl), "Living vs NanMan vs Kambal vs Kilo,", "Dnide vs Inspirit vs The vs Tergrid,". The run page's tabletop labels a seat "Kess,". The cause is upstream too: import names a deck after its first card by default, which produced "Kilo, Apogee Mind - Rock Pop", "Deadpool, Trading Card" and "Stella Lee, Wild Card" as deck names.
findings.why_it_hurts: The run title is the most-read string in the product, and it reads as machine-truncated on the report H1. Nothing signals 'no human looked at this' faster.
findings.recommendation: Derive the short label from the commander name, not the deck name: take the text before the comma, strip a leading "The ", and keep the Unbeatable/Timeless-style suffix only when two seats clash ("Kess", "Squirrel Girl", "Krenko", "Stella"). Strip trailing punctuation as a guard. In 3 to 4 deck titles, prefer a row of commander art avatars with names on hover. Leave the import deck name blank with the placeholder "e.g. Skrat's Revenge" and require it, or default it to "<commander short name> deck".

findings.where: /decks/[file] card list (web/app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:28-69, 246-300; web/app/globals.css:869-877)
findings.what_happens: Skrat's Revenge renders 75 rows at 92px each, making the page 9,370px tall in a 900px viewport (about 10 screens). Every row prints the full oracle text of cards this audience already knows. Mana costs are raw text, "{1}{G}{G}{G}", in 11.5px ink-4 mono (globals.css:874). There's no mana curve, no colour-pip demand, no type totals up top beyond one lede sentence, no bracket, and no commander art header (the commander is a 48px thumbnail row). The hover preview floats over the row you're reading.
findings.why_it_hurts: The layout ignores the conventions this audience lives in (Jakob's law). Moxfield's and Archidekt's defaults are dense text columns or stacks grouped by type, with quantity, name and cost symbols, a hover preview in a fixed column, and a stats view with curve and colour pie. Archidekt's header also carries 'Commander · Legal · Bracket: Upgraded (3) · Size 100' and theme tags. Printing every oracle text reads like a data dump rather than a curated view, and it hides the shape of the deck.
findings.recommendation: Default to a 3 to 4 column compact list grouped by type (header "Creatures 25"), with qty · name · cost drawn in the commissioned pips at 14px (generic mana as a numeral in a neutral disc token). A 100-card deck then fits in about 1.5 screens. Show oracle text only in the preview, and dock the preview in a sticky right column on desktop. Add a stats strip under the header: a 0 to 7+ mana curve histogram, type counts, and coloured pip demand against coloured sources. This is display data from Scryfall facts and involves no rules interpretation. Header: commander art_crop banner with name, identity and bracket.

findings.where: In-progress runs are surfaced only by /runs/[id] (the only api.simStatus caller is web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:61); home and /results list finished runs only
findings.what_happens: A 4-deck run takes about an hour. If you close or lose the tab, the job has no address anywhere in the UI: home 'Most recent sims' and /results filter to finished runs, and there's no nav indicator. Nothing on /runs says you may leave; the only mention is "Leave it running" inside the over-typical warning.
findings.why_it_hurts: Visibility of system status (Nielsen #1). A user who can't find their running job re-queues it, which is exactly what the engine's progress code was written to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Pin a 'Running now' row to the top of /results and the home data panel, using the design system's status shapes (filled circle with glow for running, hollow circle for queued). Add a small live dot to the Results nav item while a job is in flight. First line of /runs: "You can close this tab. The run keeps going and appears in Results when it finishes."

findings.where: /results 'Winner' column (web/app/results/page.tsx:136, 202-217); home Most recent sims (web/app/page.tsx:192-206, 404-410); home Top decklists (web/app/page.tsx:187-190, 350-360); /runs done lede (web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:497-503)
findings.what_happens: Examples: "Power Cosmic 25%" is the green-marked Winner of a 4-deck, 4-game run, and 25% is exactly the even share. "Kess, Reanimator 50%" is shown as the winner where another deck may tie. "Kilo, Apogee Mind - Mostly Precon 100%" on 2 games. The home leaderboard ranks Skrat's Revenge 8% against Ur-Dragon B3 59%, pooled across different pods, with cyan fill bars, then adds a note asking you not to compare them. The run page says "Kambal Taxes B3 won 4 of 8 games (50%)" with no baseline, although that run had 2 draws and 2 timeouts.
findings.why_it_hurts: This breaks CLAUDE.md's calibration rule to show baselines alongside any win rate. The leaderboard shows a ranking and then disclaims it in fine print, which is dishonest in shape even though the words are honest. Players over-read small samples.
findings.recommendation: Replace 'Winner' with 'Leader vs even share': "Kambal  50%  (+25 over 25%)", or a 60px bar with a 1/N tick. Show "tie" for ties and "no clear leader" when the top rate is at or below 1/N. Rank the home leaderboard by average points above each run's even share, weighted by games, and show n ("14 runs · 112 games"). The disclaimer then becomes unnecessary. Add "(even share 25%)" to the /runs lede.

findings.where: /import source tabs and lede (web/app/import/page.tsx:10, 154-158, 187-199, 222-239, 400-410)
findings.what_happens: Three of the four source tabs ("Moxfield URL", "Archidekt URL", "Upload .dck") lead to "import is coming soon. The engine only takes pasted text today." The lede promises "anything unrecognized is flagged with a suggested fix, and fixes apply only if you accept them", but no suggested-fix UI exists; the checks are card count, duplicates and a commander guess. Commander is a single select, so partner, background or friends-forever pairs can't be designated (Skrat's list itself runs Jaheira, a Choose a Background card). On success the page prints the .dck filename and offers a small text link.
findings.why_it_hurts: Dead tabs are dead chrome, and design_principles.md's structural rules forbid it. The first thing a Moxfield user tries (pasting a URL) is advertised and then refused. A lede that promises a feature that doesn't exist is the kind of copy that reads as generated. Printing the filename contradicts the Chrome.tsx:153-159 rule that addresses are not content.
findings.recommendation: Remove the three tabs until they're real. Keep one paste box that detects a pasted moxfield.com or archidekt.com URL and answers inline: "URL import isn't built yet. On Moxfield: More > Export > Copy for MTGO, then paste here." Rewrite the lede to what is true (set codes, foil markers and collector numbers parse; the engine re-checks on save). Let two cards be marked as commanders. Auto-detect Arena 'Commander' and Moxfield '// Commander' section headers. On success, go to the new deck's page with "Test this deck" as the primary.

findings.where: /decks gallery and the shared DeckGallery (web/app/decks/page.tsx:84-94; web/components/DeckGallery.tsx:71-87, 105-117; web/app/globals.css:809)
findings.what_happens: 43 flat tiles with no sort, grouping, 'mine' section, bracket, record or last-tested date. Seven Inspirit variants and eight Kilo variants share identical art. Dev names are exposed to the public: "Dnide Wildsear", "N3cro Raggadragga", "NanMan Felix Five-Boots", "Shelly Siona", "Inspirit B3 v3". The colour filter is OR (checking W and U returns every deck containing W or U), and one row mixes the spellings "Colour identity" and "Colorless". Tile pips render at 13px (globals.css:809), although DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §4 says the black skull vanishes below about 20px. The Tergrid MDFC tile has no art and falls back to a mono commander string.
findings.why_it_hurts: Commander players filter by identity as 'fits within these colours' (Scryfall id<=, Archidekt, Moxfield). OR filtering answers a question nobody asks. For comparison, Archidekt's search tile carries art, a colour bar, the name, "Commander - Bracket: Upgraded (3)", views and updated time, with a sort control. Without grouping, the gallery reads as a developer's fixtures folder rather than a collection.
findings.recommendation: Group builds under one commander tile ("Kilo, Apogee Mind · 8 builds") that expands. Add a sort (Recently tested · Most tested · Name). Add a tile meta line: "Bracket 3 · 14 tests · +6 vs pod". Put 'Your imports' first. Hide test decks behind a 'Show test decks' toggle, or rename them. Change the filter to identity subset with an 'Exactly these' toggle, and use one spelling throughout. Render pips at 18px or larger. Fall back to the front face's art for MDFCs.

findings.where: Naming across nav (web/components/Chrome.tsx:15, 26-32), home buttons (web/app/page.tsx:257-278), /new lede, deck page 'Use in a run', import 'Save deck to engine' / 'Run a gauntlet with it', report tabs (web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:193-195) vs replay tabs (web/app/results/[file]/replay/[game]/page.tsx:272-273)
findings.what_happens: One concept has seven names: simulation, sim, run, gauntlet, pod, result, report. 'Sim history & analytics' opens a page titled 'Results'. The nav comment claims every item is a noun, but 'Simulate' is a verb. The Overview page's tabs are Overview · Telemetry · Coaching, while the replay page's tabs are Overview · Replay, so the tab set changes under you. 'Engine' leaks into user copy ("Save deck to engine", "decks on this engine"). 'Telemetry' is engineering vocabulary. The Rules nav item offers ASK even though production has no model configured (/engine/health llm:false); you only find out after asking (web/app/rules/page.tsx:264-268).
findings.why_it_hurts: Consistency and standards (Nielsen #4). Each synonym makes the user wonder whether it's a different thing. A tab set that changes per page breaks wayfinding.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a four-word glossary and enforce it: Deck, Test (N games of your deck in a pod), Game, Replay. Nav: Decks · Tests · Playtest · Rules. Use one identical tab set on every run page: Summary · Games · How it wins (was Telemetry) · Coaching. Remove 'engine' from user-facing strings. On /rules, read health.llm and label the box "Search the rules" when generation is off.

findings.where: Home hero and hub (web/app/page.tsx:98-114, 241-283; hardcoded hexes at page.tsx:254, 260, 266, 274); spec at Design System/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md:221-251
findings.what_happens: The tally uses the White, Blue and Red mana medallions and the colourless one as decoration for 'decks', 'games', 'runs' and 'rules'. The action hub gives four buttons four different glowing borders (cyan, violet, sky, grey) and gradient fills, all 18px uppercase. The SVG icons hardcode #00E5FF, #C89BFA, #7DD3FC and #C3CEDA. The counters roll up on load.
findings.why_it_hurts: This breaks DS law 3 ("WUBRG is data. A colour never means two things"). A Commander player reads a red medallion as red. It breaks "Never hardcode a hex" and design_principles rule 9 ("No entrance animations"). It reintroduces four items from the project's own AI-tell list (design_principles.md:21-34): #2 glow and glass, #3 KPI banner, #6 all-caps labels, #8 Space Grotesk. The spec itself mandates the tally and the 'What would you like to do today?' prompt, so the slop is written into the binding document.
findings.recommendation: The owner should amend DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §6: drop the tally banner and the prompt line, and ban pips as ornament (use them only where they mean colour identity). Keep exactly one glowing primary; secondary destinations become sentence-case text links. Icons use currentColor with tokens. Keep the mascot, the backdrop and Cinzel, which carry the identity without the SaaS pattern.

findings.where: /runs/[id] finished state (web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:497-503, 517-521, 612-614)
findings.what_happens: On the finished job 9212fe0f3a11, the page still says "Played back at a watchable pace, not live. The simulation keeps running." and "The playback below finishes first; the full report is one click away." The fallback line reads "Check past runs on the home page.", but past runs live at /results. The headline figure block shows the top win rate with no even-share reference.
findings.why_it_hurts: State-inaccurate copy undermines trust in the status UI, which is otherwise carefully built (the liveness and stall messages are excellent). Pointing users to the wrong page wastes a click.
findings.recommendation: Make the copy state-specific. When done: "Replaying game 1 of 8 from the finished run." Point the fallback at /results. Add "(even share 25%)" to the headline and the figure label.

findings.where: Document metadata and assets (web/app/layout.tsx:9-12, 27; web/public/art/backdrop-hedron-ruins.png, 2,652,638 bytes; no icon file in web/app or web/public)
findings.what_happens: Every route's <title> is "Arcane Sim Lab", including deck pages, reports and replays, and there's no favicon. A 2.65 MB PNG backdrop loads behind every page, mobile included.
findings.why_it_hurts: With a deck, a report and two replays open, the user has four identical blank tabs and history entries (recognition over recall). The PNG is the largest paint on every first load and slows LCP on phones. Details like these are what make a site feel finished or not.
findings.recommendation: Add per-route titles ("Skrat's Revenge · Decks", "Kess vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko · Tests", "Game 4 replay · Kess vs ..."). Make a favicon from mascot-brass-archivist-head.webp. Re-encode the backdrop to AVIF or WebP (about 150 to 250 KB) with a srcset for narrow screens.

findings.where: /decks/[file] header and lede (web/app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:204-233, 246-268, 141); client key in web/lib/api.ts:44-50
findings.what_happens: On imported decks, 'Delete deck' is a same-size peer of 'Use in a run' and 'Playtest' on a public, account-less site. The lede spends half its length on bookkeeping ("Imported, so it can be deleted from here." / "This deck ships with the engine and cannot be deleted."). After a delete the page routes to /new, not /decks. apiKey() falls back to NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY, which is inlined into the client bundle, so if the key is set any visitor's browser is authorised for the delete.
findings.why_it_hurts: A destructive action at peer weight next to the primary invites slips (error prevention). The lede is the most-read line on the page and says nothing about the deck.
findings.recommendation: Move Delete into the 'Deck details' disclosure at the page foot. Rewrite the lede about the deck: "99 cards: 35 lands, 25 creatures, curve peaks at 3. Tested 14 times; wins 8% against a 25% even share." After a delete, go to /decks. Until tasks/06 identity lands, gate delete on a key the user entered in this browser, not the build-time default.

findings.where: Engine-down states: web/app/page.tsx:24, 219-235; web/app/decks/page.tsx:23, 67-72; web/app/new/page.tsx:28, 136-166; web/app/results/page.tsx:20, 83-87
findings.what_happens: If the API is unreachable, public users are told "Start it with python3 engine/mtg_engine.py serve 8484".
findings.why_it_hurts: Developer instructions on a production site confuse visitors and read as an unfinished prototype. The user can't act on them (Nielsen #9: help users recover).
findings.recommendation: Production copy: "Sim Lab's server isn't answering. Your decks and results are safe; try again in a minute." plus a Retry button. Show the shell command only when process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'.

findings.where: Gallery and home loading states (web/components/DeckGallery.tsx:135-143; web/app/decks/page.tsx:73-74; home tally web/app/page.tsx:35-76)
findings.what_happens: Tiles render as 43 identical dark rectangles for about 3 s until the batched art call returns. At 375px the Green filter pip rendered as a blank gap while loading. Home counters start at 0 and roll up, so a quick glance can read "0 decks".
findings.why_it_hurts: Grey voids look broken rather than loading. A counter that briefly shows 0 misstates the data.
findings.recommendation: Render each tile's colour-identity gradient plate immediately (identity is in the cached facts), or use a reduced-motion-aware skeleton. Preload the six pip WebPs. Render the counters at their final values, or remove them per FR-12.

strengths: Honesty machinery is real and should be showcased, not buried: per-run validity flags ('read with care', 'not comparable'), the home note "Built from 25 of 46 runs", seat rotation, and the report's even-share marker.

The report page lede is exactly the right voice ("Kess, Reanimator won 4 of 8 seat-rotated games (50%), 2 wins clear of Stella Lee, Wild Card (25%)... the median game ran 41 turns"). Home and the deck page should talk like this.

The run page's liveness copy is humane and specific ("This run is taking longer than usual, and that is normal... the last game activity was X ago... Starting the same gauntlet again would make both copies slower"), and it uses server-side typical ranges.
The primary is never disabled; the blocker sits beside it ("Pick at least 2 decks; you have 0.", "Paste a list first.").
The card hover and tap preview shows the full Scryfall card instantly, and the row is keyboard-focusable with a zoom cursor.
Mobile basics are solid: a sticky run bar on /new, a nav sheet with Escape and outside-click close, results tables that stack into cards, and a visible 2px focus ring on gallery tiles.

Import parses set codes, foil markers and collector numbers, runs live advisory checks (100 cards, singleton, commander guess), and surfaces Commander Spellbook combos with the 'floor, not a verdict' framing before a single game is simmed.
Commissioned painted pips, the brass archivist and the backdrop plates give a distinct, IP-safe identity that no competitor has; keep them and use them with more restraint.
Results rows show absolute dates, the whole row is clickable, and 'Watch' has its own separate target.
slop_signals: "What would you like to do today?" (web/app/page.tsx:248): a chatbot greeting as the page's main line.
KPI tally banner of server vanity stats with a roll-up animation: "43 decks on this engine", "3,152 rules loaded" (web/app/page.tsx:241-246). It is item #3 on the project's own AI-tell list.
Mana medallions used as decorative icons for non-colour stats (web/app/page.tsx:111-114).
Four rainbow-bordered, glowing, all-caps action buttons of equal footprint (web/app/page.tsx:252-280; globals.css:410-440).
Machine-truncated titles with dangling commas: "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal", "The vs Atraxa vs Ant-Man vs Inspirit" (web/lib/format.ts:10-15).
"NaN:NaN" in the Duration column for the drawn game 6 of sim_20260925_003803 (fmtClock at web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:28-31 gets no value).
Every card's full oracle text dumped on the deck page, 9,370px tall: data dumped rather than curated.

Lede sentences about bookkeeping instead of the subject: "43 decks. Open one to read every card.", "Imported, so it can be deleted from here.", "This deck ships with the engine and cannot be deleted."
Import lede promising a suggested-fix feature that doesn't exist (web/app/import/page.tsx:154-158), plus three 'coming soon' tabs.
Stale copy on a finished run: "The simulation keeps running." (web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:613).
Engine jargon in user copy: "Save deck to engine", "decks on this engine", "Telemetry".
A developer's fixture decks in the public gallery: Inspirit Alpha, B3, B3 v2, B3 v3, EDHREC Average, Omega, Omega V2.
Identical <title> on every route and no favicon (web/app/layout.tsx:10).
An inline style on the report games table (style={{ width: 80 }} at web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:668), against the 'all styling lives in globals.css' rule.
Glassmorphism panels over purple lightning art on every route, #2 on the project's own AI-tell list (design_principles.md:23).
craft_opportunities: Name seats the way players talk: "Kess", "Squirrel Girl", "Krenko", "Stella", each with the commander's art_crop as a round seat avatar in run titles and rows.
Put the Commander Bracket (1 to 5) on every deck tile and deck header, and offer pod presets by bracket ("Bracket 3 field").

Draw mana costs with the commissioned pips (generic mana as a numeral in a neutral disc) instead of "{1}{G}{G}{G}", and add a 0 to 7+ curve histogram plus a pip-demand vs colour-source bar using the same medallions.

Explain rotation in players' language: "16 games: every deck is on the play 4 times". On the run page, show a 4x4 seat grid that fills in as games finish, which makes the product's honesty feature visible.
Point 'Watch' in the results list at the most telling game ("Watch Kess win on round 9", "Watch the fastest loss") rather than always game 1; the replay already has 'Skip to the deciding turn'.
Add a Record block on the deck page: "14 tests · 112 games · wins 8% against a 25% even share · best game: round 9 win vs Stella", linking to the Tests tab.
Show a since-last-test diff when a deck is re-imported (Moxfield's 'Changes' tab): cards in and out, and whether the win rate moved beyond noise at this sample size.
During JVM boot, use a true, specific line: "Forge is loading its card database and shuffling four decks", not a generic spinner.
Dock the card preview in a sticky right column on desktop (Archidekt and Moxfield habit) so it never covers the list you're scanning.
Recognise Moxfield's '// Commander' and Arena's 'Commander' section headers on paste, so partner and background pairs are picked automatically, and give the exact Moxfield export path in the hint.
Empty-state copy with a light Magic touch and no gimmick: "Your deck hasn't sat down at a table yet. Test it against three others."
Group a commander's builds into one tile with a small build switcher ("Kilo · 8 builds"), the way players actually keep versions.

walkthroughs.first_impression: On the Kess/Skrat/Stella/Krenko run, the first thing I read is a title with a stray comma ("Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko"). The sentence under it is about whoever won the pod, not about the deck I brought. After that come four identical text-only cards full of blocking percentages, a "real playgroups" table that quietly reorders the decks, and a 37-row "Win conditions" table. In that table Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring "can fire; results meaningful", and my squirrel deck has 28 near-identical rows that all say "too few games to measure this". The honesty instincts are real and rare (clock-cut draws kept out of win rates, the raw sim number beside the model), but the page reads like the engine's output shown to its authors. There is no commander art and no card hovers, Forge turn counts sit next to table rounds, and a Duration cell shows NaN:NaN. An expert trusts the numbers less after reading the combo table, which is the opposite of what the careful calibration work deserves.

findings.where: /results/[file] > 'Win conditions' section. web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:438-633 (table 461-594, reading chips 565-587, produces only in a title attribute 527-533). Data from /analysis/{file}.
findings.what_happens: Every Commander Spellbook variant is a row labelled a 'win condition'. On the Kess run: Skrat's Revenge has 28 rows, 25 of them 'The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl + X + Y' where X/Y rotate through Concordant Crossroads, Cryptolith Rite, Enduring Vitality, Jaheira, Shang-Chi, Elven Chorus, Citanul Hierophants, Thousand-Year Elixir, Akroma's Memorial and Springleaf Parade. Every one of them carries the same Spellbook prerequisite ('You control four or more Squirrels'), and the same chip repeats 33 times: 'draw odds predicted ~0.2; too few games to measure this'. Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring (Spellbook results: infinite colorless mana and storm count, so an engine with no payoff) shows 'Assembled 1 of 8 (T57), Converted 1, AI can fire this; results meaningful'. Kess actually won that game by combat damage 10 turns later. Stella Lee, Wild Card appears as a one-card 'combo' (the commander): 'Assembled 8 of 8 (T11)', 'AI can fire this'. The payload records idle_online_turns 137, so the loop was never executed. Nekusar's Notion Thief + Teferi's Puzzle Box and Kambal's Vito + Exquisite Blood also read 'fired' while every Nekusar win was combat. The engine already sends Spellbook's description (steps), prerequisites and mana_needed for every combo. The page discards all of it except `produces`, which only appears in a hover tooltip.
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the section an expert checks to see whether the tool understands their deck, and it fails in front of them. Mixing engines with finishers is wrong on substance. 'Converted' is defined as 'that seat then won', but the chip turns it into a causal claim ('AI can fire this'), which breaks the product's own honesty contract (SIM_CALIBRATION: engine decks are a floor). Twenty-eight near-duplicates bury the single useful fact in the Skrat data: on the aa577 run, Squirrel Girl + Cryptolith Rite + Concordant Crossroads came together in 2 of 16 games and never fired. That violates recognition over recall and signal-to-noise. It also contradicts how the source it cites presents combos: Commander Spellbook's combo page is organised as Cards / Initial Card State / Notable Prerequisites / Steps / Results / Variants of this combo, with variants folded under one entry.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the section as per-deck 'Combo lines' with these parts. (1) Group the variants: variants with the same results set and all but one card in common collapse to one line, shown as a fixed core plus 'one of' slots. Example: 'Squirrel mana loop: The Unbeatable Squirrel Girl (commander) + one haste or untap source (Concordant Crossroads, Akroma's Memorial, Thousand-Year Elixir...) + one creatures-tap-for-mana card (Cryptolith Rite, Enduring Vitality, Elven Chorus, Citanul Hierophants, Jaheira). 25 variants in your 99.' Krenko's four rows become 'Krenko + Skirk Prospector + one haste source (Goblin Warchief, Goblin Chieftain, Fervor, Hammer of Purphoros)'. Line-level stats count ANY variant: came together in X of N games, earliest turn. (2) Classify each line from its Spellbook results. Finisher: infinite damage, life loss, poison or mill, infinite hasty tokens, 'win the game'. Engine: infinite mana, storm count, untaps, ETB/LTB triggers, draw. Only finishers go under 'How this deck can win'. Engines go under 'Engines (need a payoff)' and list the payoffs found in the 99, or say 'no outlet in this list' (Hullbreaker + Sol Ring). (3) Expanding a line shows Spellbook's own structure verbatim: Initial card state, Notable prerequisites ('Circle of Dreams Druid does not have summoning sickness. You control at least three creatures.'), numbered Steps, Results, and a 'View on Commander Spellbook' link to /combo/{id}. (4) Loops that need only the commander go under 'Commander ability'. 'Assembled' must not mean 'commander on the battlefield'; say 'online 137 turns, loop never executed; Stella's results are a floor'. (5) Replace 'Converted' with two facts: 'won that game' and 'won with it', where the second means the game's loss line matches the line's results on or right after the turn it came online. Only 'won with it' earns a 'fired' reading. (6) Sort finishers first, then by games assembled. Fold lines with expected < 1 and 0 assembled into 'N more lines never came together (expected under once in 8 games)'. (7) Drop the repeated Deck column in favour of per-deck subheads with commander art. Turn 'Piece most often missing' into each line's 'bottleneck card', with a Scryfall hover preview. Engine-side changes (grouping, classification, won-with-it) belong in analysis.py so the UI and coach agree.

findings.where: /results/[file] overall structure. web/app/results/[file]/page.tsx:272-751; no 'your deck' concept anywhere in web/app (grep for focus/your/my deck finds nothing, including web/app/new/page.tsx).
findings.what_happens: The page answers 'who won the pod', not 'how good is my deck'. I measured at 1440x900 as the owner of Skrat's Revenge (an imported deck). The lede and headline figures describe Kess. My raw rate is the third scorecard, about 0.6 screens down and not marked as mine. The modelled estimate is at 1.75 screens. Combo lines start at 2.4 screens and need sideways scrolling. 'What killed it' is on another tab behind a dropdown that defaults to Kess (2 interactions), and for my deck it has no commander data. 'What should I change' exists nowhere, because coaching is dark. The page is 5.2 screens tall at 1440x900 and 8.7 at 375px.
findings.why_it_hurts: The user came with three questions: how good is my deck, why did it win or lose, and what should I change. The page makes them hunt, and it is ordered measured, then modelled, then evidence, then raw. That fails 'verdict first, evidence second, raw last' (the Stripe principle the repo's own design_principles.md cites: 'prioritization first, explanation second, raw depth only when they ask'). Moxfield, Archidekt and EDHREC all centre a single deck identified by its commander art. 17lands lets you scope the whole view to the deck you care about.
findings.recommendation: Record a focus deck on the run: the imported deck, or the first deck picked on /new. Put a deck switcher at the top of /results/[file]: four tabs, each showing the commander's art crop (Scryfall hotlink), colour pips and win count, defaulting to the focus deck. Under it, a per-deck report in this order. (a) Verdict: one computed sentence plus the interval chart from RA-06. (b) Why it won or lost: kill sources, knocked-out round vs the table's median, how each win closed. (c) Did the plan fire: combo lines from RA-01 and commander first-cast round. (d) Did the deck function: land drops, mulligans and lands in kept hands, each against its expectation. (e) What to change: bottleneck cards and one-card-away adds. (f) This deck's games, split into won and lost, each linking to the replay. Fold the Telemetry tab into (b) and (c). Keep a single pod-comparison table for readers who want all four decks side by side.

findings.where: /results/[file]/telemetry for any imported deck. engine/mtg_engine.py:866 calls deck_telemetry.compute(data, deck, watch) without a commander; deck_telemetry.py:68-91 _commander_of fails for /data/decks/* paths. Rows hardcoded in web/app/results/[file]/telemetry/page.tsx:266-285 and the lede at 198-199.
findings.what_happens: On the Kess run, Kess, Reanimator and Skrat's Revenge both say 'No commander could be identified for this deck'. Skrat's own damage list names 'Kess, Dissident Mage 24 dmg', so the data is there. The bundled Krenko deck resolves fine ('Krenko, Mob Boss, cast in 7 of 8, T18 med'). The only 'Win-condition telemetry' rows for every deck are 'Charge counters 0.12/g Partial' and 'Proliferate 0/g Never fired'. Those are Atraxa-era metrics, and the subtitle says they are counted across 'all seats', yet each gets a status as if it were this deck's plan. The lede for a reanimator deck reads: 'The table logged charge counters 0.12 times a game and proliferate 0.'
findings.why_it_hurts: The user's own imported deck gets the broken view and the house decks get the working one, which is backwards. Telling a Krenko or Kess player that 'Proliferate: Never fired' is the kind of template leak that reads as machine-made. It also feeds the coach (coach.py:109) with the same wrong 'support chain'.
findings.recommendation: Pass the deck's [Commander] line into compute() from the route, resolving through _find_deck(Path(deck).name), and add a test with a /data/decks path. Remove charge counters and proliferate as universal rows. Build the plan rows from what the deck actually is: commander first-cast round, each combo line's key pieces (from /analysis), and the archetype's engine cards. Until that exists, show only commander ignition plus 'What killed it'. Convert the damage table to per-source-card, per-game values, and name the token's creator ('Goblin tokens (Krenko, Mob Boss): 19'). Default the deck picker to the focus deck (RA-02).

findings.where: /results/[file] lede, headline figures and scorecards. page.tsx:164 (rate = wins / all games, including draws), page.tsx:306-308 and 355-360, DeckScorecards.tsx:112-116 (wins / decided), PredictionPanel.tsx:83; telemetry header telemetry/page.tsx:174.
findings.what_happens: On the Kess run the same deck shows three different win rates within one screen. The lede says 'won 4 of 8 ... (50%)', the headline figure says '50% top win rate', the scorecard directly below says '4 of 7 57%', and the prediction table says 'Simulated 50.0%'. On the 9212 run: Kambal '4 of 8 (50%)' in the lede, '4 of 6 67%' on its card.
findings.why_it_hurts: Two numbers for one fact makes a careful reader assume the math is wrong, and it undercuts the 'numbers are honest' positioning in front of investors. The scorecard's reason (clock-cut games are excluded from decided games) is sound, but the page never reconciles the two.
findings.recommendation: Choose one denominator. Decided games is the principled choice, and the scorecards already use it. Use it everywhere: lede, figures, prediction 'Simulated' column, telemetry header. State the exclusion once, inline with the number: '4 of 7 decided (57%); 1 game hit the clock and is not counted'. The engine should publish that rate so the pages cannot drift apart.

findings.where: /results/[file] 'Win conditions' table at desktop width. page.tsx:459-461; globals.css:531 (.games td white-space: nowrap); the only-narrow sideways-scroll note is display:none on desktop.
findings.what_happens: At 1440x900 the table measures 1692px inside a 1196px scroller. The 'Reading' column, which the code comment calls 'the product', starts at x=1301, so it is completely off-screen on a normal desktop. 'Piece most often missing' is cut mid-word ('15 of 16: Gonti's Aeth'). The 'scroll sideways' hint is hidden at that width. The 37 rows run about 1,750px, roughly two full screens. At 375px the table is 5.3 times the viewport width.
findings.why_it_hurts: The conclusion the section exists to deliver is invisible unless the user discovers a horizontal scroll nobody tells them about (hidden affordance, a failure of visibility of system status). A 37-row wall pushes the Games list 4.3 screens down.
findings.recommendation: This is solved structurally by RA-01's grouped lines (about 3-6 rows per deck). In the meantime: let the combo cell wrap (remove nowrap from that column); move 'Reading' to a line under the combo name rather than a seventh column; drop the Deck column in favour of group headers; show the sideways-scroll affordance at every width where scrollWidth > clientWidth, e.g. an edge fade driven by a tiny ResizeObserver.

findings.where: 'Against real playgroups' panel. web/components/PredictionPanel.tsx:52-111; interval built in engine/predict.py:153-157 (low/high = expected ± LOO MAE, independent of games played).
findings.what_happens: The 'range each deck plausibly lands in' is always expected ± 4.0, whether the run had 6 decided games or 64. On the 9212 run, Talrand won 0 of 6 decided games and is shown as 'Expected 28.2%, 24.3 to 32.2', ranked above Power Cosmic, which won 25%. Kess won 0 of 6 and is shown as 22.9 to 30.8. The model basis is 'playgroup.gg commander precons ... stock Forge, decided games', but these runs are custom decks played by the shim's plan agent. The panel only says 'fitted against stock Forge' at the end of a 70-word note. The API also sends a per-deck `explanation` (e.g. 'Adjusted up because this deck runs few creatures') and `contributions`, and the panel renders neither. The lede still crowns the raw winner (Drana 50%) even though the panel reduces it to 27.0% and puts Nekusar first.
findings.why_it_hurts: An eight-point band on a deck that never won in six games claims far more certainty than the data supports, the exact overclaim SIM_CALIBRATION exists to prevent. With the 'why' text unused, the correction reads as an unexplained number that reverses the page's own headline. That puts two competing verdicts on one page and leaves an expert with no way to decide which to trust.
findings.recommendation: Widen the interval with sample size: carry the sim input's binomial uncertainty (Wilson interval on decided games) through the model's sim weight, then add the model MAE. Below a floor (for example fewer than 12 decided games), show 'Too few games for a confident estimate' and grey the row out, the way small samples are de-emphasised on 17lands and untapped.gg. Show one explanation line per deck under its name. In the section meta, write the basis in plain words: 'Trained on 66 precons, stock Forge AI; this run used Sim Lab's agent on custom decks.' Settle the hierarchy: if the model's ranking is the verdict, the lede leads with it and the raw figure becomes supporting evidence.

findings.where: 'How games ended' and scorecard 'how it won'. page.tsx:417-427, DeckScorecards.tsx:19-23 and 147-151, games-table annotation page.tsx:706-717.
findings.what_happens: Forge's loss line 'combat damage / life loss' is relabelled 'by combat damage' everywhere. A Vito + Exquisite Blood drain kill (Kambal, 9212 run, game 6: the combo came online on turn 30 and the game ended that turn) is therefore reported as 'by combat damage'. The draw case reads '1 by draw' / '2 by draw', and the games table prints 'Draw (draw)'. Atraxa's win shows as 'how it won: spell' on its card, while the games table knows it was 'won by Simic Ascendancy'.
findings.why_it_hurts: The note under the section says 'A pod that only ever ends in combat damage is telling you its combo decks never converted'. The mislabel makes that exact inference false. Commander players distinguish drain, poison and combat kills instinctively, so 'spell' and 'by draw' read as untranslated engine enums.
findings.recommendation: Say 'life total reached 0 (combat or life loss)' unless the event log can separate the two. Better, have analysis.py attribute the final life change to its source (combat damage event vs a trigger or spell) and label 'combat', 'drain (Exquisite Blood)', 'poison', 'spell (Simic Ascendancy)'. Render draws as 'Draw: hit the 15-minute clock' and drop the '(draw)' suffix.

findings.where: /results/[file]/coaching. web/app/results/[file]/coaching/page.tsx:276-302 (dark state), 215-231 (Matchups); engine/coach.py:101-142 (context), 50-73 (prompt).
findings.what_happens: I checked 40 runs x 4 decks through the cache-only endpoint: no coaching report exists for any of them. Every visitor sees a glowing primary, 'Generate coaching report (~$0.01, about 20 s)', followed by 'the engine has no model key ... Set MTG_LLM_API_KEY in deploy/.env and redeploy'. The note ends 'Everything else on this page ... works without it', but nothing else is on the page. When the feature is live: the coach reads only telemetry (with the broken rows from RA-03), archetype and each opponent's pod-wide win rate. It never sees /analysis combos, scorecards (mulligans, land drops, blocking) or the prediction. The 'Matchups' rows print each opponent's overall pod win rate, which reads as my win rate against that deck. Changes render with raw bracket tags '[sim-evidence]' / '[theory]'.
findings.why_it_hurts: Operator instructions and per-call pricing shown to playtesters look unfinished and expose internals. A tab that is dead on every run teaches users to ignore it. When it does run, a coach fed charge-counter telemetry will write generic or wrong advice, the 'AI slop' the owner is trying to escape, and 'Matchups' misrepresents a four-player pod as head-to-head.
findings.recommendation: While there is no model key: hide the Coaching tab, or show 'Coaching is not switched on for this server yet' with no env var names and no price. Keep the operator note in deploy/preflight.py. Before switching it on: add the grouped combo lines, scorecard mana and behaviour figures and the prediction to build_context. Require every change to quote the specific number it rests on, name a card that is in the list, and name a replacement ('Cut Sol Ring? No: cut X for Y because Scurry Oak was never available in 7 of 8 games'). Render evidence as a short inline clause, not a bracket tag. Replace 'Matchups' with 'Who beat you' (games this deck lost, by winner and kill source). Wrap card names in CardPreview.

findings.where: Win-rate rails and headline figures. page.tsx:344-366, 378-399; DeckScorecards.tsx:116-122; globals.css:473-475.
findings.what_happens: Win rates appear as big figures and 6px bars with a baseline tick at 25% and no uncertainty: Kess '57%' from 4 of 7, Krenko '0%' from 0 of 7. The prediction table uses one decimal (12.5%, 33.9%) on 8-game runs. With n=7, the 95% Wilson interval for 4/7 is roughly 25-84%, and for 0/7 it is 0-35%, which contains the 25% even share. The bars suggest a clear ordering that the sample cannot support.
findings.why_it_hurts: Sample size is printed ('4 of 7') but never visualised, so most readers compare bar lengths and go no further. False precision (one decimal on n=8) is a classic honesty failure in data display and goes against the project's own calibration rules.
findings.recommendation: Replace the rails with one interval chart for the whole pod: one row per deck on a 0-100% axis. Show a filled dot for the sim rate with its Wilson interval as a band, a hollow dot for the modelled estimate with its (widened) range, and the 25% even share as a labelled vertical rule. Put 'n = 7 decided' at the row end. This single chart answers 'how good is it and how sure are we' and merges the scorecard rail with the prediction table. Use whole percents below 30 games.

findings.where: Turn units across the area. page.tsx:702 (T{endedTurn}) next to page.tsx:69 ('won on round N'); page.tsx:538 (T{median_assembled_turn}); telemetry/page.tsx:259 ('T18 med') and 313 ('median death turn T36').
findings.what_happens: The same row says 'T36' and 'won on round 10'. Combo assembly shows 'T57' and 'T39.5' (Forge's absolute player-turn counter, sometimes fractional). The telemetry tab says Kess died on 'median death turn T36' while the overview says 'knocked out on round 10'. Krenko's commander 'T18 med' is really round 5.
findings.why_it_hurts: Commander players say 'I won on turn 7' and mean their own seventh turn, the table round. Forge's absolute count means nothing to them and 4x inflates every timing claim. Mixing units within one row forces mental conversion, which fails the 'speak the user's language' heuristic.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on table rounds everywhere, rendered as 'turn 10' with a one-time definition ('turns are table rounds: everyone's first turn is turn 1'), or as 'round 10' consistently. Convert assembled and death turns server-side. Never show fractional turns; the median of an even count takes the lower value or is labelled 'about'. Drop the 'Ended' column (see RA-13).

findings.where: 'What each deck did' scorecards. web/components/DeckScorecards.tsx:94-233; globals.css:668-686.
findings.what_happens: Four paragraph-cards of the same shape. At 1440 they fall into a 3+1 grid with Krenko alone on the second row (auto-fit minmax 320px). 'Survived to the end' always equals the win rate: Kess 57/57, Stella 29/29, Skrat 14/14, Drana 50/50, Atraxa 6/6. That is because in a four-player game only the winner survives, so the read sentence 'Still standing at the end of 57% of them' is a tautology. Blocking gives five metrics per deck ('took 91% of 11 free blocks', 'and 92% of the blocks it would survive') with no pod reference. The labelled rows wrap under their own 'Blocking' label, producing a ragged block. At about 1024px the 'how it won' value truncates to 'combat dama…' (.scv ellipsis). The most actionable figures, Skrat's 2.6 lands in kept hands, 63% keep-7 and 0.76 land drops per turn (a mana base problem), sit in 10.5px grey text with no comment. There is no commander art or colour identity, so the four cards are told apart only by title text.
findings.why_it_hurts: Comparing decks is the whole point, and paragraphs spread across cards make it slow: the eye has to find the same phrase in four places. Repeating the win rate as another stat is filler that an expert notices immediately. Burying the mana data hides the clearest 'what should I change' signal on the page.
findings.recommendation: Replace the four cards with a comparison table. Columns are decks, each headed by commander art, pips and 'W of N'. Rows are grouped: Outcome (median win turn, knocked-out turn vs table), Mana (missed land drops per 10 turns, kept 7, lands in kept hand vs the hypergeometric expectation for that deck's land count), Combat (blocked %, chump share, attackers committed), plus a 'pod average' column. Highlight only cells that differ meaningfully from the pod average. Delete 'survived to the end'. Keep one computed sentence per deck as the column footer, or move it into the per-deck report (RA-02). Blocking detail goes behind 'Combat detail'.

findings.where: Deck result chips. DeckScorecards.tsx:112, page.tsx:391 and 693; globals.css:446-462 (.st.win = done square, .st.loss = hollow circle, .st.bad = filled red circle, .st.warn = diamond).
findings.what_happens: A deck above the even share gets the job-status 'done' glyph (green square), one below gets a hollow circle (visually the 'queued' shape), and a winless deck gets the red filled 'failed' dot, so Krenko '0 of 7' looks like a crashed job. The 'warn' diamond means both 'assembled, never fired' and 'never assembled despite draw odds'. In the games table only the run leader's wins get the green square, and every other winner is plain text.
findings.why_it_hurts: The binding spec says status is shape and a colour never means two things. Here the same glyphs mean job state on /runs and deck performance on /results. Highlighting only the leader's wins gives arbitrary visual weight to one deck in a table meant to be read neutrally.
findings.recommendation: Stop using .st for deck performance. Show the relationship to baseline as text and position ('+32 pts vs even share') or in the interval chart (RA-09). Give each deck a consistent identity marker (commander art thumbnail or colour pips, which the spec permits on deck rows) and use it in the games table for every winner, not just the leader.

findings.where: 'Games' table. page.tsx:635-741; fmtClock page.tsx:28-31; draw annotation page.tsx:706-717.
findings.what_happens: Clock-cut draws show 'Duration NaN:NaN'. result.duration_ms is absent even though the raw line says 'Took 900948 ms', and it happens twice on the 9212 run. 'Decided by' repeats the winner's name ('Kess, Reanimator won on round 9') right beside the Winner column. 'Duration' is the machine's compute time (4:30), which means nothing to a player. There is a free-text filter box for 8 rows, a 'Watch' link column on rows that are already fully clickable (the spec's recent-sims rule says whole row is the link, no repeated 'Watch' column), no sorting, and nothing about who died first. The timed-out game's payload knows Skrat's Revenge was eliminated at -12 life, but the row just says 'Draw'.
findings.why_it_hurts: NaN:NaN is the single most 'unfinished' signal a data page can show. The columns spend width on things a player does not care about and leave out the story they do care about: who died when, and to what.
