findings.recommendation: Columns: Game, Winner (identity marker), 'Won on turn N' (rounds), How (kill source from /analysis, e.g. 'poison (Skrat's Revenge)'), Elimination order (small seat strip with an x and turn per player), Seat the winner played from. The whole row links to the replay, ideally deep-linked to the lethal event. Replace the text filter with deck chips ('Kess 4 · Stella 2 · Skrat 1 · Draw 1'). Parse duration from raw as a fallback, and move wall-clock time into Run details. Draw rows: 'Draw: clock hit on turn 10; Skrat's Revenge already out'.

findings.where: Page h1 on every result. web/lib/format.ts:10-15 (shortName splits on whitespace) used by runTitle format.ts:27-33.
findings.what_happens: Titles render as 'Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko', 'Kambal vs Power vs Kess, vs Talrand' and 'Nekusar vs Drana vs Skrat's vs Living'. The first-word truncation keeps a trailing comma and cuts 'Power Cosmic' to 'Power' and 'Living Energy+' to 'Living'.
findings.why_it_hurts: The h1 is the first thing read, and a stray comma in it looks careless. It is the opposite of the 'a human took care' impression the owner wants.
findings.recommendation: Title the run by commander short names, which /analysis already returns (decks[].commanders: 'Kess vs Squirrel Girl vs Stella vs Krenko'), with deck names as a fallback. Strip trailing punctuation, and never cut a two-word name to one word unless both words appear elsewhere. Better still, render four small commander art crops beside the title.

findings.where: Prediction table styling. PredictionPanel.tsx:69-96 reuses .telet, which has no th rule and no .r alignment (globals.css:551-557).
findings.what_happens: Measured computed styles: every th is text-align:center, 14px, ink-2, while every numeric td is left-aligned ('start'). So 'Simulated' is centred over left-aligned '50.0%'. Negative corrections use a hyphen ('-16.1'), not a minus sign, and have no unit. The table has five columns, and one of them (Correction) is simple arithmetic on two others.
findings.why_it_hurts: Misaligned numeric columns are the classic look of a hurried table, and the repo's own design_principles.md requires numbers right-aligned with quiet headers. A table of four numbers per deck is the wrong form for 'the sim said X, people would see Y'.
findings.recommendation: Short term: add .telet th / .telet .r rules (quiet 11.5px ink-4 left-aligned headers, right-aligned tabular numbers), and use U+2212 with 'pts' ('−16.1 pts'). Proper fix: replace the table with a dumbbell chart (sim dot to expected dot, with the range band) sorted by expected, with the explanation sentence under each deck name. Or merge it into RA-09's single interval chart.

findings.where: All analysis surfaces: page.tsx, DeckScorecards.tsx, PredictionPanel.tsx, telemetry/page.tsx, coaching/page.tsx. None imports CardPreview, ManaPips or scryfallArt (they are used only by replay, decks, playtest, home and runs).
findings.what_happens: Every card name in the analysis area is plain text: combo pieces, 'piece most often missing', kill sources ('Guttersnipe 30 dmg'), suggested adds and cuts. No commander art or colour identity appears anywhere on the results page.
findings.why_it_hurts: Moxfield, Archidekt, EDHREC, Scryfall and Commander Spellbook all show a card image on hover over any card name, and every Commander player expects it. Without images the analysis pages look like a spreadsheet export and are the least 'Magic' part of the product.
findings.recommendation: Wrap every card name on these pages in the existing CardPreview (Scryfall hotlink, keyboard-focusable, with a tap target on touch). Use Scryfall art crops for deck identity in the switcher, the comparison-table headers and the games table. Use ManaPips beside deck names, as the design system permits on deck rows.

findings.where: Headline figures strip. page.tsx:344-366.
findings.what_happens: The four figures are '8 games in this run' (already in the subtitle and the lede), '12 median rounds per game' (in the lede), '50% top win rate (Kess, Reanimator)' (in the lede, and conflicting with the card's 57%) and '1 draw' (in the lede).
findings.why_it_hurts: Four slots of prime space restate the sentence directly above them. That is the KPI-banner pattern the repo's own design_principles.md lists as an AI tell, and it carries no new information.
findings.recommendation: Delete the strip, or turn it into per-deck figures for the focus deck: decided-game record, modelled range, median win turn, missed land drops.

findings.where: Section notes. DeckScorecards.tsx:263-280 (about 70 words, four topics), PredictionPanel.tsx:104-110, page.tsx:430-434 and 599-630.
findings.what_happens: Each section ends with a long hedging paragraph at 12.5px ink-4. The scorecard note explains the baseline, rounds, clock-cut games and the observer in a single block. The prediction note spends 70 words on method.
findings.why_it_hurts: The honesty is right, but in this form it reads as defensive boilerplate and gets skipped. Caveats work when they sit next to the number they qualify.
findings.recommendation: Move each caveat inline and next to its number: 'n = 7 decided' at the row end, 'inferred' as a small label on the Assembled column head, 'modelled' in the chart legend. Collect the method in one 'How to read this run' disclosure at the foot. Keep the required honesty notes, in fewer words.

findings.where: Telemetry watched cards. telemetry/page.tsx:38 and 76 read ?watch=a|b from the URL; there is no control to set it.
findings.what_happens: A 'watched card' feature exists, with per-card events per game and a status, but it can only be reached by hand-editing the URL.
findings.why_it_hurts: An undiscoverable affordance, the exact failure the repo's ui-review skill is meant to catch. 'Did my pet card ever do anything?' is a question Commander players really ask.
findings.recommendation: Add a labelled 'Track a card' input on the per-deck report (autocomplete from the decklist, with card previews). Pre-populate it with the bottleneck cards from the combo lines.

strengths: The honesty architecture is real and should be kept: clock-cut draws are counted as played but never decided (DeckScorecards.tsx:244-255), and validity notes appear when a run is polluted (page.tsx:333-342). The prediction panel labels itself 'modelled, not simulated' and keeps the raw sim beside the correction, and its note is written to hold whether the correction runs up or down (PredictionPanel.tsx:98-110).

The ledes are computed from real data, not boilerplate ('Kess, Reanimator won 4 of 8 seat-rotated games (50%), 2 wins clear of Stella Lee ... 1 game ended drawn, and it hit the per-game clock'). This is the right voice. It just needs to be about the user's deck.
readOf() in DeckScorecards.tsx:58-81 refuses to describe a habit from a tiny denominator, and it gates every behavioural clause on its own sample. That is expert-grade restraint.
'Piece most often missing' is the most actionable idea on the page (a named bottleneck card per line). Keep it and promote it.
'What killed it' (damage by source) on the telemetry tab is exactly what a Commander player wants after a loss. It belongs in the main per-deck report.

The engine payloads are rich and well shaped: Spellbook steps, prerequisites and results; per-game piece arrival turns; prediction explanations and contributions. Most of the fixes are presentation, not new data.

Seat rotation and the played game count are stated in the subtitle. Games stack cleanly on mobile (the stackable contract), empty values use en dashes, figures use tabular mono, and the small payloads (summary, scorecards, analysis) keep the page fast.
slop_signals: 'Still standing at the end of 57% of them.' (DeckScorecards.tsx:54-56) and the 'survived to the end' stat (137-141) always equal the win rate in a four-player game. It is a tautology dressed up as insight, on every card of every run.
The same chip text appears 33 times in one table: 'draw odds predicted ~0.2; too few games to measure this' (page.tsx:575-580).

The telemetry lede for a reanimator deck reads 'The table logged charge counters 0.12 times a game and proliferate 0.', and Krenko and Kess get a 'Proliferate: Never fired' status (telemetry/page.tsx:198-199, 266-285). Metrics written for one deck are applied to every deck.
'AI can fire this; results meaningful' on Hullbreaker Horror + Sol Ring and on a one-card Stella Lee 'combo' with 137 idle turns: a confident label with no evidence behind it (page.tsx:565-569).
Mechanically truncated h1s: 'Kess, vs Stella vs Skrat's vs Krenko', 'Kambal vs Power vs Kess, vs Talrand', 'Nekusar vs Drana vs Skrat's vs Living' (format.ts:10-15).
'NaN:NaN' in the Duration column and 'Draw (draw)' in Decided by (page.tsx:28-31, 714); '1 by draw' in How games ended.
Four headline figures ('8 games in this run', '1 draw') restating the subtitle and lede: the KPI-banner tell from the repo's own design_principles.md list.
Four identical text-only scorecards with no commander art or pips: the 'everything is a card' tell, and the four decks are not visually distinguishable.

The coaching page shows end users 'Generate coaching report (~$0.01, about 20 s)' and 'Set MTG_LLM_API_KEY in deploy/.env and redeploy'. The coach output schema renders raw bracket evidence tags '[sim-evidence]' / '[theory]' (coaching/page.tsx:251).
A defensive paragraph of 50-70 words under every section, at the ink-4 floor, reads as the page justifying itself rather than informing the reader.

Worth the owner's attention: the Arcane reskin (glass panels, cyan glow, Space Grotesk plus a serif wordmark) matches tells #2 and #8 in the repo's own mockups/design_principles.md list. On the results page this makes a dense analytics surface feel like a template theme. The data areas would read as more crafted on plainer, higher-contrast table ground inside the glass panel.
craft_opportunities: Talk in Commander terms: 'won on turn 10' (table rounds) everywhere, never Forge's T36. 'Died to Goblin tokens from Krenko, Mob Boss' instead of 'Goblin Token 19 dmg'. 'Missed a land drop 1 turn in 4' instead of '0.75 land drops per turn'.

Compare mana stats against the deck's own expectation: 'kept 2.6 lands on average; a 35-land 99 should keep about 3.1', using the hypergeometric model already in analysis.py. That turns a buried stat into a deck-building note a player will act on.

Present combo lines the way Commander Spellbook does: Cards, Initial card state, Notable prerequisites, Steps, Results, then 'View on Commander Spellbook', with variants folded under one line and 'one of' slots listing interchangeable pieces.

Make 'one card away' actionable. Power Cosmic has 66 near-combos and Skrat 109: show the three cards that would complete the most finisher lines, each with a Scryfall hover preview. This is the missing 'what should I change' answer.
Show seat rotation instead of just stating it: a small 4x4 grid of deck by seat with win marks, so a player can see Kess won from seats 1, 2 and 4, not only from going first.
Deep-link each game row to the replay at the lethal event, and label the primary for the focus deck: 'Watch Skrat's Revenge poison the table (game 1)' plus 'Watch its fastest loss'.

Identify decks by commander art crop plus colour pips (Scryfall hotlink; pips are permitted on deck rows) in the deck switcher, comparison-table headers and games table, the way Moxfield and EDHREC identify every deck.

Typographic care: U+2212 minus with 'pts', whole percents under 30 games, thin-space before %, right-aligned tabular numbers with quiet left-aligned headers, and the 25% even share labelled on the chart rule instead of in a footnote.

For the Stella Lee style commander loops, write the prerequisite the AI misses in plain words: 'Needs two spells cast this turn and Stella untapped; the AI held her online 137 turns and never looped. Treat Stella's results as a floor.'
Name the elimination order in the games table (a small seat strip with an x and the turn each player died). Pod players remember games by who got knocked out first and by what.

walkthroughs.first_impression: It opens on a SaaS dashboard page, not a table. At 1440x900 the first 358px is chrome, a generic "Game 1" and a spoiler sentence. The table is a boxed 826px widget of 46x64px cards I can't read, and hovering one gives only a native browser tooltip. When I press play I spend the first minute watching "Untap step", "Upkeep step", "Draw step" and "Forest: Add {G}" tick past, each held exactly as long as a real spell. Then I jump to the "deciding turn" of the game the playtester complained about. Two players carrying 46 and 19 poison are still seated. The infect swing that killed them happened a full round earlier. And in Skrat's turns the attack markers vanish the moment blockers are declared. Clearly a lot of careful engineering went in (honest board notes, per-defender combat lanes, exact hands), but it is a debug view of a log, not a game someone staged for watching.

findings.where: Every replay where a deck name contains an apostrophe-s, e.g. /results/sim_20260925_003803…/replay/1 (Skrat's Revenge). web/lib/replay.ts:244-247 (parsePhase), :261 (isCombatPhase), :534-538 (attacks cleared on any non-combat phase), :569-573 (labelOrd falls back to 12)
findings.what_happens: Forge writes "Skrat's Revenge's Declare Blockers Step". The lazy regex /^(.+?)'s (.+)$/ splits at the first "'s", so the player becomes "Skrat" and the phase "Revenge's declare blockers step". Three visible failures follow. (1) The theater header reads "Round 9 · revenge's declare attackers". (2) No Skrat's phase counts as combat, so at event 847 (declare blockers) the attack banner and the red attacker borders disappear. The viewer then sees "Goblin Token blocks Phyrexian Beast Token" with no attack marked, and the combat damage step shows no combat at all. This is the "blocker with no attack" class of bug CLAUDE.md records as fixed. (3) labelOrd() doesn't recognise the label and returns 12 (end of turn), so every shim read (battlefield, hands, taps) jumps to Skrat's END-of-turn state at the untap step. Squirrel Token 1030, created in MAIN2 by Chatter of the Squirrel, is already on the table during declare attackers (DOM: "Squirrel Token 1T 2" at event 846).
findings.why_it_hurts: It breaks the decisive combat of the game the playtester reported, and it makes the board lie on a shim run, which the honesty note calls exact. Possessive deck names are the norm in Commander ("Edgar's Vampires", "Yuriko's Ninjas"), so this will hit most imported decks. It violates both system status visibility and the project's own board-honesty invariant.
findings.recommendation: Parse phases against the known player list, not a regex. For each key in timeline.players, test raw.startsWith(stripAi(key)+"'s ") or +"' ", longest name first, and take the rest as the label. Do the same in engine/forge_log_adapter.py if it parses phases. Add a fixture test using "Skrat's Revenge", and re-run the board.py accuracy check on a shim result.

findings.where: replay/1 of sim_20260925_003803, events 885-980. web/lib/replay.ts:468-477 (poison is added up but never eliminates) and page.tsx:341 (decidingIdx = start of the last turn)
findings.what_happens: At event 885 (round 9, Skrat's turn) Krenko shows "18 life · 12 on board · 46 poison" and Stella "· 19 poison". Both stay at full opacity, cards on the table, for the next 95 events, including Kess's whole turn 35 that they never took. Forge logs the "has lost" lines as a batch at game end, so the final frame labels both "Out round 10", but they died in round 9. "Jump to the deciding turn" goes to event 914 (round 10, Skrat's untap). The decisive Triumph of the Hordes (event 840) and the infect alpha strike (844-885) are 30 to 74 events earlier, and nothing at the landing point says so. Reaching that swing from the lede took me about 20 inputs (Jump, then shift+left twice, then 9 to 14 arrow presses), and only because I had read the raw JSON first.
findings.why_it_hurts: "How did it end" and "what was the turning point" are the two questions a replay exists to answer, and here both answers are wrong: dead players look alive, and the one shortcut to the turning point overshoots it. That breaks match between system and real world: at a real table, 10 poison means you are gone.
findings.recommendation: In the fold, eliminate a seat when poison reaches 10 or more (and when commander damage from one commander reaches 21, see RV-10), stamped with that step's round. Grey the seat out with the DS 'out' shape. Compute the deciding moment as the step where the eventual winner's last opponent became doomed: the first step of the largest single-turn swing that took an opponent from alive to lethal (life to 0 or less, poison to 10 or more). Land on the cast or attack that started it (here, event 840 Triumph of the Hordes), not on a turn boundary. Label it "Watch the swing: Triumph of the Hordes, round 9".

findings.where: page.tsx:21 (SPEED_MS 300/150/75 per event), page.tsx:208-213 (fixed-interval playback clock), event composition of every payload
findings.what_happens: Phase markers and mana taps make up 60.5% of game 1's steps (464 phase + 129 mana of 980), 64% of game 4's (1,106 of 1,724) and 58% of the Drana game's. Playback gives every step the same 300ms. "Krenko Goblins' End step", "Cleanup step", "Untap step", "Upkeep step" and "Bojuka Bog - {T}: Add {B}." each hold the screen exactly as long as "Krenko Goblins cast Ruby Medallion". At 1x a game runs 4.9 to 8.6 minutes, most of it dead air. At 4x (75ms per step) spells flash past too fast to read. There is no per-turn or highlights mode.
findings.why_it_hurts: The viewer's attention goes into the gaps, not the plays. That violates aesthetic and minimalist design (every extra unit of information competes with the relevant ones) and respect for the user's time. Nobody watches a whole replay at that pace, so the product's centrepiece mostly goes unwatched.
findings.recommendation: Classify steps into tiers when building the timeline. Tier 0: phase, mana, player_control, match_result, replacement text. Tier 1: land, cast, resolve, trigger. Tier 2: attack, block, damage, life change, zone exits of nonland permanents. Tier 3: elimination, commander cast, board wipe (3 or more permanents leaving in one phase), the lethal swing. Playback skips tier 0 and holds each step by tier (e.g. 250/600/900/1500ms at 1x). Offer three modes in place of the speed select: Highlights (tier 2 and up), Turn by turn (pause at each turn's summary), Every event. Arrow keys step visible steps only; alt+arrow steps raw events for the curious.

findings.where: Theater layout, globals.css:611 (.stage 1fr 330px, gap 40px), .page max-width 1280. Measured at 1440x900 and 375x812
findings.what_happens: At 1440x900 the stage begins at y=358. Mid-game the theater is 1,061px tall, so with its top at the top of the viewport the transport bar sits at y=1,025: you can see either the top seats or the controls, never both. The table gets 826 of 1,440px wide, while the 330px log column and margins take the rest. On a phone the four seats stack to 1,366px, the transport starts at page y=2,063 and the log at y=2,347. Tapping step changes a seat 1,500px above, off screen.
findings.why_it_hurts: Watching is a feedback loop: act, then see the result. When the control and its effect can't be on screen together, the loop breaks, and the viewer's working memory has to hold the board while they scroll (visibility of system status, Fitts's law). The Moxfield and Archidekt playtesters and 17lands' replay all give the board the full viewport and pin the transport.
findings.recommendation: Make the replay a full-bleed theater: drop the 1280 cap on this route, let the table take min(100vh minus 120px, content), and collapse the title and lede into a one-line header strip (matchup, winner chip, rounds). Pin the transport bar to the bottom of the viewport (position: sticky; bottom: 0) at every width. Put the log in a right drawer at 1440 or wider and a bottom sheet on phones. On phones, show one seat at a time (the active seat by default) with a four-avatar switcher strip, rather than four stacked seats.

findings.where: Tabletop.tsx:79 (Tile uses a native title tooltip), globals.css:644 (.tc 46x64), :664 and :688 (hand and lands 30x42). components/CardPreview.tsx is used only in app/decks/[file]/page.tsx:82 and app/playtest/[deck]/page.tsx:78
findings.what_happens: Battlefield cards render Scryfall 'small' images at 46x64 and hands and lands at 30x42, so names and text are illegible and art is barely recognisable. Hovering a card gives a delayed OS tooltip of plain text (name, type, cost, oracle). The table contains zero focusable elements (querySelectorAll('.tbl [tabindex], button, a') = 0), so keyboard and touch users cannot inspect any card. The app already has a full-size preview (useCardPreview: hover, focus and press-and-hold) on /decks and /playtest, but the replay, the centrepiece, doesn't use it. 17lands renders battlefield cards at 71x99 with P/T and status overlays.
findings.why_it_hurts: In Magic the card is the unit of meaning. A viewer who can't read Hullbreaker Horror can't follow why the game turned. It fails recognition over recall, inconsistency between pages erodes trust, and it fails WCAG 2.1.1 (keyboard) for the core content.
findings.recommendation: Render each Tile as a <button> bound to useCardPreview (the hook is input-parity ready), giving hover, focus with Escape to dismiss, and long-press on touch. Raise battlefield tiles to 63x88 at 1440 (mind the table width once RV-04 lands), use the Scryfall 'normal' image when a tile is 60px or wider, and add a name ribbon for cards under 60px. Hovering a bolded name in the log should highlight the matching tile (outline pulse) and vice versa.

findings.where: Payload fields game.agent_events and game.rubric: present in every shim result, referenced nowhere in web/ (grep: only DeckScorecards touches timedOut)
findings.what_happens: Game 1 has 37 agent_events recording the AI's actual reasoning: "finisher_hold Triumph of the Hordes creatures=1 need=3 instead=Elven Chorus" (turns 14 and 18); "kingmaker_reaim moved=2 onto=Skrat's Revenge leaderThreat=8"; "counter_veto Crackle with Power threat=4.0"; "tutor_steer steer=Hullbreaker Horror over=Blasphemous Act"; "counter_fire Finale of Devastation"; and the mulligan reasons. The rubric records per-combat block quality (freeMissed, safeMissed, legalMissed, lifeTaken) and mulligans (Skrat's mulled to 6, kept 3 lands). None of this appears in the replay.
findings.why_it_hurts: "Why did that player do that?" is the question this product is uniquely placed to answer: no other Magic tool has the pilot's reasons. It's also exactly the evidence an investor would want to see the model producing. Leaving it in the payload wastes the product's main differentiator.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Reasoning' layer. Place each agent_event as an inline, visually distinct row in the log at its turn and phase (e.g. violet-ink left rule: "Skrat's held Triumph of the Hordes: 1 creature, wants 3"), and as a small marker on the scrubber. Translate the event codes into plain English in lib/replay.ts (finisher_hold, kingmaker_reaim, counter_veto, tutor_steer, instant_hold, block_skip). Surface rubric misplays on the seat during that combat ("left 1 safe block unmade, took 4"). A 'Show AI reasoning' toggle lets a purist hide it.

findings.where: Tabletop.tsx renders only Battlefield and Hand. replay.ts:545 computes BoardState.stack but no component reads it. The zone stream carries Graveyard, Exile, Command and Library moves (game 1: 22 Battlefield→Graveyard, 64 moves to graveyard or exile, Command→Stack ×3)
findings.what_happens: Kess Reanimator's whole plan is its graveyard (Entomb, Unmarked Grave, Exhume), and the viewer can't see a graveyard, exile or library count at all. The commander isn't shown in the command zone, isn't badged when on the battlefield, and has no tax. When Kess casts Chaos Warp on a Beast token the table shows nothing: the stack exists only as a log line. 17lands shows library, graveyard and exile counts on every player plate plus a dedicated Stack row, and MTGO and Arena both render the stack.
findings.why_it_hurts: Hidden state that decides games breaks the viewer's mental model. A player sees Exhume resolve and can't tell what came back or why. In Commander the command zone and graveyard are first-class zones, so leaving them out is a mismatch with the real world.
findings.recommendation: Add a zone rail to each seat plate: library, graveyard, exile, command, each as a count, opening a popover with the actual cards (read from the zone stream with the same atPlayhead cutoff). Mark the commander tile with a small crown glyph (inline SVG, not a WotC symbol) and show "cast 2× · tax {4}" from the Command→Stack records. Render a centre-table stack lane whenever the stack is non-empty: item card, caster seat colour, and "→ target" parsed from Forge's "targeting [X (id)]".

findings.where: page.tsx:344 (phaseLabel has no player name), Tabletop.tsx:200 ('· active' em), globals.css:630 (.parea.act background rgba(0,229,255,0.045)), Tabletop.tsx:123-124 and :181 (seats placed in array order into a 2-column grid)
findings.what_happens: The only place the active player is named is a 12px grey '· active' beside one name, plus a 4.5%-alpha tint that is effectively invisible on the backdrop. The theater header says "Round 8 · untap" with no player. There's no phase ladder, so I can't see where in the turn we are relative to combat. game.players is turn order, and the grid fills TL, TR, BL, BR, so turn passes in a Z: from the top-right seat diagonally to the bottom-left, then right, then diagonally back up. At a real table turn passes clockwise.
findings.why_it_hurts: "Whose turn, which phase" should take zero effort to read. A Z-shaped rotation makes "who's next" (and so who is exposed on the crack-back) a mental calculation. That fails mapping and the conventions every Commander player carries from the physical table and from SpellTable's four-quadrant layout.
findings.recommendation: Seat clockwise: TL = seat 1, TR = 2, BR = 3, BL = 4 (grid-area per index; bottom seats keep the reversed 'near' flex). Give the active seat a 2px cyan frame, the one sanctioned glow for live activity, and dim the rest to about 0.85. Replace the text label with a compact phase ladder in the theater header (Beginning · Main 1 · Combat [attackers · blockers · damage] · Main 2 · End), current step filled, prefixed with the active player's avatar and name: "Skrat's Revenge · Round 9 · Declare blockers".

findings.where: Tabletop.tsx:236-253 (combat banners), globals.css:650 and :690 (.tc.atk and .atkbanner use --state-failed)
findings.what_happens: Skrat's split attack renders as text: "Phyrexian Beast Token + Phyrexian Beast Token + … (×10) attacking Krenko →", five wrapped lines of the same name. Every banner ends in a right-pointing "→" whether the defender is below (Krenko) or diagonally down-left (Stella). The attackers get a red border, but nothing links an attacker to its defender or a blocker to what it blocks except text. Attack red is --state-failed, which DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §3 reserves for the failed status ("a colour never means two things"), and it sits next to the red WUBRG pip, a data colour.
findings.why_it_hurts: Combat is where Commander games are decided, and a four-player split attack is the hardest thing to read at a real table, let alone in text. Pre-attentive cues (lines, grouping, count) beat parsing strings. The colour overload breaks the design system's own rule.
findings.recommendation: Collapse duplicates in banners ("10× Phyrexian Beast Token (4/4) → Krenko"). Draw an SVG overlay of attack arrows from the attacking seat's creature band to the defender's plate, one per lane, stroke width scaled to power, and blocker connector lines from blocker tile to attacker tile. Give combat its own token (e.g. --combat-attack, a warm amber not used elsewhere) and keep violet for blocks, or propose the token change to the owner with this evidence.

findings.where: Tabletop.tsx:209-213 (pnums), replay.ts:122-133 (no commander-damage op), replay.ts:873 (commanderGuess)
findings.what_happens: Life is 14px mono at the same visual weight as "· 8 on board" (a count that includes lands). Poison appears as trailing text only when greater than 0. There is no delta flash, so a 35 to -10 swing just silently changes a number. Commander damage isn't tracked, though every commander's name is in the zone stream (Command→Stack records: Krenko, Mob Boss; Kess, Dissident Mage; Drana, Liberator of Malakir) and summarizeGame already recognises "damage from generals" losses.
findings.why_it_hurts: Life totals are the scoreboard, and "who is winning" should be answerable at a glance. Commander damage (21) is a Commander-specific loss condition every player tracks, and SpellTable and every life-counter app surface it. Leaving it out reads as not knowing the format.
findings.recommendation: Make life the largest numeral on each plate (about 28px JetBrains Mono), with poison and commander damage as small counters beside it that appear only when non-zero and turn to the warning ink at 7 poison and 15 commander damage. Animate a ±delta chip for about 900ms on life changes (reduced-motion: static). Track commander damage by matching damage-event sources against the Command→Stack names, and show a per-seat popover matrix. Replace 'on board' with creature count and total power, the numbers a player actually reads the threat from.

findings.where: page.tsx:342-343 (only idx±40 rows rendered), :504-520 (rows have no click handler), globals.css:734 (.ev.cur margin 0 -10px). Engine strings are shown verbatim
findings.what_happens: Clicking a log row does nothing (verified: event counter unchanged, cursor: auto). Only 81 rows exist at a time, so the log can't be browsed to find a moment. There are no turn headers, no filters (e.g. just Kess, just combat, hide phases) and no player colour. Rows show raw Forge output: "Life: Kambal Taxes B3 50 > 47", "Ruby Medallion" (a bare resolve line), Ledger Shredder's full oracle text followed by "[Card: Chatter of the Squirrel, Activator: Skrat's Revenge, SpellAbility: Create a 1/1 green Squirrel creature token.]", "receives 46 poison counter", four "has restored control over themself" lines, "Turn 18" (a third numbering alongside round 10 and the results table's T36), and a match-score line "Kess, Reanimator: 0 Skrat's Revenge: 1 …". The current-row negative margin makes the list 325px wide inside a 315px box, so a horizontal scrollbar jitters as the playhead moves. Only the first of ten repeated card names in a row is bolded.
findings.why_it_hurts: The log is the authoritative record, per the page's own note, yet it isn't navigable and reads like stdout. Lichess and chess.com move lists, and HSReplay's play log, are the primary way to navigate precisely because they're clickable. Raw engine strings are the strongest 'made by a script' signal on the page.
findings.recommendation: Virtualise the full log (react-window, or a simple windowed list keyed to scrollTop), make every row a button that seeks to it, and group rows under sticky turn headers ("Round 9 · Skrat's Revenge" with avatar). Add filter chips: Key plays, Combat, a per-player filter, All. Rewrite strings in lib/replay.ts: life → "Kambal 50 → 47 (−3)"; resolve → "Ruby Medallion resolves"; strip Forge's [Card:… SpellAbility:…] suffix; drop player_control and match_result; make "Turn 18" a game-over row. Fix the overflow with padding-inline plus box-shadow instead of negative margins, and bold every occurrence of a name.

findings.where: page.tsx:456-477 (.scrub is a div with onClick only), :229-248 (keyboard), :260-269 (copy link); URL never updated
findings.what_happens: The scrubber is a click target, not a slider: dragging gives no live feedback and the board only updates on release (dragged from x=472 to 673 and it landed on event 659). It has no role, tabindex, aria-valuenow or hover readout of where you'd land. Its only markers are round ticks (R2…R10). Keyboard: space and ←/→ step, shift+← → jumps a turn; j, k, l, Home, End, '.' and '?' do nothing (tested). The address bar never tracks the playhead, so reloading or sharing the URL loses your place, hence the separate 'Copy link at this event' button. 17lands rewrites the URL on every step (…/3/2/29).
findings.why_it_hurts: Scrubbing is how people find the moment they're after. Without drag feedback or markers it becomes trial and error, and it fails keyboard access (WCAG 2.1.1, 4.1.2). The j/k and Home/End conventions from lichess, YouTube and every video player go unrecognised.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild the scrubber as role="slider" with pointer-capture drag (seek on pointermove, throttled to rAF), a hover tooltip ("Round 7 · Kess · Combat"), and ←/→/PageUp/PageDown/Home/End when focused. Add key-moment markers (RV-02, RV-03 tier 3, agent_events) and colour each turn segment by active seat, as 17lands does with per-player lanes. Add j/k, Home/End, and '?' for a shortcut sheet. history.replaceState(?t=) on pause and seek (not on every playback tick), and keep 'Copy link' as a convenience.

findings.where: lib/format.ts:10-15 (shortName), lib/replay.ts:873-888 (commanderGuess), format.ts:104 (scryfallArt hits api.scryfall.com per seat)
findings.what_happens: Seat plates and the back link read "Kess," (trailing comma) and "Skrat's" (a bare possessive). Skrat's Revenge and Nekusar Punisher B3 get no avatar and no colour pips because commanderGuess matches the first word of the deck name against cast spells. Skrat's commander was never cast in game 1, and "Nekusar Punisher" 404s at Scryfall. Version suffixes leak into copy ("Kambal Taxes B3", "Atraxa Counters B3"). Every replay load makes four single-card requests to api.scryfall.com for avatars.
findings.why_it_hurts: Seat identity is the anchor for everything else on the table. A stray comma and a missing avatar look careless, the opposite of 'a human took care'. Single lookups also run against the repo's own Scryfall etiquette.
findings.recommendation: Have the engine put each deck's commander name(s) (from the .dck [Commander] section) in the game payload, and drive the avatar, pips and commander badge from that. Fall back to Command→Stack zone records, and never to the first word of the deck name. Label seats with the commander's short name ("Kess", "Krenko", "Stella"), trimming punctuation, and show the deck name as the subtitle. Batch the avatar art through the existing cards.ts collection cache (art_crop URLs from the facts) rather than api.scryfall.com/cards/named.

findings.where: replay/6 (draw): page.tsx:358 (fmtClock with an undefined durationMs), :368-386 (lede), final frame of every replay
findings.what_happens: The draw's header reads "10 rounds · NaN:NaN". The lede says only "This game ended in a draw after 10 rounds", though result.timedOut is true (the 900s clock cut it off, and Skrat's was already dead), and it still offers "Jump to the deciding turn". Every game's final frame is just the last log line (a match-score string). There is no end-of-game card with final lives, who eliminated whom and in which round, or the card that killed them.
findings.why_it_hurts: The ending is the payoff of a replay and the moment most viewers arrive at, via the deciding-turn link. NaN on screen is a trust-killer for the investor audience. An unexplained draw invites the wrong conclusion about the deck (the honesty principle in SIM_CALIBRATION.md).
findings.recommendation: Guard the clock (show an en dash when duration is missing). For draws, say why: "Cut off by the 15-minute game clock in round 10 with Stella (33), Krenko (17) and Kess (8) still alive" from result.timedOut, turnCapped and seats, and hide the deciding-turn link. On the last step, overlay a glass end card on the table: winner avatar, elimination order with rounds and causes, the killing card image, and 'Watch the swing' / 'Next game' buttons.

findings.where: page.tsx:271-274 (tabs), app/layout.tsx:9 (one static title), results/[file]/page.tsx:702 (T{g.endedTurn})
findings.what_happens: There's no previous/next game control inside the replay: moving from game 1 to game 2 means going back to the overview table. The tab bar changes when you enter a replay (Overview | Replay) and loses Telemetry and Coaching. Every replay's document title is "Arcane Sim Lab", so eight open games are indistinguishable in tabs and history. The results table lists games as "T36" (Forge player-turns) while the replay they open says "10 rounds".
findings.why_it_hurts: Comparing games is the analyst's core loop ("does Kess always win the same way?"). Navigation that shifts under you breaks consistency and standards, and two numbering systems for the same game force a translation every time.
findings.recommendation: Add a game switcher strip in the replay header: chips 1–8, each with the winner's avatar and a filled square for win or hollow for draw, plus [ and ] shortcuts. Keep the run's tab set constant and show Replay as a sub-state of Overview. Set document.title to "Game 1 · Skrat's Revenge wins R10 · Sim Lab". Change the results table to R{endedRound}.

findings.where: Tabletop.tsx:97-103 (BAND, BAND_LABEL, BAND_CAP), :84-86 (token tiles without art), globals.css:655 (tapped rotation also rotates .nm text)
findings.what_happens: The creature band has no label and sits directly below "Artifacts, enchantments and unidentified", so by proximity the label seems to head the creatures too. That clumsy label appears on all four seats. Tokens have no Scryfall face, so Skrat's 10 Phyrexian Beast Tokens and 2 Squirrels render as dark 46x64 boxes with 10px names, and once tapped the name rotates 90° with the tile and becomes unreadable ("Phyr exia n Beast"). Overflow past 18 creature tiles becomes dead "+N" text.
findings.why_it_hurts: Tokens are how Commander boards win (Skrat's won with them), yet they're the least legible objects on the table. Mis-grouped labels violate the Gestalt proximity principle.
findings.recommendation: Label every band briefly and consistently (Creatures · Other permanents · Lands) or drop labels and separate bands with a hairline. Design a token tile: big P/T numeral, the name on a ribbon that doesn't rotate (rotate only the frame for tapped, or use a 'T' corner chip as for partial taps), creature type underneath, count badge. Make "+N" a button that expands the band.

strengths: The honesty note is path-aware (Tabletop.tsx:298-317): it says 'read from the zone stream' on shim runs and 'reconstructed' on stock runs instead of one blanket disclaimer. Keep it. (But see slop signals: page.tsx:492 then contradicts it.)
Rounds are counted per active player (replay.ts:84-92), not Forge's player-turn counter, which is how a table counts. Just finish the job on the results table (T36).

Combat is modelled correctly for non-apostrophe decks: one lane per defender, and blocks attributed to the blocking player. In the Drana game, the Kalitas + Drana split attack on Kambal and Nighthawk on Atraxa kept both banners and the Gray Merchant block through first-strike damage.
Exact hands for all four seats, read from the shim, are something no Arena or MTGO replay can show. It's a real differentiator once cards are legible.

Duplicates collapse into count tiles with partial-tap chips ("1T"), Forge's +N/+N counter wording, and token copies kept separate from originals. These are the right semantics for Commander token boards.
Deep links (?t=) and 'Copy link at this event' already exist; ambiguous-id disambiguation (replay.ts:192) keeps two same-named Lightning Runners distinct in the log.
It fetches one game at a time, and the lede opens with a computed prose sentence naming the winner, the round and the method.
Mobile basics were addressed in the last UX pass: single-column seats, keyboard hints hidden on coarse pointers, full-width scrubber.
slop_signals: The layout is a reskinned SaaS dashboard wireframe. mockups/simlab_v3_replay.html uses the Vercel palette (#0A0A0A, #EDEDED, Geist Mono) and `.stage{grid-template-columns:1fr 330px;gap:40px}`, copied verbatim into globals.css:611. The card game is a boxed widget inside a deploy-log page rather than a table you sit at.
The H1 is "Game 1" and the primary position readout is "event 846 of 980" (page.tsx:405-407), a developer's unit. No Magic player thinks in events.

Raw Forge strings in the log: "Life: Kambal Taxes B3 50 > 47", "[Card: Chatter of the Squirrel, Activator: Skrat's Revenge, SpellAbility: …]", "has restored control over themself" ×4, "Turn 18", "receives 46 poison counter", and a trailing match-score line.

Three stacked disclaimers under the table: the tblnote, the keyboard note, and page.tsx:492-495. On shim runs the last one ('Replays fold the event log into board state locally') contradicts the tblnote just above it ('read from the zone stream'), which is exactly the honesty error the TabletopNote comment warns about.
The same action appears twice with different verbs: 'Jump to the deciding turn' (page.tsx:385) and 'Skip to the deciding turn' (page.tsx:531).
Decorative '→' glyphs on every attack banner, pointing right regardless of where the defender sits (Tabletop.tsx:241-242).
The band label 'Artifacts, enchantments and unidentified' is repeated four times per frame, and the attack wall 'Phyrexian Beast Token + Phyrexian Beast Token + …' repeats one name ten times.
"Kess," with a trailing comma in the seat plate and back link, and 'NaN:NaN' in the draw header. Small errors like these read as 'no human looked at it'.
Meta captions like 'follows the playhead' and '· active' in grey em text, where a designed state treatment belongs.
craft_opportunities: A life race chart under the scrubber (four seat-coloured lines across rounds, poison dashed), clickable to seek, like lichess's evaluation graph. The turning point becomes visible as the moment the lines split, and it answers 'who is winning' at any playhead.

One-line turn narration at each turn boundary, computed from events: "Round 9, Skrat's: Triumph of the Hordes, swung 15 infect at Stella and Krenko; Krenko chumped 2; Stella 19 poison, Krenko 46. Both out." Turn-by-turn mode just pages through these.

AI reasoning chips from agent_events, in Commander-player language: "Held Triumph of the Hordes (1 creature, wants 3)", "Stella re-aimed at Skrat's: the table leader", "Kess let Crackle with Power resolve (threat too low to counter)".
A commander crown badge on the battlefield tile, and a command-zone chip showing "cast 2× · tax {4}" from Command→Stack records, drawn as inline SVG, never WotC symbols.
A per-seat commander damage matrix popover (SpellTable style), and 10-poison / 21-commander thresholds that flip a seat to 'out' with its round and cause.
Mulligan theatre in pregame from the rubric: "Skrat's mulled to 6: first seven had 1 land", with the kept hand fanned at readable size.
The graveyard as a first-class zone for reanimator decks: when Exhume resolves, briefly trace the returning card from the graveyard chip to the battlefield.
A 'Watch highlights' mode that auto-pauses a beat on each tier-3 moment and skips phases, so an 8-minute game becomes a 60-second story.
A token tile designed by someone who plays: big P/T, a creature-type ribbon, a count badge, and a name that doesn't rotate when tapped.

An end-of-game card: final lives, elimination order with rounds and causes, the killing blow at full size, and 'Watch the swing' / 'Next game'. Magic players screenshot this kind of card and share it.

walkthroughs.first_impression: The first ten seconds look like a generic AI SaaS landing page with a Magic skin. You see a Midjourney-style fantasy backdrop, a cute brass robot, a Cinzel wordmark, a four-cell stat strip that counts up from zero, and a chatbot greeting ("What would you like to do today?"). Nothing Magic-specific appears until you scroll. A Commander player spots the tells quickly: mana symbols used as decoration beside "decks" and "games simulated"; floating hedrons (Zendikar imagery) that the spec calls Dominaria; run titles like "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal". Past the front door every page becomes a dense grey-on-navy terminal. Half the text is monospace at 12-13px and one page uses 15 font sizes, so the fantasy shell and the data inside feel like two different products. The data-driven opening sentences and the honesty notes are the most human thing here, and they are genuinely good. The playtest sandbox is a thin prototype next to Moxfield's and Archidekt's goldfish tools.

findings.where: / (home) on first load, seen at 375px. web/app/page.tsx: useTally starts at 0 (line ~36); data panel checks `!view || view.top.length === 0` (line 297) and `!view || view.recent.length === 0` (line 395)
findings.what_happens: While data is still loading, the home page claims "0 decks on this engine", "0 games simulated", "0 finished runs" and "No finished runs yet. Run a gauntlet and the leaderboard builds itself." The link reads "All –". Right beside it the recent-sims header says "loading…" over the empty-state line "Finished runs land here." About a second later it jumps to 43 / 317 / 46 and a full leaderboard.
findings.why_it_hurts: The loading state tells a returning player, with 46 runs on record, that they have nothing. Loading, empty and error are three different states and here they share one rendering (Nielsen #1, visibility of system status). The page also contradicts itself: "loading…" sits next to "No finished runs yet." First screens that show false zeros read as broken.
findings.recommendation: Handle three states everywhere: null means loading, [] means empty, a thrown error means error. While loading, the tally shows an en dash (not 0) and the panel shows 5 skeleton rows at the real row height (64px deck rows, 2-line sim rows). Only start the count-up once the value exists, or drop the count-up (see CC-04). Show the empty-state sentence only when the fetch succeeded with zero rows.

findings.where: / home line under the hub, `hub-est` at web/app/page.tsx:283. /new estimate from web/lib/format.ts:118 `SECONDS_PER_GAME = {2: 2.5, 3: 11, 4: 52}`. Engine constant: engine/mtg_engine.py:556 `TYPICAL_GAME_SECONDS = 240`
findings.what_happens: Home promises "two decks ≈ 5 s a game · four decks ≈ 8 min for 16". The /new estimator uses 52 s per 4-player game. The engine's own re-measured figure is 240 s per game, which CLAUDE.md turns into 40-105 min for a 4-deck, 16-game gauntlet. The home line is also 12px mono in the floor grey, sitting on bare backdrop art (visibly over the lightning at 375px).
findings.why_it_hurts: The one number that sets expectations before an expensive action is wrong by 5-10x. A user who expects 8 minutes comes back to a run at 10% and concludes it is broken. It breaks the project's own honesty invariants (timing numbers are not interchangeable) and design law 2 (no text on unscrimmed art). Match between system and the real world fails.
findings.recommendation: Take the estimate from one source: expose the engine's estimate_sim_seconds on an API route (or mirror TYPICAL_GAME_SECONDS and the startup term in format.ts with a test that pins them together). Say it as a range in plain words: "Four decks, 16 games: usually 40 to 100 minutes. You can close this tab." Move it off the home art and onto /new under the primary, where the decision is made.

findings.where: /results/[file]/coaching primary; /rules "Ask" primary (web/app/rules/page.tsx:209, which never reads the `llm` flag that api.health() returns, lib/api.ts:125); engine-down copy on / and /playtest (ENGINE_CMD, "Start it with python3 engine/mtg_engine.py serve 8484"); mobile nav sheet (Chrome.tsx:136, ApiBaseSetting)
findings.what_happens: Coaching shows a glowing primary, "GENERATE COACHING REPORT (~$0.01, ABOUT 20 S)". Directly under it: "the button above will fail. Set MTG_LLM_API_KEY in deploy/.env and redeploy to enable it." On /rules the uppercase "ASK" primary leads to paid generation that production cannot do, and the free, working path ("Search the rules instead") is styled as secondary. The phone nav sheet shows "Engine /engine  Change" to every visitor, and the engine-down states tell end users to run a Python command.
findings.why_it_hurts: The most prominent control on two pages is known to fail, and the page says so. This is the literal reading of "never disable the primary" gone wrong. Environment variables, deploy paths, per-call dollar costs and an engine-address editor are operator tools leaking into a consumer product. That is the strongest possible signal that nobody walked the page as a user. It fails error prevention and match with the real world, and it breaks the one-primary rule because the primary does not do the page's job.
findings.recommendation: Gate on health().llm. When it is false: on /rules, make "Search the rules" the single primary and remove Ask, or show one quiet line ("Written answers are not switched on yet; search is"). On coaching, show a static sample report or hide the tab, and state it in user language. Put all ops copy (env vars, $ per call, engine commands, ApiBaseSetting) behind a dev-only flag (process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' or a ?debug query), never in the production nav.

findings.where: Global visual language: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §0/§6/§11; globals.css --atmosphere-leylines (lines 23-26), .action-btn--violet/--blue gradients (430-439), .tally, .masthead; home page composition
findings.what_happens: The Arcane skin hits at least 5 of the 10 "AI tells" in the project's own research doc (mockups/design_principles.md Part 1): #2 glassmorphism, violet gradients and aurora glows (the cyan and violet radial "leyline" glows under the art, the gradient-filled hub buttons); #3 a stat strip with an icon in each cell (the tally); #8 Space Grotesk; #9 a centred hero (mascot, wordmark, question); #6 all-caps labels on every CTA. Add the chatbot opener "What would you like to do today?", art generated from a prompt that ships in the spec ("--ar 16:9 --v 6.0"), and a robot mascot, which literally signals "made by AI".
findings.why_it_hurts: The owner's brief is "not AI slop", and his own doc says a page reading 4 or more of these tells gets flagged instantly. The fantasy shell costs attention and first impressions but holds no information. Every data page then drops to plain grey-on-navy, so the brand promise and the product disagree. Aesthetic-usability works in reverse here: the polish reads as template polish.
findings.recommendation: Keep one signature brand moment and make the data interior the craft. (1) Remove --atmosphere-leylines and the violet and blue gradient fills; hub buttons become a single primary plus text links. (2) Replace the home hub and tally with a content-first home. Open with a computed sentence ("Your last gauntlet: Kess won 4 of 8 (50%; 25% is an even share). Skrat's Revenge hasn't been tested since you edited it."). Then your decks as commander-art rows showing last result against baseline, and the latest run with a Resume replay link. One primary: Run a gauntlet. (3) Drop the count-up animation. (4) Keep the mascot at masthead size on the home page only. (5) Sentence-case every CTA. Take the plan to the owner as a design-system change, with the design_principles audit as evidence.

findings.where: / tally banner: web/app/page.tsx:108-111 (BADGE_SUN = W pip for "decks", WATER = U for "games simulated", FIRE = R for "finished runs", COMBO = C for "rules loaded"); sanctioned in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §6 "Rolling tally banner"
findings.what_happens: Painted mana medallions are used as ornamental icons beside counts that have nothing to do with colour.
findings.why_it_hurts: This breaks law 3 in the design system's own §0: "WUBRG is data; a colour never means two things." To a Magic player a white mana symbol beside "43 decks" reads as "43 white decks", and a red one beside "46 finished runs" reads as red decks. It tells an expert that the designer does not think in colour identity.
findings.recommendation: Remove the pips from the tally. If the tally survives CC-04, give it neutral stroke glyphs or no icon at all. Reserve pips strictly for colour identity: gallery filter, deck headers, seat plates, and mana costs (see craft opportunities).

findings.where: web/app/globals.css type declarations throughout; results page as measured
findings.what_happens: globals.css has 136 font-size declarations covering 18 distinct sizes (8.5, 9, 9.5, 10, 10.5, 11, 11.5, 12, 12.5, 13, 13.5, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 23, 26 px). The --size-* tokens are used 9 times in total. The results page renders 15 distinct computed sizes, including 10.695, 12.09, 12.555 and 13.02 px, produced by `.mono { font-size: 0.93em }` compounding. 301 of its 628 text nodes (48%) are JetBrains Mono, including words like "round 10" and "combat damage" in the scorecards. Body copy is 13px against a 15px spec; h1 is 26px while the --size-h1 token (34px) goes unused. Nine declarations sit below 11px (replay tile names 10px, .tc .tpn 9px, .tc .att 8.5px, scorecard labels .scl 10.5px).
findings.why_it_hurts: Without a scale, hierarchy flattens into a fog of near-identical small grey text. 482 of the 628 text nodes on the results page render in --ink-3 or --ink-4, against 97 in --ink-1 or white. Half the page in monospace reads as a terminal log, not an analysis written by a person. Sub-11px text is unreadable at arm's length. This is the "jank" the owner feels without naming it.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to a 6-step ramp tied to tokens: 12 (meta), 13 (data), 15 (body), 19 (section), 26 (page title), 34 (hero figure). Add a stylelint rule banning raw font-size px outside :root. Use mono only for numerals (`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` on the UI face covers most of that) and never for words. Delete the .93em mono scaling. Set a floor of 11px for any text, 12px for anything read rather than scanned. Give each page 2-3 values in --ink-1/white so the eye has somewhere to land.

findings.where: globals.css spacing throughout; /rules button row (.btns outside .head is display:block, gap normal)
findings.what_happens: The --sp-* scale is used 13 times, against about 290 raw px padding, margin and gap declarations taking 31 distinct values (1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15, 22, 26, 30, 34, 62 px among them). Visible result: on /rules the "ASK" and "Search the rules instead" buttons touch with zero gap (measured: the first ends at x=136.33, the second starts at x=136.33), at desktop and at 375px. They also mix cases in one row (ALL CAPS primary beside a sentence-case secondary).
findings.why_it_hurts: Off-scale spacing is what makes a layout feel slightly off everywhere without any single broken thing. Touching buttons read as a segmented control, or as a bug. Gestalt proximity breaks down.
findings.recommendation: Give .btns a global `display:flex; gap: var(--sp-2); flex-wrap: wrap`. Migrate padding, margin and gap to the --sp-* ramp (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64) and lint for raw px. Sentence-case .btn.pri (drop text-transform) so one row reads as one voice.

findings.where: --hairline-strong / --hairline used as the only edge of .btn, input.txt, .inp, .sel, textarea.paste, .pt-zone, .pt-mini (globals.css 386-396, 520-577, 906-908). Focus: input.txt:focus, textarea.paste:focus and .inp input set `outline: none` (lines 522, 574, 577)
findings.what_happens: Measured against the panel colour rgb(15,20,28): --hairline-strong gives 1.45:1 and --hairline 1.20:1. Secondary buttons, the rules question field, gallery search and selects are therefore barely distinguishable from the panel (the /rules input is a faint rectangle). On text inputs the promised 2px cyan ring at 2px offset is replaced by a 1px border colour change, because `input.txt:focus` (specificity 0,2,1) beats the global `:where(...):focus-visible` rule (0,1,0).
findings.why_it_hurts: DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §8 promises WCAG 1.4.11 (control edges ≥ 3:1) and 2.4.7 (a 2px ring on every focusable element). Both are broken on the controls people type into. Low-vision users cannot find the field, and keyboard users get a weak focus cue exactly where they type.
findings.recommendation: Add a --control-edge token at 3:1 or better against --bg-void (roughly rgba(148,163,184,0.55), or --ink-4 at 5:1) for every interactive boundary. Keep --hairline for decorative dividers only. Remove `outline: none` from input.txt, textarea.paste and .inp input so the global 2px ring applies; keep the cyan border as reinforcement.

findings.where: /playtest/[deck]. web/app/playtest/[deck]/page.tsx: drag-only zone moves (230-246); library pile div role=button with no tabIndex or key handler (452-461); nested buttons inside role=button card (280-315); globals.css `.pt-card:hover .cbtns` (920), .pt-mini 26px (906), .cbtns button 18px (921)
findings.what_happens: Tabbing reaches cards (the focus ring is visible) and Enter plays or taps them. But there is no keyboard or single-click way to send a permanent to the graveyard, exile, library or back to hand: that is drag-only, via HTML5 drag and drop. The library pile measured tabIndex -1, so a keyboard user cannot draw except through Next turn. Counter +/- buttons are display:none until mouse hover (not :focus-within), so keyboard users cannot add counters. The zoom and counter buttons are interactive elements nested inside an interactive role=button div. On desktop the counter buttons are 18px and the life +/- buttons 26px.
findings.why_it_hurts: This fails WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard and 2.5.7 Dragging Movements (AA in 2.2, which the design system claims), and 2.5.8 target size for the 18px buttons. It breaks the repo's own ui-review skill twice: hover-only actions, and nested interactives. On touch, drag between zones 600px apart (hand to graveyard at 375px) is effectively impossible, so on phones the sandbox is play-a-card and next-turn only.
findings.recommendation: Give every card one action menu: click or Enter opens a small popover (portaled, anchored, Escape to close) with Tap/Untap, To hand, To graveyard, To exile, To top of library, To bottom of library, Add counter, Remove counter. That matches Moxfield's "menus for all actions" alongside drag. Add keyboard shortcuts on the focused card and globally: D draw, M mulligan, N next turn, S shuffle, G/E/H/B zone moves, +/- counters, Ctrl+Z undo, ? shortcut sheet. Archidekt users already expect Shift+/ for its keybind sheet. Make the pile a real <button>. Controls at 44px (32px drawn with a grown hit area is fine).

findings.where: /playtest/[deck] feature set (page.tsx whole file: draw, mulligan, generic token, one generic counter, life, turn, reset)
findings.what_happens: Goldfishing Skrat's Revenge: the opening hand held Finale of Devastation and Nature's Rhythm (both tutors) plus Scurry of Squirrels, and the sandbox cannot resolve any of them. There is no search library, no look-at-top-N or scry, no mill, no standalone shuffle (only "Reset and reshuffle", which wipes the session with no confirmation), no undo. Tokens are all named "Token" with no type or P/T, in a squirrel-token deck. Counters are one untyped number. There is no commander tax or cast counter. The battlefield is one undifferentiated wrap of cards, lands mixed with creatures.
findings.why_it_hurts: The job of goldfishing is to find out whether the deck's opening turns function, and ramp and tutors are most of a Commander deck's opening turns. Archidekt lets you search the library with Scryfall syntax ("t:forest"), with keybinds for turn, library search, bottom-of-library and X tokens. Moxfield adds your deck's own tokens, counters, dice and card copies. An enfranchised player will open this once, compare, and go back to Moxfield.
findings.recommendation: All of these stay rules-free, because the user decides and the app only moves cards. In priority order: (1) Search library: a modal list with a name/type filter, pick a card and choose its destination, then an offered (never forced) shuffle. (2) Look at top N, sending each card to top, bottom or graveyard (covers scry, surveil and mill). (3) Shuffle library. (4) Undo stack (Ctrl+Z). (5) Named tokens drawn from the deck's Scryfall `all_parts` token list, as display data ("Squirrel 1/1"), with a quantity field. (6) Battlefield auto-sorted into rows by type line (lands / creatures / other), which is display typing CLAUDE.md allows. (7) +1/+1 and generic counter types. (8) A commander cast counter shown as "cast 2x" (a count, not tax enforcement). (9) Confirm on Reset.

findings.where: /playtest/[deck] layout; globals.css .pt-card 84px (913), .pt-zone, .pt-row; mobile 375px
findings.what_happens: Cards render 84px wide on a 1366px viewport: a 7-card hand uses 588 of 1286px, and card text is illegible without the hover preview. At 375px the library pile sits at y=1800 while the hand spans y=849-1252. Graveyard and exile are full-width 164px empty dashed boxes. On touch, every card, including hand and command-zone cards where counters mean nothing, carries three floating circles (+, −, magnifier) that cover the card's name bar and clip the zone label ("Hand (tap to play)" shows as "lay)"). The zone label "Battlefield (tap to tap)" is a pun on two meanings of tap. While images load, hand tiles are blank rectangles with no name.
findings.why_it_hurts: A playmat is spatial: your hand at your edge of the table, piles beside you, the board in front. Here every zone is a same-sized dashed box stacked in reading order, so the table metaphor, and the ability to see your whole state at once, is lost. That is especially true on a phone. Noise controls on every card cost more than they give.
findings.recommendation: Lay it out as a playmat. Battlefield fills the top (lands row and nonlands row); hand is docked at the bottom (sticky on mobile) with cards at 120-140px on desktop, overlapping fan-style when there are many. Library, graveyard, exile and command sit as piles in a right rail (a count plus the top card's face; click opens the list). Show counter controls only on battlefield cards, inside the per-card menu from CC-09 on touch. Relabel zones plainly ("Battlefield", "Hand"), with the interaction hint once in the lede. Show the card name until the image fires onLoad.

findings.where: /rules search results (HitList in web/app/rules/page.tsx:51-83, .sdesc styling globals.css:352)
findings.what_happens: Searching "Can my commander go back to the command zone when it dies?" returned 8 hits: 608.2b (targets), 601.2c, 123.6c (name stickers), 120.4d, 810.8a (Two-Headed Giant), 729.5 (subgames), 601.2b, 800.4a. None is 903.9a, the actual answer. Excerpts are cut mid-word with no ellipsis ("…each name st", "…the damage event s", "…can't lose the game. Ex"). The results render as .sdesc at --ink-4, 13px, so the page's payload sits in the floor grey. There is no quick way into section 903 (Commander).
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the most common Commander rules question, and the page's value proposition is grounded retrieval. Irrelevant hits in dim grey make the tool look broken to exactly the audience it serves. Truncation mid-word reads as a bug.
findings.recommendation: On the engine side, boost 903.* and glossary chunks for commander-zone and commander-damage vocabulary. Test a golden set of 20 common Commander questions and assert that 903.9a / 903.10a / 704.6c rank in the top 3. On the UI side, cut excerpts on sentence boundaries with an ellipsis; render hits at --ink-2, 15px, with the rule number as a mono heading; add a chip row under the field ("Commander 903", "State-based actions 704", "Layers 613", "Combat 506-511") that opens the rule panel directly. Drop the "Comprehensive Rules · June 2026" sub-line, which repeats the lede word for word.

findings.where: web/lib/format.ts runTitle/shortName (line 27ff). Seen on home recent sims, /results list, results H1, replay back link
findings.what_happens: Run titles are built from each deck name's first word: "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal", "The vs Atraxa vs Ant-Man vs Inspirit", "Living vs NanMan vs Kambal vs Kilo,", "Ur-Dragon vs Deadpool, vs Ant-Man vs Skrat's". While a replay loads, its back link shows the raw filename "‹ sim_20260907_232221_3819349fbfe4_rotated.json".
findings.why_it_hurts: This is the most repeated label in the product, and it has trailing commas and meaningless tokens ("The", "Power", "Living"). It is exactly the machine-made texture the owner is reacting to. The filename flash undoes the product's own rule that addresses belong only in the Details disclosure.
findings.recommendation: Build titles from commander names: take Scryfall's name up to the first comma and strip a leading "The" (Kess, Ur-Dragon, Stella Lee, Krenko). Never end a token in punctuation. Better still, show the pod as a stack of four commander art crops plus one line, "Kess won 4 of 8 · 4-deck pod". While the title loads, render a skeleton, never the filename.

findings.where: Nav (Chrome.tsx NAV), home hub labels (page.tsx:257-278), /new, /decks/[file] header, /import, sub-lines across pages
findings.what_happens: One destination goes by several names. Home says "SIM HISTORY & ANALYTICS" where the nav says "Results". "RUN NEW SIMULATION" = nav "Simulate" = /new H1 "Simulate" = button "RUN 16 GAMES" = deck page "USE IN A RUN" = lede "run the gauntlet". "EXPLORE DECKS" = nav "Decks". Internal words reach users ("SAVE DECK TO ENGINE", "Engine /engine", "~$0.01"). Casing changes by element: ALL-CAPS CTAs, sentence-case headings, lowercase fragment sub-lines ("one report per deck and gauntlet, cached", "goldfishing: you pilot everything…", "most run", "follows the playhead").
findings.why_it_hurts: Consistency and recognition over recall: a user following "Sim history & analytics" lands on a page called Results and has to re-map. Three casing regimes on one screen read as three authors. That is the committee-of-templates feel the owner dislikes.
findings.recommendation: Write a 10-word glossary and hold it everywhere: Run (a seat-rotated gauntlet of 2-4 decks), Game, Replay, Deck, Playtest. Hub labels = nav labels = H1s. Sentence case for every button ("Run 16 games", "Watch a winning game", "Save deck"). Sub-lines are full sentences or removed. No "engine", no dollar costs, no env vars in user copy.

findings.where: web/app/layout.tsx metadata (title: "Arcane Sim Lab" for every route); no <main> anywhere (0 landmarks measured); results games table ("Watch" x8); Chrome.tsx tabs nav
findings.what_happens: Every page, including each replay, has the document title "Arcane Sim Lab". There is no <main> landmark and no skip link. The Overview/Telemetry/Coaching sub-tab nav has no aria-current or label. On the results page, 8 links read just "Watch" with no accessible context, and each row's accessible text starts "#1#1" (the game number duplicated for a mobile-only span).
findings.why_it_hurts: WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled), 2.4.1 (Bypass Blocks) and 2.4.4 (Link Purpose). In practice, a player comparing game 1 and game 3 in two tabs cannot tell them apart, browser history is a list of identical entries, and screen-reader users hear "Watch, Watch, Watch".
findings.recommendation: Give each route a title via generateMetadata or document.title in client pages: "Game 3 · Drana vs Nekusar vs Kambal vs Atraxa · Sim Lab", "Skrat's Revenge playtest · Sim Lab". Wrap page content in <main id="content"> and add a visually hidden skip link. Add aria-current to .tab. Add aria-label="Watch game 3 (Kambal Taxes won, round 8)". Mark the mobile duplicate game number aria-hidden.

findings.where: /decks/kess_reanimator_305b76d7.dck, /new gallery, replay hand band (768px), /results/[file]/replay/[game] loading, CardPreview
findings.what_happens: While Scryfall facts load, the deck page lists all 99 cards under "Unidentified 99 cards", each tagged "type unresolved, not in the card cache yet", then re-sorts itself. /new tiles first show the no-art fallback plate (commander name in mono on grey), then pop to art. The replay's Hand (7) band shows 4-7 blank rectangles. The replay shows "Loading replay…" in an otherwise empty 700px panel.
findings.why_it_hurts: Loading dressed up as a data-quality problem ("Unidentified") erodes trust in the honesty labels that matter. Layout shift and art pop-in are the texture of an unfinished app. The design system specifies an Unidentified group for real unknowns, and this spends that signal on a spinner's job.
findings.recommendation: Give every data component a tri-state. Show skeletons sized like the final content (card rows at 48px thumbs, tiles at 16:10, the board grid with 4 seat plates). Never render "Unidentified" or the no-art plate until the facts fetch has settled. Fade art in on load. On the replay, show the card name on a tile until its image arrives.

findings.where: web/components/CardPreview.tsx:239 (`` with no key), aria-label at 233, fallback text at 245
findings.what_happens: Moving from one card to the next shows the previous card's face until the new image decodes. Reproduced: after playing Forest, hovering Finale of Devastation showed Forest. The dialog's aria-label ("Kess — card image") and the fallback line ("not in the card cache yet — no image available") contain em dashes. On /playtest the preview anchors beside the hovered card and covers the rest of the hand.
findings.why_it_hurts: A preview that briefly shows the wrong card is worse than none in a card game. The em dashes break the binding copy rule, which covers aria-label. Covering neighbouring hand cards blocks hand-scanning, which is the preview's whole reason to exist.
findings.recommendation: Add key={src} to the img (or clear the src and fade in on onLoad). Replace the em dashes: "Kess: card image", "Not in the card cache yet; no image available". On /playtest and the replay, dock the preview in a fixed slot (right edge of the board, the way Moxfield does it) instead of beside the trigger.

findings.where: /playtest, /new, /decks galleries (DeckGallery.tsx) with 43 decks
findings.what_happens: 13 of 43 tiles are variants of two commanders with identical art: Inspirit Alpha, B3, B3 v2, B3 v3, EDHREC Average, Omega, Omega V2, and Kilo Alpha, Apogee Mind, Mostly Precon, Rock Pop, Upgrade with…, Helm B3, Helm Final, Omega. The art-led gallery becomes a wall of the same spaceship. Internal benchmark decks (B3, Alpha/Omega) sit beside the player's own imports.
findings.why_it_hurts: The gallery's premise is recognition by art, and identical art defeats it (Hick's law: 43 undifferentiated choices). Mixing test fixtures with the user's decks makes the product feel like a dev sandbox.
findings.recommendation: Group variants under one commander tile with a version count ("Inspirit · 7 lists") that expands to a list. Sort by last used or last tested. Show "Your decks" first, then "Sample decks", with benchmark variants behind a "Show test lists" toggle. Put a factual line on each tile ("Tested 2 d ago · 50% vs 25% baseline"), the way EDHREC deck cards carry stats.

findings.where: public/art/backdrop-hedron-ruins.png (2,652,638 bytes, 1448x1086) loaded by layout.tsx on every route; .page uses backdrop-filter: blur(12px) over the full page height
findings.what_happens: A 2.65 MB PNG downloads on every page, phones included, to sit behind panels that are 85% opaque plus a heavy scrim. It is not WebP or AVIF and has no srcset. In this review browser, screenshots of scrolled pages rendered solid black below the first viewport. That may be a tool artefact, but it points at the cost of compositing a fixed backdrop under page-length backdrop-filter surfaces.
findings.why_it_hurts: Performance is part of perceived craft: on a mid phone over cellular this is seconds of blank sky before content. Blur behind 85% opacity is barely visible yet costs GPU on every scroll.
findings.recommendation: Re-export as AVIF/WebP at about 150-250 KB, with a 750w srcset variant for phones. Drop backdrop-filter on .page (keep it on the header and small overlays) and raise panel opacity to 0.9, which looks the same. Profile scroll on a mid-range Android.

findings.where: /decks/[file] header (Delete deck beside USE IN A RUN and Playtest); /playtest "Reset and reshuffle"
findings.what_happens: A destructive action (Delete deck) has the same weight as, and sits next to, the primary and Playtest. Reset and reshuffle wipes a goldfish session in one click, with no confirmation and no undo.
findings.why_it_hurts: Error prevention (Nielsen #5): destructive actions need distance and friction proportional to what they cost.
findings.recommendation: Move Delete into the page's Details disclosure or a "More" menu, with a confirm step that names the deck. Give Reset a confirm step, or rely on the undo stack from CC-10.

findings.where: globals.css .st i status marks (443-462), no @media (forced-colors) anywhere; html { color-scheme: dark } only
findings.what_happens: Status shapes (square = done, hollow circle = queued, filled circle = failed, diamond = warn) are drawn with background-color on an empty <i>. Windows High Contrast / forced-colors mode strips backgrounds, so the marks vanish. There is no light theme and no forced-colors handling.
findings.why_it_hurts: The design system's colour-independent status system (shape, not hue) disappears for exactly the users it exists for.
findings.recommendation: Add @media (forced-colors: active): draw the marks with borders or `forced-color-adjust: none` plus CanvasText, and give panels a 1px CanvasText border. Dark-only is defensible for this audience; do not build a light theme until the type and spacing debt (CC-06, CC-07) is paid.

strengths: The data-driven opening sentences are the most human thing in the app and must stay. For example: "Kess, Reanimator won 4 of 8 seat-rotated games (50%), 2 wins clear of Stella Lee… 1 game ended drawn… the median game ran 12 rounds." They are the answer to the AI-slop problem, not part of it. Make them more prominent, not less.

The playtest lede states the legal carve-out in plain product voice ("The app moves cards and keeps count; nothing here enforces a rule. There is no opponent and no outcome is declared."). The code has no adjudication, opponent or outcome anywhere.

The honesty discipline carries through: pooled-rate caveats on the home leaderboard, the replay's note that the board is read from the zone stream, the "not seat-comparable" exclusions. It is rare, and it builds trust with analytical players.
The ink ramp passes text contrast comfortably: --ink-4 measured 5.1:1 on the panel, --ink-3 9.0:1, violet-ink 8.4:1. The floor rule is real.
Status is carried by shape, not hue, across the app, and one-primary discipline mostly holds (the exceptions are CC-03).

The responsive work is careful: no horizontal scroll at 375px (scrollWidth 375 measured), tables re-stack at 720px, a sticky run bar on /new, a 44px nav button, and touch-size overrides under pointer:coarse. The gallery focus-ring overlay fix shows someone actually tested keyboard focus.
Scryfall hotlinking with a hover/focus/press preview and a touch magnifier. When a card is not cached, the fallback shows the name and oracle text instead of a blank back.
Tapped permanents rotate 90 degrees on the replay board and in the sandbox, a physical-table metaphor players read instantly.
The commissioned pips have distinct central silhouettes that survive greyscale. Used as identity (gallery filter, deck headers, seat plates) they are a genuine, ownable asset.
slop_signals: Home splash prompt "What would you like to do today?" (web/app/page.tsx:248): a chatbot greeting, not something a Magic tool would say.

Home composition: centred mascot, Cinzel wordmark, a 4-cell KPI strip that counts up from 0, then four equal ALL-CAPS icon-left CTAs. That is the landing-page template, and it hits design_principles.md tells #2, #3, #6, #8 and #9.

Backdrop generated from a Midjourney prompt that ships in DESIGN_SYSTEM.md §11 ("--ar 16:9 --v 6.0"). It shows floating hedrons, which are Zendikar iconography, yet the spec calls the scene Dominaria. A player notices the lore mismatch.
Glassmorphism plus cyan/violet radial "leyline" aurora glows (--atmosphere-leylines) and violet/sky gradient-filled hub buttons (.action-btn--violet, --blue).
Robot mascot (brass archivist) repeated as the nav glyph on every page: a robot literally signals "made by AI".
The Space Grotesk + JetBrains Mono pairing, which the project's own tell list names (#8). Mono takes 48% of text nodes on the results page.
Mana medallions used as decorative stat icons in the home tally (W for decks, U for games, R for runs, C for rules).
Uppercase primaries with long payloads: "NEXT TURN: UNTAP ALL, DRAW 1", "GENERATE COACHING REPORT (~$0.01, ABOUT 20 S)", "SAVE DECK TO ENGINE".
Run titles assembled from first words: "Kess, vs Power vs Talrand vs Kambal", "The vs Atraxa vs Ant-Man vs Inspirit".
Raw mana costs as bracketed mono text on the deck page ("{1}{U}{B}{R}"), which reads like a database dump.
Lowercase fragment sub-lines under headings ("one report per deck and gauntlet, cached", "most run", "follows the playhead", "goldfishing: you pilot everything…").
Operator copy in the product: "Set MTG_LLM_API_KEY in deploy/.env and redeploy", "Start it with python3 engine/mtg_engine.py serve 8484", "Engine /engine Change" in the phone nav.
Pun microcopy in zone labels: "Battlefield (tap to tap)", "Hand (tap to play)".
craft_opportunities: Render mana costs with the commissioned pips plus small numeric generic discs (our own art, never WotC symbols) on deck rows, card previews' fallback text and the replay log, instead of "{1}{U}{B}{R}".

Make commander art the identity everywhere it currently shows words. A run is a strip of its four commanders' Scryfall art crops, with the winner's crop brightest (brightness plus position, not hue). Seat plates on the replay use the scrimmed art crop as their background.

Speak table vernacular consistently. The summary says "round 10" while the games list says "T36"; pick "turn" (what players say) and show "turn 10 (the table's 36th turn)" once where it matters. Use "pod", "goldfish", "fastest win: turn 6".

Playtest: a factual opening-hand line in product voice, with no verdict and no rules ("7 cards: 3 lands, 2 ramp, average MV 2.7"). Add a mulligan counter on the hand and a "lands in play by turn" tally players actually track.

Playtest keyboard shortcuts that match Moxfield and Archidekt muscle memory (D draw, M mulligan, N next turn, S shuffle, Ctrl+Z undo) with a ? sheet. That is a small detail that tells an enfranchised player a player built it.
Tokens named from the deck itself: Skrat's Revenge offers "Squirrel 1/1" in one click from Scryfall's all_parts data, with a quantity field (make 5).
Show commander damage per opponent on replay seat plates next to life. In Commander that is the number people watch, and the log already carries combat damage by source.
Event-log card names become hover targets for the same card preview, the way Scryfall and Moxfield let you hover any card name.
Deck tiles carry one honest stat line ("last tested 2 d ago · 50% vs 25% even share"), like EDHREC's deck cards, so the gallery answers "which deck needs work" before you click.
Replace the generic home greeting with a computed sentence about the user's own decks. It is the prose-opener rule, applied to the page that currently breaks it.
